# CI and contribution automation

`workflows/ci.yml` runs npm ci, npm run check, npm test and npm run test:db on Node 24 with an isolated PostgreSQL 17 service. Keep its disposable database credentials confined to CI and preserve minimal contents:read permissions. Database tests require TEST_DATABASE_URL and create their own schema.

`ISSUE_TEMPLATE/task.yml` defines structured task intake. Align changes with the product/backlog docs without claiming those snapshots are live issue state. Workflow edits should preserve reproducible lockfile installation and separate memory/database verification; no real provider credentials or outbound messaging are required for CI.

CI also runs `python3 scripts/update-context.py --check`; changes to indexed sources/docs/guides must regenerate and commit the canonical graph/report/hash metadata. Keep this gate enabled.

nodes.label: scripts/AGENTS.md
nodes.description:
# Operator scripts

`database.ts` dispatches migrate, seed, staff and revoke actions through the repository helpers. `import-catalog.ts` reads a bounded JSON file, authenticates CATALOG_STAFF_TOKEN, then runs owner-only `catalog.replace` in a scoped transaction. Graph seeds: `seedBranch`, `issueStaffToken`, `validateCatalogImport`.

Run through root package scripts so tsx and env-file handling match the server. Validate arguments before side effects, retain authenticated scope, close pools in finally blocks and never print stored credentials. Staff issuance deliberately emits a new credential for its operator; do not copy that output into docs or commits. Use `examples/catalog.sample.json` for the reviewed/versioned import shape.

Read `docs/postgres-storage.md` and `docs/catalog-and-availability.md`. Validate with `npm run check`; database script changes need disposable-database integration coverage. Do not run seed, issue/revoke tokens or import catalogs merely to inspect behavior.

`update-context.py` is an offline context maintenance tool. Refresh with the pinned Graphify environment; `--check` needs only Python standard library and validates graph integrity plus source/artifact hashes. It must not run migrations, issue tokens or call providers.

`rehearse-demo.ts` starts and stops isolated loopback memory-mode servers through the real entrypoint. Run `node --import tsx scripts/rehearse-demo.ts` for Spanish/English local pickup and both simulated POS labels, HTTP/auth/replay/state/metrics checks. It accepts no target URL, overrides persistence/transport for its own child processes, uses ephemeral credentials without printing them, and never contacts providers or an existing database. See `docs/operations-rehearsal.md` for separate browser, PostgreSQL, packaging, privacy and staging gates.

`database.ts sandbox-mode` explicitly selects a development branch for Webpay integration/local fulfillment, disables pay at pickup for new orders and leaves confirmed snapshots unchanged. See `docs/webpay-sandbox.md`.

# Toteat and Fudo readiness

This checklist supports [#13](https://github.com/arkajyotiMukherjee/easy-eatery/issues/13), [#22](https://github.com/arkajyotiMukherjee/easy-eatery/issues/22) and [#23](https://github.com/arkajyotiMukherjee/easy-eatery/issues/23). Both connectors remain restaurant-pilot requirements. The prospect demo can use the application's local kitchen independently of either connector. A branch selects one provider; an order keeps that selection after later branch changes.

The sources below were recorded in the repository's 28 October 2026 research. A fresh read from this cloud machine on the same date returned proxy `403 Forbidden` for the Toteat and Fudo documentation hosts. The account-specific contracts and provider behavior have therefore **not been revalidated here**. No vendor account, credential, order or kitchen acceptance was obtained. Recheck the authoritative documents and the authorized restaurant account before implementing external requests.

nodes.label: docs/pos-readiness.md: Access package for the owner and restaurant partner
nodes.description:
## Access package for the owner and restaurant partner

Prepare this information without sending a vendor request or creating an account:

1. Name the consenting restaurant, operational owner, selected provider, isolated test branch and permitted test window. Confirm who may inspect the kitchen and authorize synthetic orders. Do not use customer data for this exercise.
2. Obtain current authorized technical documentation, a definite test base URL, supported API version, allowed routes, rate limits and credential scope. Store credentials through approved secret configuration, outside Git, logs, fixtures and issue comments.
3. For Toteat, confirm API enablement, restaurant/local/user identifiers, external-order/origin configuration and shift rules against its configuration guide. Confirm the usable base URL: the recorded specification contains differing descriptive and `servers` URLs.
4. For Fudo, confirm external-order approval and Delivery availability. Obtain that integration's Client ID/Client Secret and approved contract. General/Pro API keys do not establish external-order permission; confirm any separate catalog requirement before purchasing or granting extra access.
5. Request sanitized examples of success, validation/authentication rejection, rate limiting, server failure, closed shift and timeout/status lookup. Ask which identifiers are stable correlation keys and which operations can charge or resend an order.
6. Confirm payment-method mapping, tax/tip/service assumptions and the settlement recipient. An order marked paid inside a POS is not evidence that a gateway settled money. Use authorized sandbox evidence before a real-money pilot.

These are preparation questions, not instructions to contact vendors, accept terms, purchase a plan or provision a merchant account. Those actions retain the documented owner and provider gates.

nodes.label: docs/operations-rehearsal.md: Automated local acceptance
nodes.description:
## Automated local acceptance

From the repository root with Node 24+ and `npm ci` completed:

```sh
npm run check
npm test
node --import tsx scripts/rehearse-demo.ts
python3 scripts/update-context.py --check
```

The rehearsal starts three fresh, loopback-only server processes using the real entrypoint: local pay at pickup, simulated Toteat and simulated Fudo. Each process uses its own random in-memory panel credential and available local port. No credential or customer identifier is printed. Existing `.env` files and existing servers are preserved; explicit child environment settings select memory persistence and console transport even when a developer has configured PostgreSQL or Cloud transport elsewhere. The script accepts no target URL or arguments, so it cannot mutate an existing deployment.

Each mode exercises Spanish and English ordering through actual HTTP requests, duplicate message/confirmation handling, the CLP 11,500 total, required payment/fulfillment gates, duplicate staff actions, collection metrics, missing-auth rejection, and delivery of the known browser assets. The script closes the processes it starts, including after a failed assertion, and returns a nonzero exit status on failure. Its data disappears when each process stops. No database migration, staff issuance or provider API call occurs.

Passing this script establishes HTTP demo behavior only. Run `npm run test:db` separately with an explicit disposable `TEST_DATABASE_URL` for PostgreSQL isolation, rollback, replay and process-restart recovery. Never use a production database URL. Automated checks do not prove keyboard accessibility, mobile layout, a real WhatsApp recipient loop, payment-provider authorization, POS kitchen acceptance or cloud backup recovery.

nodes.label: docs/operations-rehearsal.md: Browser and restaurant feedback rehearsal
nodes.description:
## Browser and restaurant feedback rehearsal

Use the README to start a separate supervised demo with synthetic data. For each language, use a narrow mobile viewport and then a desktop viewport; record the browser and viewport with the result. Complete these actions using only the keyboard as well as the pointer:

1. Open the panel, select the language, enter the panel key, and verify visible focus and readable error messages after an invalid key.
2. Add items, change language while a cart exists, edit the cart, and confirm the authoritative total. Check that accessible names and labels change with the selected language.
3. Complete the appropriate simulation or local pay-at-pickup flow. In local mode, confirm that preparation and readiness remain unpaid until staff records payment at the store. Attempt collection before payment and verify the refusal.
4. Mark an item unavailable or close pickup. Confirm that a new order is blocked and that existing confirmed orders keep their original method and price.
5. Verify empty, loading, unavailable and error states without exposing credentials or real contacts in a screenshot. Reload and confirm the panel key is not retained. In memory mode expect order data to disappear after server restart.

Capture results using this template in an approved private evidence location; keep only a redacted summary in issues:

| Field | Record |
| --- | --- |
| Build and workflow | Commit SHA; local memory / disposable PostgreSQL / authorized sandbox |
| Reviewer and session | Assigned operator role, date, browser, viewport, ES/EN |
| Menu and service | Synthetic catalog version; service hours and expected pickup promise |
| Cases | Pass/fail/unrun for each step above; observed behavior and reproduction |
| Restaurant feedback | Menu/modifier clarity, missed or duplicate tickets, staff effort and objections |
| Timing | Confirm-to-accept and ready-to-collection; synthetic measurements only |
| Follow-up | Issue, owner, next action and acceptance evidence still needed |

Do not invent restaurant validation or record an unchecked case as passed. Ask the restaurant partner to sign off actual menu, kitchen ownership, service hours and support responsibility before a real pilot.

nodes.label: docs/graphify.md: Cloud bootstrap
nodes.description:
## Cloud bootstrap

Graphify's package is **graphifyy** (double y). Python 3.10+ and uv are required for regeneration. Install the pinned 0.9.97 CLI with MCP and SQL extras from the package registry:

```sh
uv venv .graphify-venv
uv pip install --python .graphify-venv/bin/python 'graphifyy[mcp,sql]==0.9.97'
.graphify-venv/bin/graphify query 'WhatsAppQueue delivery retries' --budget 1500
.graphify-venv/bin/graphify query 'Meta verification blocker' --budget 1500
.graphify-venv/bin/graphify explain 'PostgresRepository'
.graphify-venv/bin/graphify path 'Conversation' 'OrderingService'
```

Run from the repository root, or pass `--graph /absolute/checkout/graphify-out/graph.json`. The committed graph is already usable; do not rebuild just to ask a question. Read Git status/history and root AGENTS.md, query narrowly, read the nearest scoped guide, then inspect targeted code. If a query reports truncation, narrow it or increase the modest token budget rather than dumping the full report.

A plain clone can validate freshness without installing Graphify:

```sh
python3 scripts/update-context.py --check
```

If installation is unavailable, use the committed handoff/scoped guides and source references as a focused fallback; record that limitation. Do not skip checking actual code because an inferred edge is absent.

nodes.label: docs/cloud-agent-handoff.md: Cloud delivery evidence: 28 October 2026
nodes.description:
## Cloud delivery evidence: 28 October 2026

The cloud checkout began at current `main` commit `0b4070001a734fc6cc66ba630ea78c1ce4a166ab`. This delivery adds migration 005 and authenticated redacted WhatsApp recovery: known failed jobs can be retried; uncertain sends require explicit review without resend and never become delivery receipts. See `docs/whatsapp-recovery.md`. The original PostgreSQL suite passed 13 TAP results and the recovery suite passed six results. The database script selects all `*.integration.ts` files so new coverage runs in CI.

A disconnected Webpay sandbox adapter follows the official Transbank Node SDK contract at `52ad60075ce7d9eacf7f8cc42a795ae43bd483ff`. Five local mock HTTP tests pass for create/commit/status, mismatches, declines, ambiguous errors and hostile inputs. This is boundary coverage only: no actual sandbox checkout, application checkout flow or settlement is proved by this slice.

`scripts/rehearse-demo.ts` exercises real local HTTP processes in Spanish and English for local pay at pickup and both simulated POS labels. See `docs/operations-rehearsal.md` for execution, feedback, staging/rollback and privacy gates. Baseline type checks, 16 application tests, committed context hash checks and an independent HTTP CLP 11,500 ordering/collection rehearsal passed before implementation.

Git HTTPS reads work. The public GitHub issue listing was read on 28 October and showed the outstanding pilot issues open; REST and GraphQL calls to `api.github.com` were denied by the runtime proxy. The required domain was saved in the environment draft, but draft saving does not apply runtime policy. Live issue comments/criteria updates remain blocked; `docs/issue-evidence.md` contains pending truthful updates. No issue is claimed updated or closed. Installation/start instructions were saved for review; publication and fresh-task restoration are not verified.

nodes.label: docs/operations-rehearsal.md: Incidents, rollback and privacy
nodes.description:
## Incidents, rollback and privacy

Stop a supervised demo or pause new orders when payment state, kitchen acceptance or delivery outcome is uncertain. The operator owns customer follow-up; engineering owns diagnosis. Inspect scoped dashboard counts and redacted correlation/order references. Do not dump queue payloads, messages, phone numbers, access tokens, checkout URLs or raw provider responses into logs, screenshots, Git or issues.

For ambiguous outbound sends, preserve the recorded attempt and reconcile the provider outcome before retrying. A provider HTTP acceptance is not device delivery. Do not delete a parked job, edit order/payment rows or replay an unknown POS submission to clear a dashboard warning. An operator must not infer payment from a browser redirect or mark a real payment settled using a demo endpoint. Escalate unsupported reconciliation/refund operations instead of fabricating success.

For an application rollback, first pause incoming work through the hosting system's approved controls, retain the database and audit history, and route traffic to the last compatible image/revision. Check migration compatibility before switching. Numbered migrations are not an automatic down-migration plan; do not drop tables or reset data to make an older revision start. If compatibility is unknown, keep the service paused and use a reviewed forward repair or an isolated restore rehearsal. After recovery, recheck health, staff scope, queue state and synthetic ordering, then have the assigned operator authorize resumption.

The application stores conversation and order state; existing memory maps and durable inbox/outbox data do not establish a production retention policy. Agree access, retention periods, deletion/export handling and incident contacts with the restaurant before collecting customer data. Keep demo evidence synthetic. Backups and restores must be tested using isolated data before claiming recovery readiness, and any real data restore must preserve access controls and reconciliation obligations.

nodes.label: docs/graphify.md: Optional MCP registration
nodes.description:
## Optional MCP registration

This desktop previously registered an enabled stdio server named `graphify-easy-eatery`; a cloud checkout does not inherit it. Querying through CLI needs no registration. If the cloud client supports MCP, register using that checkout's absolute paths:

```sh
codex mcp add graphify-easy-eatery -- /absolute/checkout/.graphify-venv/bin/graphify-mcp --graph /absolute/checkout/graphify-out/graph.json
codex mcp get graphify-easy-eatery
```

Tools include query_graph, get_node, get_neighbors and shortest_path. Reconnect if the client caches a stale graph. MCP discovery/state is not a substitute for Git/source hash verification. The upstream `.codex/skills/graphify` installation is optional local tooling, not the authoritative project handoff; root/scoped guides and the committed context files are authoritative repository context.

Official upstream: [Graphify](https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify). Revalidate installation/support details when changing the pinned tooling.

nodes.label: docs/operations-rehearsal.md: Packaging and authorized staging
nodes.description:
## Packaging and authorized staging

The checked-in Dockerfile runs Node 24 as the `node` user, starts the same TypeScript server, and defaults to port 8080. Building an image is a local packaging check:

```sh
docker build -t easy-eatery:rehearsal .
```

In a managed environment whose approved HTTPS proxy uses an additional CA, forward existing proxy bindings and mount the existing CA only for installation:

```sh
docker build --build-arg HTTP_PROXY --build-arg HTTPS_PROXY --build-arg NO_PROXY \
  --secret id=build_ca,src="$NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS" -t easy-eatery:rehearsal .
```

The optional BuildKit secret is available only during `npm ci`; its contents and the proxy bindings must not be copied into the image or repository. Normal environments omit this secret and use their normal verified trust store. Keep TLS and npm artifact integrity checks enabled. If Docker's client cache directory is read-only, use writable task-local `DOCKER_CONFIG` and `BUILDX_CONFIG` directories instead of changing trust or credentials. The image runtime does not require these build-only settings.

The image needs development dependencies because `tsx` is the runtime loader. Do not prune them without changing and validating the packaging design. `.dockerignore` excludes `.env`, local dependencies, Git metadata and the context graph; never add a credential file to the build context or image. Before accepting the packaged build, run it with a fresh random `ADMIN_TOKEN` injected through the runtime environment, bind its published port to loopback, and verify `/health`, unauthenticated API rejection and a synthetic ordering journey. Stop the test container afterward. A successful build alone does not establish runtime readiness.

Staging remains gated on an approved account, budget and hosting plan. The documented target is Cloud Run and Cloud SQL in Santiago; check service availability and cost before provisioning. Hostinger is not an approved alternative merely because a connector is available. No paid resource creation or provider setup is part of this runbook.

Before an authorized staging launch, assign an operator and record the image digest, revision, nonsecret configuration, schema version and rollback revision. Use a separate database, least-privilege identity and secure runtime secret bindings. In PostgreSQL mode, apply reviewed migrations explicitly before starting the server; startup does not migrate or seed. Keep staff credentials scoped and expiring. Do not expose the in-memory demo as a customer service. Live pilot deployment also needs simulation mutation controls, retention/deletion policy, tested database backup restoration, provider reconciliation and operational ownership; these are separate acceptance gates.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md: Required context lifecycle
nodes.description:
## Required context lifecycle

This repository's portable context is versioned in Git. At the start of work: inspect Git status/history and live issues/PRs; read this guide; query `graphify-out/graph.json`; read the relevant scoped AGENTS.md and ancestors; then inspect targeted source/tests. Read `docs/cloud-agent-handoff.md` for product decisions, verified state, blockers and cloud orchestration instructions. `docs/context-decisions.json` is the curated decision/blocker index, not an external acceptance ledger.

Before completing an implementation slice or handoff:

1. Update the relevant scoped guide when responsibilities/invariants change. Update the handoff/decision index for changed product decisions, external evidence, blockers or next actions. Keep GitHub issue criteria and backlog files honest and aligned.
2. Run `python3 scripts/update-context.py`. It refreshes the code/SQL graph, overlays explicit Markdown/decision context, rebuilds the report and records portable source/artifact hashes without an LLM call. Do not use a plain AST rebuild as the final step: it omits the curated overlay.
3. Run `python3 scripts/update-context.py --check` and the normal code checks appropriate to the change. Commit source, guides/decisions, `graphify-out/graph.json`, `GRAPH_REPORT.md` and `context-meta.json` together. CI rejects stale context. Refresh again after conflict resolution or later source/doc edits. A large generated graph diff is expected; do not remove the freshness check to avoid updating it.
4. Exclude tokens, cookies, private account details, customer messages, runtime data, virtual environments and graph caches. Never treat a node marked EXTRACTED/INFERRED as provider acceptance. Read its source and current tests.

Cloud agents can query the committed graph immediately after installing the pinned CLI; desktop MCP/OAuth registration is not portable. If tooling is unavailable, use the committed handoff/scoped guides for focused reads, record the limitation, and restore/rebuild context before declaring the slice complete. See `docs/graphify.md`.

nodes.label: docs/graphify.md: Required maintenance
nodes.description:
## Required maintenance

After changing indexed source, docs, guides or configuration:

1. Update the relevant AGENTS.md for moved responsibilities/new invariants. Record new decisions, blockers and acceptance evidence in the handoff and curated decision index. Keep GitHub/backlog status aligned; never record a credential or customer message.
2. Run `python3 scripts/update-context.py`. It rebuilds the code/SQL layer, replaces the explicit context overlay, clusters without LLM labeling, writes graph/report, then records source and artifact hashes. It makes no model API call and needs no model key. Additions, removals and deleted symbols are rebuilt from current files.
3. Run `python3 scripts/update-context.py --check`, review the generated diff, and stage canonical graph/report/hash metadata with the source/context edits. CI runs the same standard-library check and fails when a source changed without a refresh or a canonical artifact changed without updated metadata. Commit only reviewed changes.
4. After conflict resolution, repeat the refresh against the final merged source. Do not resolve a graph conflict by blindly retaining one agent's old output. A source hash is the freshness check; recorded Git revisions are provenance, not a circular requirement to regenerate after the commit itself.

The hash check validates indexed file contents and graph structural integrity; it cannot prove that prose is truthful, tests are adequate or external approvals exist. Human/agent review remains required. Do not weaken the check or exclude a touched file simply to get CI green. If upgrading Graphify, change the pin/metadata and validate the new graph behavior as a separate reviewable change.

nodes.label: AGENTS.md: Retrieve context
nodes.description:
## Retrieve context

Graphify is installed at `.graphify-venv/bin/graphify` (0.9.97, MCP + SQL extras). Run commands from the repository root, or use absolute graph paths from a subdirectory. Prefer a focused graph query, then verify the relevant source: AST edges show structure, not proof of runtime behavior. The graph indexes code/SQL and an explicit Markdown/decision overlay; CSS is not semantically indexed. The overlay copies source text and links, rather than inferring runtime truth. Consult the scoped guides for those.

```sh
.graphify-venv/bin/graphify query "OrderingService confirm" --budget 1500
.graphify-venv/bin/graphify explain "PostgresRepository"
.graphify-venv/bin/graphify path "Conversation" "OrderingService"
```

If the graph is absent, rebuild with `.graphify-venv/bin/graphify extract . --code-only --no-cluster --max-workers 2`. After source or context changes, run `python3 scripts/update-context.py` to preserve both code and decision layers. Do not block source verification on unavailable or incomplete graph results. The environment/caches are ignored by Git; canonical graph/report/hash metadata are committed. All graph output is excluded from Docker images.

nodes.label: docs/pos-readiness.md: Shared acceptance rehearsal, once access exists
nodes.description:
## Shared acceptance rehearsal, once access exists

Run these cases separately for each authorized connector, retaining the exact contract/version and a redacted evidence record:

| Case | Required observation |
| --- | --- |
| Correct immutable order | Server-authoritative integer CLP total, approved products/modifiers, original confirmed price and selected branch/provider reach the intended test kitchen. |
| Provider switch | Changing branch defaults after confirmation never redirects the existing order. No fallback sends it to another provider or restaurant. |
| Replay and concurrent workers | The authorized duplicate/correlation mechanism proves one kitchen ticket for one payment/order intent across retries and process restart. A local Map is insufficient. |
| Rejection and unavailable service | Unknown mapping, closed shift, explicit rejection and rate limiting leave truthful payment/kitchen states and bounded recovery. No failure is labeled accepted. |
| Ambiguous outcome | Timeout or connection loss after submission pauses uncertain work, queries the documented correlation/status operation and never blindly resubmits. |
| Status and scope | Authenticated events/status queries cannot cross tenant/branch/provider scope; replay and late/out-of-order events cannot regress authoritative state. |
| Payment and pickup | Only the approved payment evidence permits paid submission; acceptance, readiness and collection remain distinct from financial settlement. Refund/cancellation exceptions have an identified operator and approved procedure. |

Record provider, test environment, contract version, application commit, synthetic case, expected/observed result, redacted reference, staff witness role and unresolved limitation. Keep account identifiers, credentials and customer contacts in the authorized private evidence system. An issue comment should link a safe evidence summary, never raw requests with credential-bearing URLs.

Keep business rules in platform services and external payloads behind integrations. Tenant and branch come from authenticated staff or mapped WhatsApp accounts. 1. Read root `AGENTS.md`; inspect `git status`, recent commits, branch/base and live PR/issue state. Preserve unrelated changes. Start from current `origin/main`, not the old development branch named in a chat.

nodes.label: docs/graphify.md: What Git preserves
nodes.description:
## What Git preserves

The repository commits root/scoped `AGENTS.md`, `docs/cloud-agent-handoff.md`, `docs/context-decisions.json`, the canonical `graphify-out/graph.json`, its `GRAPH_REPORT.md`, and `context-meta.json` source/artifact hashes. Together they preserve explicit product decisions, implementation navigation, blockers, evidence and work rules. They do not preserve the entire chat, browser sessions, customer records, credentials or the desktop agent's OAuth/MCP configuration.

The code/SQL layer uses Graphify AST extraction. A deterministic, project-owned overlay copies Markdown sections and curated decisions with source paths/line references and links them to named code paths/symbols. This is explicit source-backed context, not an LLM inference that a feature or provider has passed acceptance. Query results locate relevant evidence; verify the source and current tests. CSS is included in freshness hashes but has no semantic graph extraction. Some test callbacks do not produce individual AST symbols.

`graphify-out/cache`, generated HTML, manifests, temporary sidecars and `.graphify-venv` stay local/ignored. Docker excludes all graph output. Canonical files intentionally may have large diffs when code or communities change.

# Database schema history

Ordered SQL migrations are loaded by `migrate` in `apps/server/src/persistence/database.ts`, using an advisory transaction lock and SHA-256 checksums. `001_restaurant_storage.sql` introduces scoped storage/access, `002_catalog_availability.sql` extends catalog/quotes, and `003_pickup_payment.sql` adds pickup payment state. `004_whatsapp_jobs.sql` adds durable message processing; `005_whatsapp_recovery.sql` adds the explicit staff-reviewed `resolved` terminal state without calling it sent or delivered.

Add the next numbered migration for schema changes; never rewrite applied history. Preserve tenant/branch composite keys, foreign-key isolation, nonnegative integer monetary constraints and immutable snapshots. Update repository load/save and domain types alongside schema changes. Migration execution is explicit (`npm run db:migrate`), never implicit server-startup DDL.

Use `docs/postgres-storage.md` and `tests/postgres.integration.ts`. Verify repeatable migrations, rollback and cross-scope rejection with `npm run test:db` on a disposable database. Do not migrate a live database for context discovery.

Migration 006 adds explicit sandbox branch selection, immutable attempts and test financial states; 007 stores signed delivery evidence independently; 008 adds verified provider timestamps, order contacts, staff handoffs and notification claims. Apply all pending migrations explicitly; old timestamp-less replies are parked for staff review.

nodes.label: src/AGENTS.md
nodes.description:
# HTTP boundary and runtime composition

Start at `createApp` in `app.ts`; it constructs ordering and conversation services, wraps scoped PostgreSQL units of work, authenticates API requests, validates payloads, maps localized errors, serves allowed static files and verifies webhook ingress. `index.ts` selects memory/PostgreSQL mode and console/Cloud WhatsApp transport, checks startup configuration and closes resources.

Query `createApp` or `Config` in Graphify before following dependencies. Shared decisions live in `platform/`; external I/O in `integrations/`; durable state and roles in `persistence/`; WhatsApp commands in `modules/whatsapp/`. Each has a scoped guide.

Preserve bearer authentication for `/api/`, schema rejection of extra input, raw JSON bytes for webhook HMAC, mapped receiving account scope, CSP and no-store responses. Demo routes are under `/api/demo`; pickup actions under `/api/pickup`. Do not trust body-supplied tenant/branch or browser totals. Network sends happen outside database transactions; PostgreSQL Cloud webhooks commit jobs before acknowledgment; memory mode is synchronous and test-only. Unknown outbound outcomes are parked for review. A process queue is not distributed exactly-once delivery.

For routes/auth/signatures run `npm run check`, `tests/poc.test.ts` through `npm test`, and database integration checks when storage scope changes. For local pickup also inspect `tests/pickup.test.ts`.

Durable exception recovery routes live under `/api/whatsapp/delivery/jobs`; `persistence/whatsapp-recovery.ts` owns scoped listing and guarded transitions. Route schemas require explicit expected state and review-without-resend confirmation. See `docs/whatsapp-recovery.md`; do not turn uncertain sends into automatic retry or claim delivery from staff review.

nodes.label: persistence/AGENTS.md
nodes.description:
# PostgreSQL repository and access

`database.ts` owns Pool creation, checksum-tracked migrations, staff-token hashing/issuance, channel identity, role authorization and `PostgresRepository.transaction`. Query `PostgresRepository`, `authenticate`, `channelIdentity`, `migrate` and `seedBranch`.

Transactions lock the branch row, recheck access, load a transaction-local MemoryStore, invoke services, persist mutations and audit, then commit or roll back and release the client. Maps here are working sets; PostgreSQL is durable truth. Scope every read/write and constraint by tenant and branch. Viewer is read-only; catalog replacement requires owner. Recheck token revocation, expiry, active membership and role inside the unit of work.

Preserve immutable confirmed lines, price/provider/payment-method snapshots, integer totals, scoped inbox/delivery deduplication and outbox keys. External sends stay outside transactions; persisted receipts cannot resolve a crash after send but before commit. Schema changes require a new migration in `migrations/` plus load/save alignment. Never edit an applied migration: checksums reject drift.

Read `docs/postgres-storage.md`; run `npm run check`, `npm test` and `npm run test:db` against a disposable explicit TEST_DATABASE_URL for repository/schema changes.

`whatsapp-queue.ts` owns persisted inbound jobs, atomic domain/reply processing, claimed external sends, bounded retries and uncertain-outcome parking. Branch locks coordinate workers; provider acceptance is not device delivery. Query `WhatsAppQueue` before changing delivery behavior. Update the handoff and canonical context after changes.

`whatsapp-recovery.ts` exposes a redacted exception list and staff-only recovery through the same branch transaction and current-token authorization. Retry is limited to `failed` jobs; ambiguous `needs_attention` jobs can only be explicitly resolved without resending. The terminal `resolved` state unblocks later conversation messages but does not create a delivery receipt or imply success. Recovery requires the listed version and increments it atomically, so an old retry cannot reopen a later failure after the worker returns to the same state. Recovery audit actions include the job ID; do not add freeform customer text.

`whatsapp-status.ts` stores verified provider status events separately from queue state. Correlate only scoped phone/provider message IDs. Preserve read/delivered evidence under out-of-order callbacks; retain failures as separate evidence. Status events never authorize a resend, payment or kitchen action. Read `docs/whatsapp-delivery-status.md`.

`sandbox-payments.ts` owns durable sandbox claims and authoritative observations outside staff transactions; full reversals require a current owner and revision. `whatsapp-status.ts` records signed evidence separately from queue state. `whatsapp-support.ts` stages verified-state notifications, preserves provider windows and records redacted human review. Never retry ambiguous sends/reversals or infer success from browser returns.

nodes.label: docs/completed-issues.md: Issue #12 completion evidence
nodes.description:
## Issue #12 completion evidence

- Unknown requests, allergies, payment problems and rejected-order requests route to durable scoped staff review with bilingual replies, preserved carts, replay deduplication and no allergen-safety/contact promise. A targeted signed rejected-order request was checked through the webhook, worker and staff API using a fake transport.
- Accepted/ready/store-payment-recorded notifications derive from persisted local domain state, deduplicate by order/kind, and recheck current state before sending. Store payment is labeled as an audited staff assertion; sandbox notifications are labeled as tests. Neither implies provider settlement.
- Verified provider timestamps enforce the customer-service window for replies and notifications. Missing/future/expired windows fail closed and route to staff. An approved-template fallback is not required because the issue explicitly permits staff fallback instead.
- PostgreSQL integration checks cover explicit rejection retry bounds, ambiguous-send parking, late/superseded readiness, privacy, tenant/role isolation and no marketing or sensitive payment data. Browser checks cover the ES/EN staff controls.

`apps/server/src/persistence/whatsapp-support.ts`, `whatsapp-queue.ts`, migrations 005–008 and `tests/whatsapp-support.integration.ts` contain the implementation/evidence. Real-phone acceptance remains open in #9/#27; closing this software issue does not claim a real message or provider acceptance.

From the Mac's authenticated GitHub CLI:

```sh
gh issue close 12 --repo arkajyotiMukherjee/easy-eatery --reason completed \
  --comment "Implementation merged into main: durable bilingual staff handoff, verified-state pickup notifications, customer-service-window enforcement with staff fallback, and failure/privacy tests. Fresh checks passed: 28 application tests and 43 PostgreSQL TAP results. See docs/completed-issues.md for all four criteria. Real-phone acceptance remains tracked in #9 and #27; no live provider acceptance is claimed."
```

No other currently open issue is fully complete. In particular, keep #7/#8/#10/#11/#14/#15/#17/#18/#19/#20/#21/#27 and the provider-access/integration issues open for their remaining criteria. No milestone qualifies for closure. This cloud task did not close an issue or milestone.

These tests establish local behavior. They do not prove an approved sender/recipient, provider subscription, real-device status delivery or a real-phone ordering loop. Those gates remain in the cloud handoff. No provider account or real message was used for this validation.

nodes.description:
# Provider contracts and WhatsApp I/O

`contracts.ts` defines `PaymentProvider`, `PosProvider`, `WhatsAppTransport` and labeled demo payment/POS implementations. `whatsapp.ts` owns `CloudWhatsAppTransport`, raw-body `validSignature` HMAC checks and account-filtered `parseMessages` normalization. Query those symbols for callers.

Keep external request/response shapes out of shared domain rules. Cloud WhatsApp transport is real outbound I/O; payment/POS contracts currently use simulated implementations. Toteat and Fudo access and kitchen workflow gates are documented in `docs/integrations.md`; one branch uses one selected provider per order. A local fake reference or idempotency Map does not establish real financial settlement or provider exactly-once behavior.

Preserve constant-time signature verification, receiving phone-ID filtering, bounded message parsing and non-leaking error handling. Never log tokens, credential URLs, raw customer messages or checkout links. Use fake transports in tests; do not send actual messages for validation. Run `npm run check` and `npm test`; routing and restart changes also need database tests.

`webpay.ts` implements sandbox-only create/commit/status/full-reversal transport against the official Transbank Node SDK contract at `52ad60075ce7d9eacf7f8cc42a795ae43bd483ff`. `persistence/sandbox-payments.ts` owns durable authority and `sandbox-routes.ts` owns the guest POST handoff. Fixed integration origin, immutable merchant/CLP/order/session verification and no automatic unknown-outcome retry are mandatory. Sandbox authorization is not settlement/revenue; real hosted acceptance is unverified. See `docs/webpay-sandbox.md`.

`whatsapp.ts` normalizes bounded inbound timestamps and signed status events, never raw provider errors. `customerWindowOpen` reserves the transport timeout within the verified 24-hour window; missing/future/stale timestamps cannot open it. Status evidence never authorizes queue retries, payment or kitchen transitions.

nodes.description:
# Shared domain, catalog, ordering and locale

`domain.ts` defines tenant/session/cart/quote/order types, `MemoryStore`, pricing, snapshot construction and `DomainError`. `catalog.ts` owns strict import validation, modifiers and provider mappings, versioned changes and service hours. `ordering.ts` owns confirmation, simulated checkout/POS, local pickup acceptance, store payment recording, allowed transitions and dashboard metrics. `i18n.ts` owns server error codes and Spanish/English messages.

Graph seeds: `MemoryStore`, `CatalogService`, `OrderingService`, `validateCatalogImport`, `withinHours`. Follow callers to conversation, HTTP, persistence and catalog tests before changing a public contract.

Validate availability, modifiers, provider mappings and integer CLP pricing server-side. `confirm` must reject expired/version-changed/cart-changed quotes and direct line changes; retain immutable order snapshots. Keep payment method/state separate from fulfillment and operational status. Local pickup cannot be collected before staff records store payment; simulated payment must not process a pickup payment. Select one POS provider per branch/order. Shared services must remain reusable by future channels without depending on WhatsApp.

Run `npm test` (catalog, POC and pickup cases). Type/serialization changes also require persistence SQL, migrations and database integration review. Keep error keys and both languages aligned.

Sandbox orders snapshot `webpay_sandbox` and local fulfillment. Only authoritative sandbox service observations can authorize a test ticket; readiness/collection require `sandbox_authorized`. `sandbox_review` and `sandbox_reversed` block further fulfillment. nodes.description:
# Shared domain, catalog, ordering and locale

`domain.ts` defines tenant/session/cart/quote/order types, `MemoryStore`, pricing, snapshot construction and `DomainError`. `catalog.ts` owns strict import validation, modifiers and provider mappings, versioned changes and service hours. `ordering.ts` owns confirmation, simulated checkout/POS, local pickup acceptance, store payment recording, allowed transitions and dashboard metrics. `i18n.ts` owns server error codes and Spanish/English messages.

Graph seeds: `MemoryStore`, `CatalogService`, `OrderingService`, `validateCatalogImport`, `withinHours`. Follow callers to conversation, HTTP, persistence and catalog tests before changing a public contract.

Validate availability, modifiers, provider mappings and integer CLP pricing server-side. `confirm` must reject expired/version-changed/cart-changed quotes and direct line changes; retain immutable order snapshots. Keep payment method/state separate from fulfillment and operational status. Local pickup cannot be collected before staff records store payment; simulated payment must not process a pickup payment. Select one POS provider per branch/order. Shared services must remain reusable by future channels without depending on WhatsApp.

Run `npm test` (catalog, POC and pickup cases). Type/serialization changes also require persistence SQL, migrations and database integration review. Keep error keys and both languages aligned.

Sandbox orders snapshot `webpay_sandbox` and local fulfillment. Only authoritative sandbox service observations can authorize a test ticket; readiness/collection require `sandbox_authorized`. `sandbox_review` and `sandbox_reversed` block further fulfillment. Keep test-authorized totals separate from paid revenue and never permit simulation or cash recording for sandbox snapshots.

nodes.label: whatsapp/AGENTS.md
nodes.description:
# WhatsApp conversation

`conversation.ts` is the deterministic bilingual command handler. `Conversation.receive` serializes each customer's work; `process` normalizes commands, checks module entitlement and caches replies by tenant/customer/message; `handle` translates commands into shared cart/ordering operations; `cartSummary` refreshes the displayed quote.

Graph seeds: `Conversation`, `OrderingService`, `cartSelection`. Transport/signature parsing is in `../../integrations/whatsapp.ts`; durable jobs/delivery claims are in `../../persistence/whatsapp-queue.ts` and ingress is in `../../app.ts`; domain decisions belong in `../../platform/`.

Preserve Spanish default and explicit English/Spanish switching, stable product/modifier IDs, quantity bounds, candidate-cart validation before mutation, quote review on changed confirmation and cached duplicate replies. Confirmed orders cannot silently mutate their carts. Preserve truthful copy for simulation versus pay-at-pickup. In-memory queues do not provide distributed serialization; database branch locks provide scoped unit-of-work serialization.

Run `npm test`, especially POC language/replay, catalog quote/modifier and pickup flows. Run database integration tests for persisted replay or session changes.

nodes.label: docs/pos-readiness.md: Capability and evidence matrix
nodes.description:
## Capability and evidence matrix

| Question | Toteat | Fudo | Evidence needed before acceptance |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Who grants access? | Recorded configuration guide describes owner-enabled API access and account-specific restaurant/local/user identifiers. | Recorded external-order guide requires approval and a Delivery-enabled account; general API access is separate. | Owner authorization, permitted test account/branch, current integration contract and supported environment. |
| Catalog and modifiers | Public specification lists product access; actual IDs and modifier mappings remain account-specific. | General API documents business/product data; whether it supplies this integration's catalog needs confirmation. | Sanitized catalog fixture, approved bilingual menu/prices, modifier and tax/payment mappings for this branch. |
| Create a pickup order | Recorded order contract describes an external-order endpoint and open-shift precondition. | Requires the approved external-order contract; no request schema is inferred from generic sales APIs. | Authorized request/response fixtures, supported pickup semantics, required fields and accepted reference. |
| Which kitchen receives it? | Printer/KDS routing and the account's shift configuration are unverified. | Recorded guide says external orders use Delivery rather than Mesas y Mostrador; actual restaurant routing is unverified. | Staff observes one test order in the intended branch/workflow and confirms preparation/readiness. |
| Can an uncertain request be retried? | Idempotency/correlation lookup guarantees remain unverified. | Idempotency/correlation lookup guarantees remain unverified. | Official duplicate semantics, correlation/status query, timeout procedure and a repeatable uncertain-outcome rehearsal. |
| Status callbacks and recovery | Public index lists status/events; authentication, ordering and account behavior need verification. | Authorized event/status contract is required. | Sanitized signed/authenticated fixtures, replay/out-of-order behavior, readiness mapping and recovery ownership. |
| Does the POS create hosted checkout? | Not established by recorded order payment fields. | Not established by recorded help documentation. | Explicit supported checkout contract or owner-approved independent gateway, authoritative reconciliation and merchant settlement recipient. |
| Is local adapter evidence sufficient? | No: current `DemoPosProvider` creates synthetic references. | No: the same demo class uses a different label. | Separate provider contract tests and real authorized kitchen evidence for each connector. |

The current shared `PosProvider` port exposes only `submitPaidPickup(order) -> {reference}`. It does not define vendor authentication, HTTP payloads, acceptance callbacks, refund behavior or uncertain-outcome classification. Do not invent those details to fill a mock. The demo adapter's process-local Map and deterministic reference demonstrate local replay behavior; neither establishes distributed vendor idempotency or durable kitchen acceptance.

nodes.label: docs/cloud-agent-handoff.md: Orchestrate independent work in parallel
nodes.description:
## Orchestrate independent work in parallel

Use up to 3–4 implementation agents when available, plus the orchestrator/reviewer if the host supports it. Scale down to actual capacity. Give each agent a bounded outcome, owned paths, source/issue references, invariants and verification commands. Ask for a commit/diff, tests and unresolved assumptions. Agents may report progress to the orchestrator through supported collaboration tools; this does not authorize contacting third parties.

| Workstream | Scope and issues | Completion evidence now | External acceptance later |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Messaging reliability / staff handoff | #10–#12: delivery callbacks, unknown-media/status batches, retention policy, dead-letter/recovery UX, permitted ready notifications, human help | Signed callback fixtures, state-ordering/replay/failure tests, auth/isolation, ES/EN staff flows; no blind resend of unknown outcomes | Approved recipient and actual phone journey; approved utility template outside service window |
| Checkout / financial orchestration | #8/#14/#15/#17 and local slice #27: durable attempts, separate financial/fulfillment states, Webpay sandbox adapter, cancellation/late payment/reconciliation | Mock gateway tests, immutable total checks, duplicate callbacks, concurrent workers, unknown outcomes, safe cash-vs-online choices, clear sandbox UI | Reachable hosted sandbox; merchant settlement/refund contract for real money |
| POS contract readiness | #2/#3/#7/#13/#16/#22/#23: Toteat/Fudo capability matrix, adapters where contract is known, synthetic harness and fail-closed configuration | Two isolated provider configurations, routing/mapping/error tests, exact evidence labels and access checklist | Approved accounts/contracts and real kitchen confirmation in each provider |
| Demo / deployment / operations | #18–#21/#27: bilingual dashboard/recovery, staging recipe, local acceptance scripts, privacy/runbooks and customer feedback kit | Reproducible build, isolated PG tests, keyboard/mobile ES/EN rehearsal, deployment/rollback checks without paid provisioning | Restaurant ownership/sign-off, cloud/budget authorization, real traffic go/no-go |

Allocate migrations and shared contracts to one owner at a time. Reserve migration numbers centrally. Sequence changes to `domain.ts`, `database.ts`, `app.ts` and `contracts.ts`; independent agents should not concurrently rewrite them. Use an integration branch with exclusive file ownership in this isolated cloud checkout, or sequential cherry-picks; never use shared uncoordinated edits. Do not create worktrees during cloud setup unless explicitly requested. Re-run the relevant integration suite after combining changes. A reviewer should examine payment authority, tenant isolation, message/order duplication, unknown outcomes and truthful statuses.

Recommended order: finish messaging recovery/status handling and financial state contracts; implement independent sandbox checkout; add ready notifications and staff exception flows; prepare staging and scripted bilingual rehearsal; continue POS readiness concurrently without claiming vendor acceptance. M0–M4 are outcome groups, not a requirement to finish all vendor approvals before writing independent code. #27 is the first standalone demo target; #21/#23 contain later restaurant/both-provider gates.

nodes.label: docs/architecture.md: Original prototype and durable extension
nodes.description:
## Original prototype and durable extension

- `platform/domain.ts`: demo tenant, catalog, session/cart and order snapshots. One process-local repository.
- `platform/ordering.ts`: confirmation, simulated payment/POS and allowed operational transitions.
- `modules/whatsapp/conversation.ts`: deterministic Spanish text flow and per-customer serialization.
- `integrations/contracts.ts`: typed `PaymentProvider`, `PosProvider`, `WhatsAppTransport` and labeled demo adapters.
- `integrations/whatsapp.ts`: Cloud API sending, raw-byte signature helper and mapped-message normalization.
- `app.ts`: schema validation, bearer-protected demo APIs, static asset allowlist, security headers and webhook ingress.

In the original memory mode, demo duplicate detection and mock POS idempotency work only within a process lifetime. WhatsApp delivery currently happens before the webhook returns; failures receive 5xx and replay reuses the cached domain reply. This is intentionally a test-account scaffold. Restart-safe ingress, distributed concurrency and delivery ambiguity need #6/#8/#10. Memory Maps have no retention pruning beyond session expiry on access; use test data only. The current mock provider cannot exercise real provider timeout ambiguity or financial correctness.

The browser UI uses native HTML/CSS/JavaScript and semantic forms. It sends a page-memory bearer token, uses text-only DOM insertion, and makes no automatic third-party requests. Its local key is temporary demo access, not the owner/staff identity system. All demo order endpoints are isolated under `/api/demo`. A deployed pilot must use real staff authentication and disable all simulation mutations.

UI language defaults to Spanish and supports explicit English selection; the browser stores only that preference and updates document `lang`, labels, accessible names, error text and number/date presentation. Chat locale is conversation-scoped; explicit language commands work in WhatsApp. Catalog snapshots include Spanish and English names, while item IDs and CLP totals stay stable across language changes. Persist these preferences/translation fields in the durable model; do not infer a customer's identity from the selected language.

nodes.label: docs/live-demo-onboarding.md: 1. Recommended route
nodes.description:
## 1. Recommended route

Use Meta WhatsApp Cloud API directly for the first real-phone demo: the repository already contains its signed ingress and text transport. Twilio is an optional alternative that needs its own transport, webhook parser/signature validation and configuration. Do not create/pay for both routes merely to get started.

Use a test sender and enrolled recipients initially. Your existing WhatsApp Business app/number can remain unchanged and your phone can be a test recipient. No Twilio account is needed for the recommended direct-Meta route. Use synthetic restaurant/menu data until a restaurant partner approves its own data. Obtain actual Toteat/Fudo integration access after a pilot partner is available; a generic developer signup is not equivalent to an API-enabled restaurant environment.

There are three distinct deliverables:

| Deliverable | What is real | What is still needed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| POS-independent prospect demo | WhatsApp conversation, menu, persisted order, local kitchen dashboard, pay at pickup | Meta test assets, approved recipients, public HTTPS webhook, durable order processing and explicit local-fulfillment mode |
| Full payment prospect demo | Everything above plus provider-hosted Webpay sandbox and verified test-payment result | Reachable integration environment, checkout/commit/status adapter, callback route and failure tests; no restaurant POS account required |
| Limited live restaurant pilot | Registered restaurant sender, real settlement, actual kitchen/pickup operations | Merchant/provider/sender approvals, operational ownership, production configuration and acceptance |

Tokens do not finish the implementation automatically: the current POS and payment adapters are simulated. State/retry workers, local fulfillment, pay-at-pickup handling, real checkout and reconciliation still need engineering work. The existing browser simulator is not evidence of real-phone or Webpay acceptance.

nodes.label: docs/live-demo-onboarding.md: 10. First handoff
nodes.description:
## 10. First handoff

Meta's developer entry redirected to the official Business Suite login. The founder needs a new Facebook owner account, and its registration form is now open in the in-app browser. Complete registration yourself, including new password, terms and verification, then tell the agent when signed in. We can inspect existing assets, prepare the app under Arkaive Studio, and guide recipient verification afterward. We have not created a developer account/app, generated a Meta token, subscribed to a paid service, migrated a live phone or contacted a vendor. Do not create Twilio, Toteat or Fudo accounts merely to satisfy a signup checklist.

The next engineering slice is durable state separation plus local kitchen/pay-at-pickup support; Webpay connectivity/adapter work and Meta setup can proceed independently. The first completed prospect-demo rehearsal must show actual phone messages, persisted order/restart recovery, truthful payment labels, one local kitchen ticket, ready/collected actions and reconciled counts, in English and Spanish. A subsequent sandbox rehearsal adds verified hosted payment. Real settlement and POS acceptance are separate later evidence.

nodes.description:
## 2. What you provide first—without secrets in chat

| Needed from the founder | When | How |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sign in to Meta/Facebook and complete developer enrollment if requested | Now | Use the opened Meta browser tab; password, OTP, CAPTCHA and terms stay under owner control |
| Verify the phone used as a permitted test recipient | Meta setup | Enter the verification code on Meta's page; the phone can use ordinary WhatsApp or the Business mobile app |

No Chilean tax identity, bank account, restaurant subscription or live card is needed for the proposed first demo. If a provider actually requests additional identity information, review that requirement rather than inventing restaurant details. Business name and registration email alone cannot create a verified Meta identity.

Passwords, API secrets, payment credentials and OTPs do not belong in the repository, GitHub issues or chat. Sign in through the provider's browser page. Configure runtime secrets privately in ignored local environment files or a staging secret manager. We can verify presence/permissions without printing secret values.

## 3. Browser-assisted setup and staying in the loop

This session currently exposes the in-app browser, not Chrome. We can navigate Spanish pages, explain fields in English and prepare settings there after you sign in. If an approved Chrome connection is made available, it can work with existing signed-in tabs; bulk copying/exporting a Chrome profile, cookies or saved passwords is not the setup plan. Account setup will be user-owned. We can fill non-binding fields with your supplied details, prepare configurations and verify results. You take over for new password entry and verification prompts as needed. Accepting terms, granting new sensitive permissions, changing a live sender/account and activating paid services must be surfaced at the actual step. Billing purchases and real financial transactions remain with you. Vendor messages can be drafted in Spanish; sending requires the recipient and text to be authorized.

At each meaningful account milestone, report the account/environment, completed setup, current blocker and next action in English. Capture progress without exposing secrets. Do not claim a provider integration works until its API response and restaurant-side result have been verified.

nodes.description:
## 4. WhatsApp: account assets and the test journey

The mobile Business app is different from the API assets. Meta's [official Cloud API collection](https://www.postman.com/meta/whatsapp-business-platform/collection/wlk6lh4/whatsapp-cloud-api) describes a business portfolio, WABA and sender, plus user/system-user access tokens and messaging permissions. Some current Meta setup pages require login, so test-number availability and restrictions must be confirmed in your own console.

| Asset/configuration | Who supplies it |
| --- | --- |
| Meta login and business-asset administrator | You/the business owner |
| Developer app with WhatsApp use case | We help configure under your account |
| App ID, WABA ID, sender phone-number ID | Generated/located in Meta |
| App secret and suitable scoped access token | Generated through Meta; stored privately |
| Permitted test recipients | You/partner verify them in Meta and receive messages on their phones |
| Webhook verify token | We generate it and match it in Meta/application config |
| HTTPS callback and supported Graph version | We configure and verify |

Test sequence: a permitted phone sends a greeting to the test sender → Meta posts a signed event → our mapped branch loads its catalog → the app replies in Spanish/English → the customer selects and confirms items → a persisted order appears. For pay at pickup, staff accepts the order into the local kitchen queue while payment remains due. For Webpay sandbox, send the application checkout link, verify the test-payment result server-side, then enqueue local kitchen work. Staff marks ready/collected and the customer receives permitted notifications. Transport-only smoke tests may still use the existing simulator, explicitly labeled.

Your existing Business number is not required as the initial API sender. Do not deregister or migrate it just to test. If it is later intended as the live restaurant sender, inspect account eligibility, supported coexistence/migration and ownership implications before changing it. For onboarding other restaurants, confirm the applicable Meta review/permissions/onboarding requirements separately.

For longer-running staging, use an appropriate scoped system-user credential rather than relying on a temporary dashboard token. Recipient verification and sender ownership may require actions on your phone that browser automation cannot perform for you.

## 5. Toteat access

The [official configuration reference](https://developers.toteat.com/tags/config_tag.yaml) requires restaurant-owner API enablement and provides a token plus restaurant, local and user IDs. It describes the external-order setting and origin-channel configuration.

Request an authorized test branch or vendor-provided development account. Collect the environment/base URL, API token, restaurant/local/user IDs, permitted routes, origin channel, product/modifier identifiers, payment-method mapping and a way for staff to inspect a test order. Verify access to catalog, shift/status and external-order creation. Do not assume a public developer signup grants this environment.

The [API specification](https://developers.toteat.com/toteatApi_v2.yaml) documents order-related paths. Obtain a definite answer on hosted-checkout creation, duplicate/timeout lookup and actual kitchen routing. A test endpoint alone does not prove a test restaurant or printer/KDS configuration exists.

nodes.description:
## 6. Fudo access

Fudo's [external-order guide](https://soporte.fu.do/es/articles/15707531-integracion-de-pedidos-externos-via-apis) requires an active account and approval, which it says can take up to a month. The Delivery module is required; externally created pickup orders use that workflow. Approved setup generates Client ID/Client Secret credentials.

Request this early. We need approval, authorized technical documentation, isolated test operations and credentials—not merely a trial login. Ask how catalog, pickup/payment mapping, status callbacks and kitchen acknowledgment work for that account.

Fudo's separate [general API](https://soporte.fu.do/es/articles/11939789-api-publica-de-proposito-general) is a Pro-plan data interface with its own key/secret setup. Confirm whether it is needed for catalog access alongside the approved integration before buying a plan or generating extra credentials. General access does not substitute for external-order approval.

nodes.label: docs/live-demo-onboarding.md: 7. Payments: prove the supported flow before choosing accounts
nodes.description:
## 7. Payments: prove the supported flow before choosing accounts

For the prospect demo, choose **Webpay Plus integration environment**, independently of Toteat/Fudo. The founder explicitly approved a test-payment demonstration without a POS. The [official runnable Node example](https://proyecto-ejemplo-node.transbankdevelopers.cl/webpay-plus) configures SDK-provided integration credentials; no new production merchant account is needed for that documented sandbox path. The [operations example](https://proyecto-ejemplo-node.transbankdevelopers.cl/api-reference/webpay-plus) describes authoritative status and reversal operations.

Verification on 28 October: an isolated transaction-creation probe using published integration credentials and synthetic order data received **HTTP 403 with an Incapsula security page** from the current development network, before an API JSON response. No checkout token or payment was obtained. This does not prove missing merchant access; sandbox connectivity must be resolved through a supported network/deployment or vendor guidance before claiming that the full flow works. Retain pay at pickup as the working fallback; do not bypass a security challenge or silently substitute a simulated approval.

Implementation sequence:

1. Server creates a payment attempt for the immutable order total, with unique buy-order/session references and sandbox environment recorded.
2. WhatsApp contains an opaque, expiring HTTPS application link. Its landing page submits `token_ws` by POST to the allowlisted Webpay sandbox URL returned by creation; a plain GET of the gateway URL does not implement the documented handoff.
3. The customer uses only Transbank's published test card/bank identity on the provider's page. Our app never collects card data.
4. The callback uses the saved token and server-side commit/status response to verify authorization, amount, order and session. Handle cancel, rejection, timeout and duplicate returns separately; a success-looking browser URL is not payment proof.
5. Store `sandbox_authorized` distinctly from real-money receipts and from pay-at-pickup amounts. Enqueue one local kitchen ticket. Show provider reference and fulfillment/payment states separately in the dashboard.

Pay-at-pickup is a separate explicit payment method: confirmation creates an unpaid order, staff acceptance permits preparation, and a scoped staff action can record payment at pickup with audit history. Preparation/readiness must never imply payment. Do not automatically change a failed/uncertain online payment into pay at pickup; get an explicit choice and reconcile the original attempt to avoid double collection.

For the later restaurant pilot:

Ask each POS whether its approved API creates a hosted checkout URL for an external pickup order, how payment is authoritatively verified and how refunds work. Public order payment fields are not evidence of link generation or actual settlement.

If POS-hosted checkout is supported, use the documented test contract. Otherwise, record approval for an independent Chile-supported sandbox gateway. [Transbank's official Webpay Plus example](https://proyecto-ejemplo-node.transbankdevelopers.cl/webpay-plus) uses provided integration credentials, returns a payment token and URL, and submits the token through a payment form. We can build our own opaque checkout link around that documented flow; it is not a POS-created link. Production merchant onboarding is separate.

Mercado Pago is another candidate. Its [integration dashboard](https://www.mercadopago.cl/developers/es/docs/your-integrations/introduction) distinguishes test/production setup; exact test credentials/account requirements depend on the chosen Checkout variant. Do not infer test/production solely from a token prefix. Select one gateway after confirming the restaurant's existing arrangement and the supported POS reconciliation path.

For a real-money pilot, the restaurant must supply the merchant authorization and whatever business/tax/settlement information the selected provider requires. Configure the intended settlement recipient explicitly; do not route restaurant receipts into a developer's personal account by default. Card details remain on the provider's hosted page.

## 8. Engineering execution and exit evidence

| Stage | Inputs needed | Work and exit evidence | Existing issues |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Meta access and ownership | Founder login and recipient phone | Developer app/test sender and verified recipient; no restaurant POS prerequisite | #9 |
| POS-independent prospect demo | Synthetic menu and founder testing | Local kitchen mode, pay at pickup, separate payment/fulfillment ledger, bilingual dashboard | [#27](https://github.com/arkajyotiMukherjee/easy-eatery/issues/27) |
| Real WhatsApp transport | Meta assets, recipient verification, HTTPS endpoint | Actual greeting/menu/cart from your phone; verified signature/routing; redacted delivery evidence | #9 |
| Durable orchestration | Development access; no additional vendor account needed | Separate payment/fulfillment states, idempotent workers, retry/error visibility | #8/#10/#12 |
| POS adapters | Authorized Toteat/Fudo contracts and test credentials | Real catalog mapping; one test pickup accepted in each selected restaurant workflow; references/status proof | #7/#13/#22 |
| Hosted sandbox checkout | Webpay integration credentials and reachable sandbox | Test approval/failure/abandonment; authoritative amount/order/session verification; no simulated pay endpoint in sandbox mode | #14; local fulfillment tracked separately from #15's POS acceptance |
| Integrated rehearsal | Staff test window, menu approval, both provider configurations | WhatsApp → sandbox payment → one kitchen order → ready → pickup → reconciled dashboard | #16–#18/#21/#23 |
| Live pilot | Registered sender, merchant activation, cloud budget and operational owner | Restricted real traffic, actual settlement, recovery/refund runbook and restaurant sign-off | #19–#21 |

First complete the standalone prospect demo; then obtain a restaurant partner and start its owner-authorized access requests. Both-provider pilot acceptance remains later work. Provider waits are external; do not promise a fixed launch date before access is proven. Existing roadmap gates for actual restaurant/POS acceptance do not block the standalone demo.

Staging needs a stable HTTPS app/worker endpoint, PostgreSQL, secret storage and logs with redacted credentials/contacts. The existing architecture targets Santiago. A local tunnel can prove an early webhook with test data; an unattended customer demo needs hosted staging. We need your chosen cloud project/access and cost cap before resource creation.

Acceptance includes duplicate messages/callbacks, wrong payment totals, closed/sold-out state, expired checkout, POS timeout, late payment and paid-but-unaccepted recovery. A success redirect is not payment proof, and payment success is not kitchen acceptance. Record one provider reference and one restaurant-side acknowledgment for each test order, not merely our dashboard status.

## Implementation progress — local pay-at-pickup slice

The bilingual local kitchen/pay-at-pickup workflow is implemented with PostgreSQL migration 003, per-branch configuration, immutable order payment/fulfillment method, separate due/store-paid states, scoped accept/payment actions and audit/outbox persistence. See README for setup. A browser rehearsal completed one synthetic CLP 4,500 pickup and recovered it after server restart on port 3312. Checks: 15 application tests; 10 database subtests plus the parent passed. This does not complete the real-phone, notification, Webpay or POS criteria of #27. No legal business information was invented or submitted.

nodes.label: docs/live-demo-onboarding.md: Fudo
nodes.description:
### Fudo

Asunto: Solicitud de evaluación de integración de pedidos externos — Easy Eatery

Hola, solicitamos evaluar una integración para el restaurante [cuenta/local], con autorización de [administrador]. Easy Eatery permite pedidos por WhatsApp con retiro en local; nuestro caso específico es [necesidad no cubierta por las soluciones actuales]. El desarrollo estará a cargo de [nombre/contacto]. Queremos confirmar la aprobación, el Módulo de Delivery y la disponibilidad de una cuenta o entorno de pruebas. ¿Qué documentación y credenciales necesitamos para catálogo/modificadores, pedidos de retiro pagados, eventos y confirmación en cocina? ¿Existe un API para enlaces de pago alojados o un flujo admitido con una pasarela externa? Gracias.

Before sending either draft, fill the placeholders and confirm the official recipient/support channel inside the authorized account. Do not send credentials in the request.

nodes.label: docs/live-demo-onboarding.md: Optional Twilio route
nodes.description:
### Optional Twilio route

If direct Meta setup is blocked, evaluate Twilio's testing environment. Its [current quickstart](https://www.twilio.com/docs/whatsapp/quickstart) covers the trial flow; the [legacy Sandbox](https://www.twilio.com/docs/whatsapp/sandbox) uses a shared sender and recipient enrollment with a join code. An existing WhatsApp Business API sender is not needed for that Sandbox. Trial limits, billing and the console variant must be checked in the account. It is a test environment, not a customer deployment.

We would need a user-owned Twilio project, Account SID and appropriate API credentials, sender configuration, joined test recipients and inbound/status webhook settings. It requires additional adapter work; our Meta webhook route cannot simply be pointed at Twilio. The [customer-service window/template rules](https://www.twilio.com/docs/whatsapp/key-concepts) still apply; delayed pickup notifications need approved templates when outside the allowed window.

nodes.label: docs/live-demo-onboarding.md: Toteat
nodes.description:
### Toteat

Asunto: Acceso de pruebas e integración de pedidos por WhatsApp — Easy Eatery

Hola, estamos desarrollando Easy Eatery para pedidos por WhatsApp con retiro en local en Chile. Contamos con autorización del restaurante [nombre/local]. Necesitamos confirmar el acceso a un ambiente de pruebas, la habilitación de órdenes externas y los permisos del API. ¿Pueden indicar los requisitos, credenciales y documentación para catálogo/modificadores, estado de turno, creación y seguimiento de pedidos y notificaciones? ¿Existe un API para generar un enlace de pago alojado? También necesitamos confirmar la conciliación de pagos externos y el comportamiento ante pedidos duplicados o timeouts. No activaremos pedidos reales sin coordinar una prueba con el restaurante. Gracias.
