nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/00-product-direction-and-milestones.md: 1. Product thesis
nodes.description:
## 1. Product thesis

Build a modular restaurant technology platform for Chilean independent restaurants and small multi-branch operators. The platform sells independently useful modules that share data when the restaurant enables multiple services. Each additional module can close more of the customer loop, but no module should require a different paid module unless that dependency is explicitly disclosed and accepted.

Initial modules:

1. QR digital menu (optional)
2. Pickup ordering and kitchen/order dashboard
3. Loyalty program with Google Wallet and POS support
4. CRM and customer/event aggregation
5. WhatsApp conversational ordering, campaigns and payment links
6. Catering/private-event estimation and quotations

Important shared capabilities: tenant/branch administration, menu and product catalog, order management, identity/consent, integration connections, payment abstraction, notifications, audit log, module entitlements and an event outbox.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/00-product-direction-and-milestones.md: 2. Two-person-team delivery rule
nodes.description:
## 2. Two-person-team delivery rule

**Do not build the whole platform before the first customer.** Start with design prototypes and a concierge pilot. Use the partner's industry access to recruit 3–5 qualified restaurants, interview them, show realistic clickable flows, and obtain a written pilot commitment from one customer. The first release may use manual steps behind a polished interface where safe and transparent; automate only when repeated pain has been observed.

Two founders should divide ownership by capability rather than by customer-facing module:

- **Product/domain owner:** restaurant interviews, Chilean operations, workflow design, data and integration access, onboarding, pricing and support.
- **Engineering/design-system owner:** prototype system, shared platform skeleton, deployment, quality, security and reusable implementation patterns.
- Both founders participate in design reviews, pilot onboarding and weekly priority decisions.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/00-product-direction-and-milestones.md: 3. How to choose the first workflow
nodes.description:
## 3. How to choose the first workflow

Score candidate workflows from 1–5 on: (a) pain intensity, (b) frequency, (c) customer willingness to pay, (d) time to first measurable value, (e) ability to demo without deep integration, (f) integration risk, and (g) ability to create a repeatable loop. Weight pain, willingness to pay and time-to-value twice as strongly as novelty. Pick the one workflow with the best evidence, not the most ambitious bundle.

Candidate starting wedges to test:

- Pickup storefront + order-status screen, with menu sync/manual fallback.
- WhatsApp inquiry capture + catering quote PDF, for restaurants with high event sales.
- POS sales import + simple customer visit report, if the restaurant already has a POS and wants customer data.
- Loyalty enrolment and manual staff-assisted point earning, if retention is an acute concern.

Do not decide from founder preference alone. The design partner's current process, current spend and willingness to pilot determine the first wedge.
nodes.norm_label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/00-product-direction-and-milestones.md: 3. how to choose the first workflow

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/00-product-direction-and-milestones.md: 4. Milestones ordered by value and risk, not by original module numbering
nodes.description:
## 4. Milestones ordered by value and risk, not by original module numbering

| Milestone | Value | Relative complexity | Required outcome / exit gate |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| M0 — Problem validation | Very high | Low | 3–5 interviews; one written problem statement with current workaround, cost of problem and buying trigger |
| M1 — Clickable prototype | Very high | Low–medium | Testable prototype of onboarding + chosen workflow + owner dashboard; at least 3 users understand it without explanation |
| M2 — Pilot commitment | Very high | Low | One named restaurant agrees on scope, success metric, owner/contact, data access and pilot date; no production build before this |
| M3 — Concierge/manual pilot | High | Low–medium | Deliver the workflow using prototype/no-code/manual back office where possible; measure outcome and failures over actual restaurant operations |
| M4 — Minimal shared platform | High | Medium | Tenant/branch, user roles, audit, module entitlements, menu or lead data required by the chosen wedge, backup and production deploy |
| M5 — First paid workflow | Very high | Medium | One module works end-to-end for one restaurant, including support runbook and basic billing outside product if needed |
| M6 — Close one data loop | Very high | Medium | A real event (order/sale/quote) updates customer or lead record and yields one useful outcome/report; no requirement to automate every integration yet |
| M7 — First provider integration | High | Medium–high | One chosen POS/payment provider is validated in a real account and its retries, reconciliation and credential rotation are tested |
| M8 — First additional module | High | Medium | A second separately purchasable module can be enabled without breaking existing workflows; proves modularity |
| M9 — Self-service onboarding and subscriptions | Medium–high | Medium–high | Admin can pick modules, complete setup and understand pricing; automate only after the initial manual process is stable |
| M10 — CRM segments and campaign automation | Medium–high | High | RFM, consent rules, campaign audience preview, suppression and delivery reporting are reliable |
| M11 — Native Google Wallet lifecycle + POS redemption | Medium–high | High | Issuer approval, pass lifecycle, POS scan/redeem and reversals tested across failure cases |
| M12 — AI WhatsApp ordering and advanced attribution | Medium | High | Only after deterministic ordering/campaign ROI is demonstrated; AI never controls payment or pricing correctness |
| M13 — Multi-POS coverage, multi-country and advanced analytics | Lower near-term | Very high | Enter only after repeatable local onboarding, support and positive gross margin |
nodes.norm_label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/00-product-direction-and-milestones.md: 4. milestones ordered by value and risk, not by original module numbering

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/00-product-direction-and-milestones.md: 5. Minimum sellable V1 — define it after M1/M2
nodes.description:
## 5. Minimum sellable V1 — define it after M1/M2

There is no universal V1 that includes all six modules. V1 is the smallest complete restaurant outcome. Its common foundation should include:

- Spanish (Chile) UI, CLP, `America/Santiago`, one restaurant + branch, secure login/roles.
- Branded owner dashboard with module status, onboarding checklist, support/contact route and recent activity.
- One actual independently valuable workflow.
- Clear error states and manual recovery; order/payment/quote states are visible.
- Basic audit log, consent recording where customer data is collected, export/delete process, backups and error reporting.
- Production deploy, environment separation, restore test and support runbook.

Only add a paid module after its minimum flow can complete without depending on an unpurchased module.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/00-product-direction-and-milestones.md: 7. Out of scope before proven demand
nodes.description:
## 7. Out of scope before proven demand

- Microservices, Kubernetes, Kafka, data warehouse, graph database, separate auth service.
- An LLM-based general assistant across all features.
- Every Chilean POS provider and every payment provider.
- Fully automated billing/tax documentation before local accountant/legal review.
- Native mobile apps; responsive web/PWA first.
- Fully autonomous customer identity merging.
- Loyalty points earned from uncertain/unreconciled POS events.
nodes.norm_label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/00-product-direction-and-milestones.md: 7. out of scope before proven demand

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/00-product-direction-and-milestones.md: 8. Risk register
nodes.description:
## 8. Risk register

| Risk | Mitigation / gate |
|---|---|
| Restaurant does not pay for the integrated bundle | Sell a narrow workflow; obtain pilot commitment before implementation |
| POS API unavailable/approval-gated | Get provider account, API docs, permissions and test data before promising connector support |
| Modular product becomes a bespoke integration agency | Standardize provider adapters, onboarding checklist and supported capability matrix |
| Feature interdependence defeats modular billing | Capability graph and module-isolation acceptance tests |
| Customer data without consent | Purpose-bound consent records, minimal collection and Chilean legal review before campaigns |
| Third-party API outage loses events | Transactional outbox, retries, replay and reconciliation |
| Support burden overwhelms two founders | Manual concierge is acceptable in pilot; log recurring intervention, automate only recurring steps |

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/00-product-direction-and-milestones.md: 9. Decision log format
nodes.description:
## 9. Decision log format

Keep `docs/decisions/NNN-short-title.md` with: context, decision, alternatives, reasoning, consequences, date, owner and revisit trigger. Any unresolved provider access must be marked `BLOCKED_PENDING_PROVIDER_VALIDATION`, not presented as shipped capability.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/00-product-direction-and-milestones.md: Business
nodes.description:
### Business
- Paid restaurants and active branches.
- Activation rate per module.
- Gross margin per tenant/module, including third-party fees and support time.
- Onboarding hours per tenant; support minutes per week.
- Module expansion/retention and cancellation reasons.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/00-product-direction-and-milestones.md: Discovery / sales
nodes.description:
### Discovery / sales
- Interview-to-prototype acceptance rate.
- Prototype-to-pilot commitment rate.
- Time from first meeting to first usable outcome.
- Stated monthly willingness to pay and current workaround costs.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/00-product-direction-and-milestones.md: Product
nodes.description:
### Product
- Time to complete core task (menu/order/quote depending on wedge).
- Successful workflow completion rate.
- Number of staff interventions per order/quote.
- Integration events matched and reconciled; duplicate/missed event count.
- Repeat purchase or qualified catering lead conversion, only where measurable.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/00-product-direction-and-milestones.md: Rule for moving work between milestones
nodes.description:
### Rule for moving work between milestones

A feature is P0 only when at least one is true: (1) without it, the first contracted workflow cannot run; (2) the buyer explicitly says it is a purchase blocker; (3) it protects money, privacy or order correctness; or (4) it is required by a provider/contract/legal obligation. Otherwise it is P1/P2 and must compete on evidence.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/01-platform-architecture.md
nodes.description: # Shared Platform Architecture

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/01-platform-architecture.md: Shared Platform Architecture
nodes.description: # Shared Platform Architecture

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/01-platform-architecture.md: 1. Architectural decision
nodes.description:
## 1. Architectural decision

Use a **TypeScript monorepo with a modular monolith**, PostgreSQL as the system of record, a PostgreSQL-backed job queue/outbox, and a single regional deployment. Modules have explicit domain boundaries but share a database and deployment initially. Split into services only when an independently scaling/operating requirement is demonstrated.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/01-platform-architecture.md: 10. Deployment topology for first customers
nodes.description:
## 10. Deployment topology for first customers

- `web`: Cloud Run service in `southamerica-west1` (Santiago), public storefront/admin UI.
- `api`: Cloud Run service in `southamerica-west1`.
- `worker`: Cloud Run service/job in `southamerica-west1`; concurrency and max instances constrained to avoid overwhelming PostgreSQL/provider rate limits.
- Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL in `southamerica-west1`; same region as API/worker.
- Cloud Storage regional bucket; verify data location/backup behavior.
- Cloudflare for DNS/CDN/WAF if useful; public static images can be cached, never private customer/checkout responses.
- Secret Manager for provider credentials.
- CI builds immutable container images; separate dev/staging/prod projects/environments where practical.

Google documents Cloud Run and Cloud SQL locations for Santiago. Availability of each specific ancillary service (scheduler, storage, secret manager and monitoring) must be checked during deployment design. AWS announced Chile region plans for end of 2026, but do not assume it is production-available until the official region/service matrix says so.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/01-platform-architecture.md: 11. What not to build yet
nodes.description:
## 11. What not to build yet

No microservices, Kafka, Kubernetes, Elasticsearch, graph database, Redis, separate analytics warehouse or SpacetimeDB in the initial architecture. PostgreSQL plus reviewed SQL is enough for transactional and early reporting workloads. SSE serves live kitchen updates.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/01-platform-architecture.md: 12. Architecture acceptance criteria
nodes.description:
## 12. Architecture acceptance criteria

- Each module can be entitlement-disabled in tests without disabling other modules.
- Cross-tenant access tests fail closed.
- All money-related state transitions use database transactions and integer CLP.
- Outbox failure/retry/replay is tested.
- Database migration and rollback/forward-recovery policy is documented.
- API schema and migration checks run in CI.
- One scripted deployment provisions staging and smoke-tests it.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/01-platform-architecture.md: 2. Common stack (all modules)
nodes.description:
## 2. Common stack (all modules)

- **Language:** TypeScript end-to-end for application code.
- **Monorepo:** `pnpm` workspaces + Turborepo (or pnpm alone if Turborepo adds friction).
- **Public/admin web:** Next.js App Router, React, TypeScript.
- **UI:** Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui/Radix; shared tokens and accessible components.
- **Forms/validation:** React Hook Form + Zod; server validates every payload independently.
- **API:** NestJS REST API (clear module boundaries, DI, guards, OpenAPI generation). Use REST for stable internal/public contracts.
- **Database:** managed PostgreSQL. Prisma for normal CRUD and migrations; allow reviewed SQL for reports/locking when required. Never let Prisma model design replace explicit database constraints.
- **Jobs:** `pg-boss` or an equivalent PostgreSQL-backed queue. Use one implementation; do not add Redis just for jobs in MVP.
- **Real-time:** Server-Sent Events (SSE) for kitchen/order status. Start with polling fallback. WebSocket is not required unless bidirectional interactive features prove necessary.
- **Files:** Google Cloud Storage (signed URLs for private files) or equivalent S3-compatible object storage.
- **Auth:** start with a mature hosted/managed auth provider or a well-maintained auth library; enforce tenant+branch membership server-side. Pick one and document the trade-offs before coding. Never DIY password/session cryptography.
- **Tests:** Vitest/Jest for unit/integration; Playwright for end-to-end; provider sandbox contract tests.
- **Observability:** structured JSON logs, error tracking, uptime monitoring, key domain metrics and redacted integration request IDs.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/01-platform-architecture.md: 3. Repository layout
nodes.description:
## 3. Repository layout

```text
apps/
  web/                 # Next.js owner dashboard and public storefront
  api/                 # NestJS REST API
  worker/              # job/outbox processors, same domain packages
packages/
  ui/                  # shared accessible UI components and design tokens
  config/              # eslint, tsconfig, test config
  contracts/           # Zod schemas, event types, API DTOs
  domain/              # entities, use cases, policies, module registry
  integrations/        # provider interfaces and adapters
  localization/        # es-CL labels, formatting and messages
  testing/             # fixtures, factories, test helpers
docs/
  specs/ decisions/ runbooks/
prisma/                # schema and migrations (or package-local schema)
```

Use import boundaries so modules cannot directly depend on another module's internal implementation. Cross-module behavior should use public application services or versioned domain events.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/01-platform-architecture.md: 4. Logical architecture
nodes.description:
## 4. Logical architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  W[Next.js web: owner + public storefront] --> API[NestJS REST API]
  K[Kitchen display] --> API
  API --> D[(PostgreSQL)]
  API --> O[Transactional outbox]
  O --> Q[pg-boss / worker]
  Q --> POS[POS adapters]
  Q --> PAY[Payment adapters]
  Q --> WAL[Google Wallet adapter]
  Q --> WA[WhatsApp adapter]
  Q --> PDF[PDF / email jobs]
  API --> GCS[Object storage]
  CDN[CDN / DNS / WAF] --> W
```

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/01-platform-architecture.md: 5. Bounded contexts/modules
nodes.description:
## 5. Bounded contexts/modules

- `platform`: tenants, branches, users, roles, audit log, feature/module entitlements, support metadata.
- `catalog`: menus, categories, items, modifiers, prices, availability, source-of-truth flags and catalog imports.
- `orders`: cart validation, order lifecycle, item snapshots, pickup slot, kitchen state.
- `payments`: payment attempts, provider references, webhook inbox, reconciliation, refunds.
- `loyalty`: accounts, immutable ledger, rules, redemption, reversal, pass sync status.
- `crm`: customer identity aliases, profiles, consent purposes, visit/transaction aggregation, segments.
- `messaging`: templates, conversation state, outbound campaign, delivery events and suppression.
- `catering`: event inquiry, pricing rules, quote versions, PDF artifacts, lead lifecycle.
- `integrations`: connection credential references, provider capabilities, sync runs, webhook inbox/outbox.
- `billing`: platform subscriptions, entitlements, usage events and invoices/charges; do not conflate with restaurant order payments.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/01-platform-architecture.md: 6. Dependency rule
docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/01-platform-architecture.md: 7. Tenancy and identity
nodes.description:
## 7. Tenancy and identity

- `tenant_id` on every tenant-owned root/record; `branch_id` where an operation is branch-specific.
- UUID/ULID internal identifiers; do not expose sequential database IDs publicly.
- Resolve tenant context from authenticated membership or unguessable public slug; never trust a client-supplied `tenant_id` alone.
- Add composite unique constraints including `tenant_id` for tenant-scoped slugs/external provider IDs.
- Consider PostgreSQL RLS as defense in depth, but still scope every query and use least-privilege DB roles.
- Tenant timezone/currency are configuration fields; for Chile default timezone is `America/Santiago`, currency `CLP`.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/01-platform-architecture.md: 8. API standards
nodes.description:
## 8. API standards

- REST `/api/v1/...`; OpenAPI generated and checked into CI.
- Use Zod DTO schemas from `packages/contracts` or generate clients from OpenAPI; avoid duplicate schemas drifting.
- Error envelope `{ code, message, requestId, details? }`; do not leak provider payloads/secrets.
- Idempotency key on operations that create orders, payment attempts, redemptions, quotes where appropriate, and outbound messages.
- Pagination is cursor-based for high-volume resources.
- Rate-limit public endpoints and webhook endpoints separately.
- All time instants stored as `timestamptz`; render in `America/Santiago`.
- Store CLP amounts as integer pesos; never use floating point for currency.
- Currency code is always explicit, even when CLP is tenant default.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/01-platform-architecture.md: 9. Data and event consistency
nodes.description:
## 9. Data and event consistency

Use a transactional outbox: the domain transaction writes both business state and an outbox row. Worker delivery is at-least-once; consumers must be idempotent. Keep processed provider webhooks in a deduplicated inbox. Do not attempt distributed transactions across POS/payment/Wallet/WhatsApp systems.

Examples: `order.confirmed.v1`, `payment.succeeded.v1`, `payment.refunded.v1`, `pos.sale.imported.v1`, `loyalty.points_earned.v1`, `quote.accepted.v1`, `campaign.delivery_updated.v1`.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/10-chile-integrations-pos.md: 1. Do not pretend market share is known
nodes.description:
## 1. Do not pretend market share is known

No independent, reliable public dataset found in this research establishes the most-used restaurant POS specifically in Chile. Vendor-reported figures are not directly comparable: Fudo markets 35,000+ businesses across Latin America; Toteat markets 5,000+ customers across the Americas. These are self-reported, multi-country figures, not Chile market shares.

**Product decision:** Build a provider-neutral connector interface. For actual implementation, prioritize the POS already used by the first contracted restaurant, provided the owner can authorize access. If both are available, Toteat is the first API prototype candidate because its public docs explicitly cover external order creation, product/menu retrieval, order status, sales/reporting and webhooks. Fudo is a strong second candidate due to broad regional footprint, but its external-order integration requires approval. Do not advertise either as universally supported until certified against multiple tenant accounts/plan tiers.

Sources: [Toteat API](https://developers.toteat.com/), [Toteat Chile](https://toteat.com/es-cl/), [Fudo Chile](https://fu.do/es-cl/), [Fudo general API](https://soporte.fu.do/es/articles/11939789-api-publica-de-proposito-general), [Fudo external-order integration](https://soporte.fu.do/es/articles/15707531-integracion-de-pedidos-externos-via-apis).

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/10-chile-integrations-pos.md: 2. Connector capability model
nodes.description:
## 2. Connector capability model

Each tenant/branch connection records capabilities independently:

- `catalog.read`
- `sales.read`
- `sales.details.read`
- `sales.events.receive`
- `orders.create_external`
- `orders.status.read`
- `orders.status.events.receive`
- `customers.read`
- `inventory.read`
- `discounts.apply`
- `refunds.read`
- `fiscal_documents.read`

Capability values: `supported`, `unsupported`, `approval_required`, `plan_required`, `not_tested`, `temporarily_unavailable`. Admin dashboard must show capability statuses. A connector being “connected” does not mean all features are supported.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/10-chile-integrations-pos.md: 3. Toteat public API findings
nodes.description:
## 3. Toteat public API findings

Official portal: <https://developers.toteat.com/>. The documentation says:
- Production base URL: `https://api.toteat.com/mw/or/1.0/`
- Development base URL: `https://apidev.toteat.com/mw/or/1.0/`
- Credentials are enabled by the restaurant owner in `Configuración > Print Server & API > API Config`; token can be refreshed, invalidating old token.
- Requests are JSON; restaurant/local/user identifiers and `xapitoken` are required query parameters for the documented endpoints.
- Available surface includes retrieving menu/products, sales for periods, daily collection, external order creation, shift status, open/specific order status, inventory/accounting reports, available tables, cancelled orders, documents, and webhooks for order/shift/menu changes.
- General limit reported: 10 requests/second; specific endpoints have lower limits (e.g. shift status docs show 3 requests/minute). Follow per-endpoint limit in current OpenAPI spec.
- Webhook receiver must use HTTPS, acknowledge HTTP 200, and respond within 3 seconds; process work asynchronously. Webhook availability/payload fields can differ for legacy vs migrated environments.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/10-chile-integrations-pos.md: 4. Fudo public API findings
nodes.description:
## 4. Fudo public API findings

Official help page: <https://soporte.fu.do/es/articles/11939789-api-publica-de-proposito-general>.
- Public general API is listed as available on Fudo Plan Pro.
- Owner enables it under `Aplicaciones externas > API Pública General`.
- Create a dedicated least-privilege API user under `Administración > Usuarios`; API Key and API Secret are generated there.
- Credentials/token described in the help page expire after 24 hours by default; follow current official API auth/renewal spec. Missing secret must be regenerated.
- Exposed resources include customers, discounts, expenses, ingredients, kitchens, payments, orders, products, suppliers, sales, tables, users and related data.
- Official technical documentation: <https://dev.fu.do/api/> (OpenAPI 3 per Fudo help page).

External order creation is a separate integration path: <https://soporte.fu.do/es/articles/15707531-integracion-de-pedidos-externos-via-apis>. Fudo states it is an exception subject to approval, requires an active account and detailed use case, may take up to one month for a response, and creates a link with Client ID/Client Secret. Events include order rejected/confirmed/ready-to-deliver/delivery-sent/closed. The public API's read access does not imply that external order creation is approved.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/10-chile-integrations-pos.md: 5. Normalized internal model
nodes.description:
## 5. Normalized internal model

`NormalizedSale` fields:
- `tenantId`, `branchId`, `providerKey`, `externalSaleId`, `externalOrderId?`, `occurredAt`, `closedAt?`, `currency`, `grossMinor`, `discountMinor`, `taxMinor?`, `tipMinor?`, `netEligibleMinor?`, `status`, `refundOfExternalSaleId?`, `customerExternalId?`, `items[]`, `rawReference`, `syncRunId`.

Store original payload only if necessary, redacted/minimized with retention. Keep provider amounts separate until finance/accountant confirms which subtotal is eligible for loyalty and RFM.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/10-chile-integrations-pos.md: 6. Shared `PosAdapter` contract
docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/10-chile-integrations-pos.md: 7. Sync safety
nodes.description:
## 7. Sync safety

- Use per-connection sync cursors and overlap windows to handle late-arriving updates.
- Deduplicate on `(tenant_id, provider, external_event_id)` or provider object ID + version/timestamp where no event ID exists.
- Import updates are idempotent; preserve deleted/inactive products as inactive rather than deleting historical references.
- Avoid full-period re-import each time; paginate and use modified timestamps where available.
- Provider rate limits belong in adapter config; schedule jobs with per-connection concurrency control.
- Fail closed on schema changes and emit metrics; don't silently discard unknown required fields.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/10-chile-integrations-pos.md: 8. Certification checklist before listing a provider as supported
nodes.description:
## 8. Certification checklist before listing a provider as supported

- Live connection created by restaurant owner, credentials stored safely, rotation tested.
- Test data covers open/closed shift, product modifier, cancelled order, sale/refund, missing customer, duplicate event and timeout.
- Create order exactly once despite worker retry/ambiguous network failure.
- Order statuses correctly mapped; terminal transitions reconciled.
- Provider API outage produces alert and safe retry.
- Sales total reconciles against the POS UI/report for selected date range.
- Written matrix of feature/plan/permission requirements provided to sales/support.
nodes.norm_label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/10-chile-integrations-pos.md: 8. certification checklist before listing a provider as supported

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/10-chile-integrations-pos.md: Fudo implementation gate
nodes.description:
### Fudo implementation gate

Before production scope commitment, the restaurant and Fudo must confirm:
- Plan Pro status and API access.
- Auth/refresh operation and exact endpoint contracts from current OpenAPI.
- Permitted sales/customer fields and request limits.
- Whether external order creation is approved and which event callback/auth scheme is supported.
- Whether the integration overlaps with Fudo's own products and any terms constrain an external storefront.

Do not invent a Fudo route or auth flow: obtain the OpenAPI specification from `https://dev.fu.do/api/` with authorized credentials and use its exact request/response schemas.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/10-chile-integrations-pos.md: Important Toteat endpoints (verify exact schema in current OpenAPI before coding)
nodes.description:
### Important Toteat endpoints (verify exact schema in current OpenAPI before coding)

| Operation | Documented operation | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Menu/products | `GET /products` | Source menu/price should be treated as authoritative if restaurant chooses POS source-of-truth |
| Create external order | `POST /orders` | Request includes restaurant/local IDs, external `orderReference`, order type/channel, status, document/lines; sync product codes and modifiers beforehand |
| Order status | `GET /orderstatus` | `ic` identifies a specific order; `listing` lists open orders; `det` controls detail |
| Shift status | `GET /shiftstatus` | Low documented limit; don't poll frequently |
| Webhook updates | configured callback URL | Events can include status/menu/shift changes; acknowledge quickly and queue work |
| Sales/reporting | listed in API docs | Use for reconciliation and CRM import; confirm date-window limits and identifiers from OpenAPI |

The public docs show parameters such as `xir`, `xil`, `xiu`, and `xapitoken`; these map to restaurant ID, local/branch number, user ID and API token. Do not put tokens in logs or browser code. Exact query schema and endpoints can differ across legacy/migrated configurations; download and version the current OpenAPI document in the implementation repository after authorized access.
nodes.norm_label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/10-chile-integrations-pos.md: important toteat endpoints (verify exact schema in current openapi before coding)

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/10-chile-integrations-pos.md: Toteat order integration sequence
nodes.description:
### Toteat order integration sequence

1. Owner creates API integration in Toteat and enables the minimum required endpoints/permissions.
2. Store token and provider IDs in Secret Manager; store only the secret reference and nonsecret connection metadata in DB.
3. Fetch menu/products; map provider product code and modifiers to local catalog. Detect unmapped/inactive products.
4. Confirm open shift and branch readiness using appropriate rate limits.
5. Translate internal order into Toteat order schema. Keep the platform order ID in `orderReference`; map pickup/takeaway type and webstore channel correctly.
6. Submit once with a stable idempotency key in local DB. If provider lacks idempotency support, do not blindly retry after ambiguous timeout; query provider by external reference/status first.
7. Store Toteat order ID and accepted response. Receive configured webhook or poll order status within provider limits.
8. Map provider status to internal lifecycle without allowing backward/unknown status to overwrite terminal states without reconciliation.
9. Reconcile daily sales/order totals and report mismatches.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/10-chile-integrations-pos.md: Toteat webhook receiver
nodes.description:
### Toteat webhook receiver

- `POST /api/v1/webhooks/pos/toteat/:connectionPublicId` on HTTPS.
- Validate configured authentication header/signature if provider supports it; if not, use unguessable route token, network/provider constraints where available, strict schema validation, rate limiting and replay defenses.
- Persist redacted payload + delivery ID/time before HTTP 200. Acknowledge within 3 seconds.
- Worker validates tenant mapping and deduplicates. Unknown/unmapped event is stored and alerts operator.
- Do not assume webhook contains every order from the POS: docs indicate order webhook scope may be orders created through the configured API unless provider enables a global webhook. Confirm whether “all POS sales” can be subscribed to.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/05-module-pickup-ordering.md: Module Specification — Pickup Ordering & Kitchen Dashboard
nodes.description: # Module Specification — Pickup Ordering & Kitchen Dashboard
nodes.norm_label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/05-module-pickup-ordering.md: module specification — pickup ordering & kitchen dashboard

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/05-module-pickup-ordering.md: 1. Product contract
nodes.description:
## 1. Product contract

**Commercial module:** `pickup-ordering`  
**Purpose:** Direct website pickup ordering with requested/scheduled pickup times and a reliable restaurant order workflow. QR menu is optional; this module can expose its own branded storefront.

Required capabilities: `catalog.read_orderable`, `order-management`, `pickup-slot-rules`. A payment provider is required only if online prepayment is selected; support `pay-at-pickup` when the restaurant explicitly enables it.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/05-module-pickup-ordering.md: 10. Acceptance tests
nodes.description:
## 10. Acceptance tests

- Repeated checkout request with same idempotency key creates one order.
- Client price tampering does not affect calculated total.
- Two concurrent requests cannot oversubscribe a slot.
- Payment return URL alone cannot mark paid.
- Duplicate/reordered webhooks do not double-confirm or double-earn points.
- Kitchen reconnect restores current state; no lost order due to missing SSE event.
- Module works when QR menu is disabled.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/05-module-pickup-ordering.md: 2. MVP customer flow
nodes.description:
## 2. MVP customer flow

1. Customer opens a branch storefront (direct link, website, social link or WhatsApp link—QR is not required).
2. Selects items/modifiers; frontend displays current price and availability.
3. Selects ASAP or an available pickup slot.
4. Enters minimum contact details needed for order updates; marketing consent is separate and unchecked by default.
5. Server validates catalog version, opening hours, item availability, modifiers, pickup capacity and total.
6. Create a pending order with an idempotency key.
7. If prepaid, create provider payment; only verified provider status confirms payment.
8. On confirmed order/payment policy, mark order accepted and notify kitchen.
9. Kitchen staff move through configured statuses; customer receives order status and pickup instructions.
10. Complete/cancel/refund/reconcile with clear state history.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/05-module-pickup-ordering.md: 3. State machines
nodes.description:
## 3. State machines

Order state and payment state must be separate.

Order (initial proposal): `draft -> pending_confirmation -> confirmed -> preparing -> ready -> completed`; terminal exceptions: `cancelled`, `rejected`, `expired`. If restaurant acceptance is manual, `pending_confirmation` remains until accepted. Define allowed transitions in one domain service.

Payment: `not_required | pending | requires_action | authorized | paid | failed | cancelled | partially_refunded | refunded | unknown`. Actual states map provider-specific statuses into this internal set. No UI redirect may directly set payment to `paid`.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/05-module-pickup-ordering.md: 4. Data model
nodes.description:
## 4. Data model

- `orders(id, tenant_id, branch_id, channel, status, customer_id nullable, guest_contact_json, pickup_slot_start, pickup_slot_end, currency, subtotal_minor, discount_minor, tax_minor, total_minor, catalog_version, idempotency_key, created_at)`
- `order_items` with immutable name/price/modifier snapshots, quantity, notes, source catalog ID.
- `order_status_history(order_id, old_status, new_status, actor_id, reason, occurred_at)`
- `pickup_slots(tenant_id, branch_id, local_date, start_local, end_local, max_orders, current_count, enabled)`
- `payment_attempts(order_id, provider, provider_reference, idempotency_key, amount_minor, currency, status, timestamps)`
- `payment_webhook_inbox(provider, provider_event_id, received_at, processing_status, payload_redacted)`

All monetary values are integer CLP and item price/description snapshots are immutable after confirmed order except audited adjustments.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/05-module-pickup-ordering.md: 5. API sketch
nodes.description:
## 5. API sketch

- `POST /api/v1/public/branches/:slug/order-quotes` — validate cart and return authoritative total/availability; not a durable order.
- `GET /api/v1/public/branches/:slug/pickup-slots?date=YYYY-MM-DD`.
- `POST /api/v1/public/branches/:slug/orders` — requires idempotency key; creates order.
- `GET /api/v1/public/orders/:publicToken` — minimal order tracking, rate-limited and unguessable token.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/orders/:id/accept|reject|transition` through a single transition endpoint/policy.
- Provider webhooks under `/api/v1/webhooks/payments/:provider`.

These are product routes, not provider API endpoints.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/05-module-pickup-ordering.md: 6. Kitchen dashboard
nodes.description:
## 6. Kitchen dashboard

- Lanes for New/Confirmed, Preparing, Ready, Completed (hide completed by default after a time window).
- Order card shows order number, elapsed time, promised pickup time, item count, modifiers, customer initials/limited detail and payment state.
- Touch-friendly state transition actions; server validates permissions and current transition.
- SSE stream for `order.status_changed.v1`, with polling fallback and last-event/connection indicator.
- On reconnect, fetch authoritative lane snapshot; SSE is a notification channel, not the source of truth.
- Optional sound/visual alerts configured per branch.
- Never display PII beyond what kitchen staff need.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/05-module-pickup-ordering.md: 7. Scheduling/availability logic
nodes.description:
## 7. Scheduling/availability logic

- Store the branch's opening hours and pickup slot definitions in local time with IANA zone.
- Handle DST/holiday closures and manual “temporarily closed” state.
- Reserve slot capacity atomically to avoid overbooking. Use database row locks or conditional updates.
- A provider payment pending timeout should release slot only under an explicit policy; avoid freeing capacity while a payment can still complete without reconciliation.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/05-module-pickup-ordering.md: 8. Integration and recovery
nodes.description:
## 8. Integration and recovery

- Payment create request idempotent per order/attempt.
- Provider webhook is verified, stored in inbox, and enqueued; respond quickly; heavy processing in worker.
- `payment.succeeded` and order-confirmation side effects are idempotent.
- Support reconciliation query/report for “payment provider says paid, platform not paid” and inverse cases.
- If a POS connection exists, submitting the order to POS must be a retryable job and independent from customer payment confirmation. Show POS sync status; do not silently duplicate external orders.
- POS order submission failure must result in visible operator alert/manual recovery. Do not tell the customer the restaurant received the order if submission is a mandatory acceptance condition and it failed.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/05-module-pickup-ordering.md: 9. V1 boundaries
nodes.description:
## 9. V1 boundaries

Include only one selected checkout provider or pay-at-pickup, simple modifiers, limited pickup slot configuration and one kitchen board. Exclude delivery fleet/logistics, multi-channel dispatch, complex promotions, gift cards, refunds automation across multiple providers and complex tax/fiscal receipts until validated.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/06-module-loyalty-and-pos.md: Module Specification — Loyalty, Google Wallet & POS Verification
nodes.description: # Module Specification — Loyalty, Google Wallet & POS Verification
nodes.norm_label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/06-module-loyalty-and-pos.md: module specification — loyalty, google wallet & pos verification

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/06-module-loyalty-and-pos.md: 1. Product contract
nodes.description:
## 1. Product contract

**Commercial module:** `loyalty`  
**Purpose:** Let a restaurant operate a transparent points/reward program, enrol members in Google Wallet, earn points from verified eligible purchases and redeem rewards during supported checkout workflows. The Wallet pass is a presentation/identification layer; the platform ledger is authoritative.

Loyalty must work without QR menu or CRM campaign module. Google Wallet and POS are optional providers, but an earning/redemption method must be available for an active loyalty deployment (e.g. staff-assisted lookup/scan and admin adjustment with audit) or the module must clearly remain in setup mode.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/06-module-loyalty-and-pos.md: 10. Acceptance criteria
nodes.description:
## 10. Acceptance criteria

- Concurrent redemption cannot overspend balance.
- Duplicate POS sale events earn once.
- Refund creates reversal rather than deleting original entry.
- Wallet API outage does not corrupt ledger or block valid backend redemption.
- Staff can see Wallet sync state and retry safely.
- Loyalty works with QR menu and CRM marketing both disabled.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/06-module-loyalty-and-pos.md: 2. MVP phases
nodes.description:
## 2. MVP phases

**MVP-A:** rule configuration, member ID/barcode, immutable points ledger, staff search/scan, manual earned-points adjustment with reason, redemption validation and transaction history.  
**MVP-B:** Google Wallet loyalty object creation/update.  
**MVP-C:** automated POS sale ingestion and redemption writeback only after the provider supports the required events/actions.

Never promise “real-time POS loyalty” if the connector only permits read-only sales import or manual polling.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/06-module-loyalty-and-pos.md: 3. Data model
nodes.description:
## 3. Data model

- `loyalty_programs(tenant_id, name, status, earning_rule_version, redemption_rules_json, expiry_policy_json)`
- `loyalty_accounts(tenant_id, customer_id, account_code, current_balance, status)`
- `loyalty_transactions(id, tenant_id, account_id, type, points_delta, source, source_reference, idempotency_key, rule_version, actor_id, reason, occurred_at)` — immutable append-only ledger.
- `loyalty_redemptions(id, tenant_id, account_id, order_id nullable, reward_id, points_reserved, status, idempotency_key, branch_id, actor_id)`
- `loyalty_rewards(id, tenant_id, name, points_cost, reward_type, eligible_item_ids, discount_rules, active)`
- `wallet_passes(tenant_id, account_id, issuer_id, class_id, object_id, sync_state, last_sync_at, last_error_code)`
- `loyalty_sale_events` or canonical `provider_events` for POS source IDs and deduplication.

Balance is a cached projection of the ledger. Write both ledger entry and account balance in one DB transaction. Enforce unique idempotency keys and a unique `(tenant_id, provider, external_sale_id, rule_version)` or equivalent earning key.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/06-module-loyalty-and-pos.md: 4. Earning rules
nodes.description:
## 4. Earning rules

Owner-configurable parameters: eligible subtotal definition, included/excluded categories, accrual rate, rounding method, branch scope, campaign multiplier and refund/reversal policy. For Chile and CLP, define an integer monetary basis; e.g. points per `CLP 10,000` is only an example, not a hard-coded rule. Make rule versions immutable once used; changing the rule applies to future eligible events only unless an explicit retroactive recalculation is run.

Accrue only from an authoritative paid/closed sale or a staff adjustment with reason. If a POS event is not trustworthy or sale total is incomplete, hold for review instead of issuing spendable points automatically.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/06-module-loyalty-and-pos.md: 5. Redemption rules
nodes.description:
## 5. Redemption rules

- Customer/staff identity is resolved before redemption.
- Reserve/deduct points atomically using a balance check and transaction lock/conditional update.
- Tie redemption to order/POS transaction and branch.
- Mark as completed only when the corresponding sale/checkout condition is confirmed; otherwise release reservation or reverse with auditable entry.
- Refunds/cancellations create compensating ledger records, never edit/delete original entries.
- Prevent repeated QR scans from redeeming the same reward twice using single-use server-issued redemption tokens/nonce and expiry.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/06-module-loyalty-and-pos.md: 6. Google Wallet implementation
nodes.description:
## 6. Google Wallet implementation

Official API uses a `LoyaltyClass` for program-level styling and a `LoyaltyObject` for each customer pass. The object can include `accountId`, `accountName`, `barcode` and `loyaltyPoints.balance`; REST resources include insert/get/list/patch/update. Source: <https://developers.google.com/wallet/reference/rest/v1/loyaltyobject> and <https://developers.google.com/wallet/retail/loyalty-cards/use-cases/create>.

Implementation work:
1. Confirm issuer account, business verification, publishing requirements and service-account permissions before promising launch date.
2. Configure issuer/class per platform/tenant policy. Avoid one class per customer; one program class can have many customer objects.
3. Create unique object ID with issuer ID + opaque suffix; barcode contains opaque random/revocable member token, never PII or the current points balance.
4. Generate pass-save link using the officially documented save-to-Wallet flow.
5. On ledger balance change, enqueue Wallet `patch` of the object's balance and relevant fields; use retry/backoff and track last-sync status.
6. Periodically reconcile platform account balances against Wallet objects for failures.
7. Pass update lag must not change reward eligibility; backend ledger is authoritative.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/06-module-loyalty-and-pos.md: 7. POS verification contract
nodes.description:
## 7. POS verification contract

Define provider-neutral adapter capabilities:
- `read_products`, `read_sales`, `read_sale_details`, `receive_sale_events`, `submit_external_order`, `read_order_status`, `apply_discount_or_reward`, `void_or_refund_reference`, `read_customer`.

Every connector capability is recorded as `supported`, `unsupported`, `approval_required`, `not_tested` or `temporarily_unavailable` per account/branch. Do not infer support from another provider's docs.

Staff-assisted V1: scan opaque loyalty QR using a tablet/phone camera or type member code; authenticated staff can look up balance/rewards; reward validation returns a short-lived single-use authorization. If POS cannot consume the authorization, staff marks redemption completed with a required reason and transaction reference; report this as a manual integration, not a POS integration.

Automated V2: receive sale event, normalize identity and final eligible amount, dedupe, evaluate rule version, accrue ledger entry, then update Wallet. Reconcile sales/refunds nightly or at provider-supported interval.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/06-module-loyalty-and-pos.md: 8. Customer identity and consent
nodes.description:
## 8. Customer identity and consent

A member can exist without marketing consent. Record the channel and terms/version for loyalty program acceptance and separately record consent for WhatsApp/email marketing. Phone numbers, names or Wallet `accountName` alone should not be used for fuzzy automatic identity merges.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/06-module-loyalty-and-pos.md: 9. Security and fraud
nodes.description:
## 9. Security and fraud

- Barcode token is random, opaque, revocable and rate-limited.
- Redemption requires authenticated staff/POS authority and tenant+branch permissions.
- Store audit trail for manual changes; manager approval threshold can be configured.
- Rate limit lookup and redemption, alert on repeated failed scans, high-value redemption or abnormal point adjustments.
- Don't trust a QR scan on its own as proof a customer has permission to redeem a reward.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/07-module-crm.md
nodes.description: # Module Specification — Restaurant CRM & Data Aggregation

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/07-module-crm.md: Module Specification — Restaurant CRM & Data Aggregation
nodes.description: # Module Specification — Restaurant CRM & Data Aggregation
nodes.norm_label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/07-module-crm.md: module specification — restaurant crm & data aggregation

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/07-module-crm.md: 1. Product contract
nodes.description:
## 1. Product contract

**Commercial module:** `crm`  
**Purpose:** Provide usable customer profiles and aggregated purchase/engagement history from the channels a restaurant has enabled. It must tolerate missing identity and partial channel coverage. CRM is not a prerequisite for pickup orders, WhatsApp order-taking or catering quotations; those modules may create operational records that later become linked to CRM if the CRM module is purchased/enabled.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/07-module-crm.md: 10. Acceptance criteria
nodes.description:
## 10. Acceptance criteria

- POS sales with no customer ID remain usable as aggregate revenue but do not create fake customer profiles.
- Marketing opt-out blocks new campaign sends even if customer remains in an RFM segment.
- Identity merge/unmerge is audited and preserves historical transaction association.
- RFM report shows calculation window, data source coverage and last computed time.
- Disabling CRM does not delete customer records needed by active orders/loyalty; retention/deletion follows policy.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/07-module-crm.md: 2. V1 features
nodes.description:
## 2. V1 features

- Customer profile with verified identifiers, origin/source, purchase summary and consent status.
- Merge/link/unlink workflow requiring evidence and audit.
- Transaction/visit history from platform orders and supported POS imports.
- Simple RFM segmentation: New, Frequent, High Value, At Risk, Inactive; thresholds configurable per restaurant.
- Saved segments and audience preview when campaign module is enabled.
- Import and export with explicit permissions, retention and privacy safeguards.
- No campaign sending if no messaging/marketing module entitlement exists.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/07-module-crm.md: 3. Data model
nodes.description:
## 3. Data model

- `customers(id, tenant_id, display_name, created_at, updated_at, status)`
- `customer_identities(id, tenant_id, customer_id, identity_type, normalized_value_hash, encrypted_value nullable, verification_status, source, linked_at, revoked_at)`; uniqueness scoped to tenant and identifier rules. Hashing/normalization must be designed to support lookup while minimizing unnecessary plaintext storage.
- `customer_consents(id, tenant_id, customer_id, purpose, channel, status, source, notice_version, captured_at, withdrawn_at, evidence_reference)`
- `customer_events(id, tenant_id, customer_id nullable, anonymous_session_id nullable, event_type, source, source_event_id, occurred_at, data_minimized_json)`
- `customer_metrics(tenant_id, customer_id, last_purchase_at, eligible_purchase_count, monetary_value_minor, r_score, f_score, m_score, segment_key, calculated_at)`
- `segment_definitions(tenant_id, key, rules_json, version, active)`
- `customer_merge_audit(tenant_id, from_customer_id, to_customer_id, actor_id, rationale, timestamp)`

Canonical purchase events point to order/sale records. Avoid duplicating raw order data into a CRM JSON blob.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/07-module-crm.md: 4. Identity resolution
nodes.description:
## 4. Identity resolution

Priority levels:
1. Authenticated account/customer ID within tenant.
2. Verified phone/email explicitly linked by customer or staff using a verification step.
3. Provider's stable customer ID if the provider and tenant account scope it reliably.
4. Anonymous transaction when no identity exists.

Never fuzzy-merge by name alone. Phone/email may be shared among family members. Provide review queue for suspected duplicate profiles. Unmerge must preserve original transactions and audit trail.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/07-module-crm.md: 5. RFM and lifecycle definitions
nodes.description:
## 5. RFM and lifecycle definitions

- Recency = days since latest eligible purchase.
- Frequency = distinct completed/refunded-adjusted eligible purchases in configured window.
- Monetary = eligible net spend in CLP in configured window.
- Scores use tenant-configured percentile or simple bands; store calculation version and timestamp.
- Exclude failed/cancelled transactions and apply refund/discount/tax policy consistently.
- Scheduled hourly/daily refresh is sufficient for MVP. Don't run heavy segmentation on every checkout.
- “At risk”/“inactive” are operational labels, not factual claims about a person. Allow tenant configuration and clear thresholds.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/07-module-crm.md: 6. Source collection paths
nodes.description:
## 6. Source collection paths

- Platform pickup order: emit confirmed/completed order events; anonymous unless customer identity was supplied and linked.
- POS: import sales with external IDs and reconciliation state; sales can remain anonymous.
- WhatsApp: store only necessary customer channel identifier and conversation/order metadata; conversation body retention is configurable and minimized.
- Loyalty: link account ID to customer after a supported identification step.
- Catering: business lead/contact record can remain separate from a customer record until consent/identity linking is appropriate.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/07-module-crm.md: 7. Privacy and marketing safety
nodes.description:
## 7. Privacy and marketing safety

Operational order messages and marketing campaigns have distinct purposes. Track consent per purpose and channel; default marketing opt-in to false unless a valid documented basis is confirmed by Chilean legal advice. Consent withdrawal must propagate to scheduled/sent campaign suppression. Data export/deletion/rectification requests need an auditable workflow and lawful-retention review. No purchased/inferred sensitive attributes.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/07-module-crm.md: 8. Reporting UX
nodes.description:
## 8. Reporting UX

Show counts, sample audience and rule summary before segment activation. Use small explainable segments initially. Exports require `crm.export` permission and audit; mask identifiers where feasible. Display data freshness and sources for every metric. If POS import is disconnected, mark metrics partial rather than silently showing complete customer history.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/07-module-crm.md: 9. APIs/jobs
nodes.description:
## 9. APIs/jobs

- Customer CRUD/link/unlink endpoints under tenant context.
- `POST /api/v1/crm/segments/preview` returns counts and explainable matched rules.
- `POST /api/v1/crm/segments` saves versioned definition.
- Scheduled job recomputes derived RFM metrics.
- Event consumers update aggregates idempotently.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/08-module-whatsapp.md
nodes.description: # Module Specification — WhatsApp Conversations, Ordering & Campaigns

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/08-module-whatsapp.md: Module Specification — WhatsApp Conversations, Ordering & Campaigns
nodes.description: # Module Specification — WhatsApp Conversations, Ordering & Campaigns
nodes.norm_label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/08-module-whatsapp.md: module specification — whatsapp conversations, ordering & campaigns

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/08-module-whatsapp.md: 1. Product contract
nodes.description:
## 1. Product contract

**Commercial module:** `whatsapp` (possible separately priced sub-capabilities: `whatsapp-support`, `whatsapp-ordering`, `whatsapp-campaigns`).  
**Purpose:** Use WhatsApp as a channel for support, ordering, event leads and permissioned outbound communication. WhatsApp ordering must function without QR menu and without the CRM campaign module. CRM segments enrich targeting only when CRM is active.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/08-module-whatsapp.md: 10. Acceptance criteria
nodes.description:
## 10. Acceptance criteria

- Webhook retries do not duplicate messages or orders.
- Opt-out suppresses subsequent campaign messages across all scheduled jobs.
- AI cannot change price or mark payment as complete.
- Outbound campaigns cannot be sent without a preview/approval step.
- WhatsApp ordering can place an order with QR module disabled.
- Provider outage creates visible delayed/failed state and replay path.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/08-module-whatsapp.md: 2. Integration rule
nodes.description:
## 2. Integration rule

Use the official WhatsApp Business Platform/Cloud API directly or a provider that is explicitly authorized and has acceptable Chile coverage/pricing. Do not automate consumer WhatsApp Web. Pricing, templates, message windows, opt-in and category rules change; verify current official Meta docs and provider-specific fees before commercial release. Make the adapter provider-independent.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/08-module-whatsapp.md: 3. MVP scope (deterministic before AI)
nodes.description:
## 3. MVP scope (deterministic before AI)

- Connect/verify business phone and configure approved templates.
- Receive inbound message webhooks and respond using deterministic menu/FAQ/order flows.
- Capture catering inquiry and send confirmation.
- Create a cart/order through the shared order domain service.
- Generate a hosted payment link for an order where online payment is configured.
- Opt-in/opt-out/suppression management.
- Campaign audience preview, scheduled send and delivery/failure report only after campaign module and required consent rules are validated.

AI phase: intent classification, FAQ answer draft from restaurant-approved sources, guided menu recommendation. AI must not invent stock/price/pickup estimates, confirm payment or autonomously apply unapproved discounts. All tools that alter state require server-side authorization and deterministic validation.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/08-module-whatsapp.md: 4. Data model
nodes.description:
## 4. Data model

- `messaging_connections(tenant_id, provider, business_account_ref, phone_number_ref, credential_secret_id, status, capabilities_json)`
- `conversations(id, tenant_id, customer_id nullable, channel, external_conversation_id, state, assigned_user_id, last_message_at, retention_deadline)`
- `messages(id, tenant_id, conversation_id, provider_message_id, direction, message_type, template_key nullable, delivery_status, timestamp, minimized_content_ref nullable, error_code)`
- `conversation_states(conversation_id, state_key, state_json, version, expires_at)` for cart/flow state; do not use untrusted AI output as state authority.
- `campaigns`, `campaign_audiences`, `campaign_recipients`, `template_registry`, `suppression_entries`.
- `message_events` dedupes provider delivery/read/failure callbacks.

Keep free-text retention short and configured; do not retain full transcripts indefinitely by default.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/08-module-whatsapp.md: 5. Order conversation state machine
nodes.description:
## 5. Order conversation state machine

`idle -> browsing -> cart_open -> awaiting_customer_confirmation -> order_created -> awaiting_payment (optional) -> paid/accepted -> complete`; exception states include `expired`, `cancelled`, `human_handoff`, `provider_failure`.

The flow must confirm order items, quantities, modifiers, branch, pickup time and total in user-facing language before creating a durable order. Reuse the same order service as web pickup. Use idempotency keys per conversation action so provider retries cannot create duplicates.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/08-module-whatsapp.md: 6. Payment link flow
nodes.description:
## 6. Payment link flow

- Backend creates an order/payment attempt and asks chosen payment adapter for hosted checkout URL.
- Message contains a time-limited or provider-valid link and clear order reference.
- Browser returning to WhatsApp or clicking a “paid” button never marks transaction paid.
- Provider webhook/verified query updates internal payment state.
- Send receipt/status message only after verified event.
- Expire/reconcile stale links and prevent multiple live attempts from being applied to the same order unless policy allows.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/08-module-whatsapp.md: 7. Outbound campaign workflow
nodes.description:
## 7. Outbound campaign workflow

1. User chooses a consent-safe segment or imports an eligible list.
2. System previews audience size and exclusion reasons.
3. Apply tenant timezone, quiet hours, frequency caps, do-not-contact, opt-outs, provider constraints and approved template rules.
4. Display estimated provider charges based on current configured rate table where available; do not guarantee cost until actual provider pricing is confirmed.
5. Require explicit approval before send.
6. Send in rate-limited batches with retries only where safe.
7. Process delivery/failure/opt-out webhooks; update suppression promptly.
8. Report sends, deliveries, failures, responses, order/lead attribution where lawful and measurable.

Do not import contacts or message people without an appropriate legal basis/consent. Do not bypass template approval or messaging windows.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/08-module-whatsapp.md: 8. AI behavior and guardrails
nodes.description:
## 8. AI behavior and guardrails

- Approved knowledge: restaurant FAQs, opening hours, policy, current published menu, pickup rules and approved catering packages.
- Use structured tool calls for catalog lookup, quote draft and order creation; validate every argument server-side.
- Never allow an LLM to construct arbitrary provider API requests or access other tenants.
- Treat user messages as untrusted input; tool permissions are narrow and tenant-scoped.
- Handoff to a person on ambiguity, complaint/refund, allergen uncertainty, failed payment, unsupported POS state or repeated failed turns.
- Display “assistant may make mistakes” only if useful; more importantly, operationally prevent unverified statements.
- Log tool/action outcome metadata, not unnecessary private transcript content.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/08-module-whatsapp.md: 9. Operational dashboard
nodes.description:
## 9. Operational dashboard

Connection status, template status, inbound/outbound volume, current conversation queue, human handoff, failed messages, opt-outs, estimated costs, and test-message function. API errors must not expose access tokens.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/17-testing-and-acceptance.md
nodes.description: # Testing Strategy & Definition of Done

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/17-testing-and-acceptance.md: Testing Strategy & Definition of Done
nodes.description: # Testing Strategy & Definition of Done

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/17-testing-and-acceptance.md: 1. Test layers
nodes.description:
## 1. Test layers

1. **Unit/domain tests:** state machines, pricing, CLP calculations, point rules, RFM and entitlement resolution.
2. **Database integration tests:** transactions, constraints, locking, tenant filters, outbox/inbox and migrations against real PostgreSQL in CI.
3. **Provider contract tests:** sandbox/fake server schemas and normalized status mapping. Keep sanitized fixtures with provider permission; never commit real secrets or customer data.
4. **End-to-end tests:** Playwright across public/customer, owner admin, kitchen and module activation flows.
5. **Operational tests:** webhook replay, worker retry, rate-limit response, backup restoration, credential rotation and provider outage.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/17-testing-and-acceptance.md: 2. MVP critical scenarios
nodes.description: ## 2. MVP critical scenarios

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/17-testing-and-acceptance.md: 3. Definition of Done for a ticket
nodes.description:
## 3. Definition of Done for a ticket

- Acceptance criteria implemented and tests added.
- API/schema/docs updated.
- Tenant and permission boundary verified.
- Loading, empty, error, retry and success UI states included.
- Logs and metrics include correlation/request IDs without secrets/PII leakage.
- Migration is safe for rolling deploy or explicitly coordinated.
- Disabled-module behavior is handled.
- New provider capability is documented in capability matrix.
- Spanish (Chile) user-facing copy reviewed.
- No secret, real customer data or card data committed.
nodes.norm_label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/17-testing-and-acceptance.md: 3. definition of done for a ticket

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/17-testing-and-acceptance.md: 4. Definition of Done for a module
nodes.description:
## 4. Definition of Done for a module

- Can be enabled independently with documented prerequisites.
- Has own onboarding checklist, health state, operational runbook and success metric.
- Has at least one full end-to-end test.
- Its critical domain operation is idempotent and audited.
- Has privacy/retention behavior and permission matrix.
- Clear manual fallback for provider outages.
- Tested when adjacent commercial modules are disabled.
nodes.norm_label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/17-testing-and-acceptance.md: 4. definition of done for a module

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/17-testing-and-acceptance.md: Catering
nodes.description:
### Catering
- Quote uses deterministic total and stored rule version.
- Pricing update does not alter prior quote.
- PDF failure is visible and allows retry/manual fallback.
- Date is not called reserved unless the availability workflow explicitly confirms it.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/17-testing-and-acceptance.md: Loyalty
nodes.description:
### Loyalty
- Concurrent redemption cannot overspend.
- Same eligible sale earns only once per rule version.
- Refund creates reversal.
- Google Wallet API failure leaves ledger intact and retries pass update.
- Staff adjustment requires permission and reason.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/17-testing-and-acceptance.md: Orders/payments
nodes.description:
### Orders/payments
- Duplicate checkout request produces one order.
- Price tampering/modifier injection does not change server total.
- Concurrent pickup requests cannot exceed slot capacity.
- Payment return redirect without verified provider success leaves payment pending.
- Duplicate/late/out-of-order provider events do not double process.
- Provider timeout after create triggers status lookup/reconciliation, not blind duplicate order creation.
- Refund/reversal preserves original event/audit.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/17-testing-and-acceptance.md: POS
nodes.description:
### POS
- Product mapping/unknown product surfaced before order send.
- API 429 respects provider rate limit and backoff.
- Token expiry prompts reconnection/refresh safely.
- Duplicate webhook/sale import creates one canonical record.
- Provider sale total and normalized totals can be reconciled.
- Order submit timeout has a manual recovery path; no silent retry duplicates.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/17-testing-and-acceptance.md: Platform/entitlements
nodes.description:
### Platform/entitlements
- Tenant A cannot read/update Tenant B's data even if IDs are known.
- Pickup enabled, QR disabled: storefront and orders work.
- Catering enabled alone: quote page and leads work.
- Disabled module API returns controlled `FORBIDDEN/FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED`; no data mutation.
- User branch scope enforced at API.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/17-testing-and-acceptance.md: WhatsApp/CRM/privacy
nodes.description:
### WhatsApp/CRM/privacy
- Opt-out after schedule but before send blocks message.
- Duplicate provider webhook does not duplicate order/message state.
- AI suggestion cannot set price/paid state or access another tenant.
- Customer with no consent not included in marketing campaign.
- Anonymous sale stays anonymous.

No real provider acceptance claimed. GitHub API updates blocked, pending evidence retained locally.
