nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/04-module-qr-menu.md
nodes.description: # Module Specification — QR Digital Menu

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/04-module-qr-menu.md: Module Specification — QR Digital Menu
nodes.description: # Module Specification — QR Digital Menu

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/04-module-qr-menu.md: 1. Product contract
nodes.description:
## 1. Product contract

**Commercial module:** `qr-menu`  
**Purpose:** A fast, mobile-responsive public menu accessed through restaurant/table QR codes. It is optional and must never be a dependency for pickup, WhatsApp ordering, CRM, loyalty or catering.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/04-module-qr-menu.md: 2. MVP scope
nodes.description:
## 2. MVP scope

- Publish menu by branch with categories, products, descriptions, images, CLP price, modifiers/add-ons, availability and optional allergen notes maintained by staff.
- Mobile-first public page with category navigation and restaurant branding.
- Stable QR URL per branch, optional table-specific URL if product design validates dine-in use.
- Preview/publish/unpublish and scheduled availability.
- CDN cache/invalidation for published public data.
- Analytics limited to page/menu views and click metrics without invasive tracking.

Out of scope: payment/order capture unless `pickup-ordering` is separately enabled; table service workflow; complex inventory; AI-generated nutrition/allergen facts.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/04-module-qr-menu.md: 3. Domain model
nodes.description:
## 3. Domain model

- `catalogs(id, tenant_id, branch_id, status, version, published_at)`
- `menu_categories(id, tenant_id, catalog_id, name, sort_order, active)`
- `menu_items(id, tenant_id, catalog_id, category_id, source, external_product_id, name, description, price_minor, currency, active, availability_json)`
- `modifier_groups` and `modifier_options` with min/max selection and price delta
- `menu_item_images(object_key, alt_text, sort_order)`
- `public_slugs(tenant_id, branch_id, slug, active)`
- `table_qr_codes(id, tenant_id, branch_id, table_label, slug_or_token, status)` if validated as necessary

Published items are read-only snapshots to the public storefront. Editing creates a draft/version and requires publish. Price/availability must be evaluated server-side when forming a cart.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/04-module-qr-menu.md: 4. Public routes
nodes.description:
## 4. Public routes

- `GET /r/:restaurantSlug/:branchSlug/menu` — published catalog.
- `GET /r/:restaurantSlug/:branchSlug` — branded entry point.
- Optional `GET /r/:restaurantSlug/:branchSlug/t/:tableCode` — table context, no secret data.
- Admin: catalog CRUD, reorder, availability updates, preview, publish.

Do not expose internal IDs or connection metadata. Use stable slug or random non-sensitive QR token. QR tokens can be revoked/rotated.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/04-module-qr-menu.md: 5. UX
nodes.description:
## 5. UX

- Menu landing page: branding, opening/availability information, categories, menu items.
- Item detail: modifiers, description and selected allergens/restaurant notes.
- Unavailable products should remain visible only if restaurant chooses “show unavailable”; they must not be added to cart.
- QR scan should arrive directly at the menu without requiring account creation.
- If pickup ordering is not purchased, no fake or nonfunctional cart/checkout button may appear. Optional CTA can link to telephone/reservation only if configured.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/04-module-qr-menu.md: 6. Data and integration behavior
nodes.description:
## 6. Data and integration behavior

- Catalog may be authored locally or imported from a POS adapter. Store `source` and external IDs.
- POS-sourced prices should show last successful sync and import conflict warnings. The restaurant must define whether POS or local catalog wins for price/availability.
- Catalog updates publish a `catalog.published.v1` event; CDN cache invalidation should be asynchronous and retryable.
- Do not let an integration failure unpublish the latest working menu without an explicit policy.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/04-module-qr-menu.md: 7. Acceptance criteria
nodes.description:
## 7. Acceptance criteria

- QR menu works when all other commercial modules are disabled.
- Pickup ordering still operates if QR module is disabled.
- Published menu is mobile responsive, accessible and cached safely.
- A staff member can update availability without developer help.
- Stale POS sync shows a warning but does not corrupt manual entries.
- No client-side submitted price is trusted by a downstream order module.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/04-module-qr-menu.md: Optional integrations
nodes.description:
### Optional integrations
- Pickup cart/order service (only if restaurant has pickup ordering entitlement)
- Loyalty sign-in/reward display (only if loyalty is active and policy allows)
- Analytics events

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/04-module-qr-menu.md: Required capabilities
nodes.description:
### Required capabilities
- `catalog.read_published`
- `public_storefront`
- tenant/branch branding and public slug

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/09-module-catering.md
nodes.description: # Module Specification — Catering & Private Event Estimator

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/09-module-catering.md: Module Specification — Catering & Private Event Estimator
nodes.description: # Module Specification — Catering & Private Event Estimator
nodes.norm_label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/09-module-catering.md: module specification — catering & private event estimator

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/09-module-catering.md: 1. Product contract
nodes.description:
## 1. Product contract

**Commercial module:** `catering`  
**Purpose:** Self-service lead and quote flow for private dining, group bookings and corporate catering. It must function without QR menu, pickup ordering, loyalty or CRM campaigns.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/09-module-catering.md: 2. MVP customer journey
nodes.description:
## 2. MVP customer journey

1. Customer opens standalone restaurant-branded catering page.
2. Enters event type, date, start/end time, estimated guest count, location, service format and contact details.
3. Selects a configured package (e.g. Standard, Premium, Cocktail, Open Bar if applicable) and add-ons.
4. Sees an indicative estimate with assumptions and exclusions; if configured as a formal quote, owner-approved terms and validity appear.
5. Submits request; create a lead and quote version.
6. Generate PDF and send email or WhatsApp link after the contact-channel/provider is configured.
7. Owner/staff reviews, edits, approves, sends revised quote, records acceptance/rejection/expiry and follows up.

The calculator must clearly distinguish an indicative estimate from a binding offer. Legal/financial terms and tax behavior require local review.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/09-module-catering.md: 3. Pricing engine
docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/09-module-catering.md: 4. Data model
nodes.description:
## 4. Data model

- `event_leads(id, tenant_id, branch_id nullable, source, customer_id nullable, contact_name, contact_method, contact_value, consent_to_follow_up, event_type, event_date, start_at, end_at, guest_count, venue_location, requirements, status, assigned_user_id)`
- `catering_packages(id, tenant_id, name, description, active, version)`
- `catering_price_rules(id, tenant_id, package_id, version, rules_json, effective_from, effective_to, approved_by)`
- `quotes(id, tenant_id, lead_id, quote_number, version, status, currency, total_minor, valid_until, terms_snapshot, pricing_snapshot_json, created_by, approved_by, pdf_object_key)`
- `quote_items` immutable lines; `quote_events` status audit.

Lead should exist independently of CRM. If CRM is active, optional identity linking can occur using consent/matching rules; don't require CRM purchase to create a catering lead.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/09-module-catering.md: 5. Statuses
nodes.description:
## 5. Statuses

Lead: `new -> qualifying -> quoted -> negotiating -> won/lost`; separate operational status from quote status.  
Quote: `draft -> approved -> sent -> viewed (if supported) -> accepted/rejected/expired/superseded`. Acceptance action needs authenticated secure link or owner confirmation; email opens alone do not prove acceptance.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/09-module-catering.md: 6. PDF/communications
nodes.description:
## 6. PDF/communications

- Generate PDF server-side in worker; store private object, use expiring signed URL when necessary.
- Include restaurant name/contact, quote number/version, event assumptions, itemized quantities/rates/totals, explicit exclusions, validity, payment/deposit terms and status.
- Use Spanish (Chile) and CLP formatting.
- Email/WhatsApp delivery is asynchronous; document the send result and retry state.
- If provider is unavailable, allow owner to download PDF and send manually.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/09-module-catering.md: 7. Admin screens
nodes.description:
## 7. Admin screens

- Leads inbox with filters by event date, guest count, status and source.
- Lead detail and activity timeline.
- Package editor with preview and effective-date/versioning.
- Quote builder with live deterministic total and explicit warnings for missing/overridden pricing.
- Approval step for discounts beyond tenant thresholds.
- Quote history and download/send/revise actions.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/09-module-catering.md: 8. Capacity and feasibility
nodes.description:
## 8. Capacity and feasibility

MVP may accept a request without reserving actual venue capacity. If calendar/booking availability is not integrated, state “request submitted; date is not confirmed.” Do not promise availability based only on a quote calculator. Add availability/reservation workflows later if paid demand proves it.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/09-module-catering.md: 9. Acceptance criteria
nodes.description:
## 9. Acceptance criteria

- Quote total is reproducible from stored snapshot.
- Editing package prices does not change previous quotes.
- PDF generation/send failure remains visible with manual download fallback.
- Catering works when CRM, QR, loyalty, WhatsApp and pickup modules are disabled; email fallback/manual review may be used.
- Customer consent and retention behavior is recorded.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/13-deployment-and-operations.md
nodes.description: # Deployment, Environments & Operations

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/13-deployment-and-operations.md: Deployment, Environments & Operations
nodes.description: # Deployment, Environments & Operations

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/13-deployment-and-operations.md: 1. Initial provider/region recommendation
nodes.description:
## 1. Initial provider/region recommendation

Use Google Cloud as the initial managed deployment baseline because the official location documentation lists both Cloud Run and Cloud SQL PostgreSQL in `southamerica-west1` (Santiago). Keep frontend/API/worker/database in the same region to reduce latency and cross-region charges. Use Cloudflare for DNS/CDN/WAF if its plan and configuration are appropriate; cache only public static assets/menu responses.

References: [Cloud Run locations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/locations), [Cloud SQL PostgreSQL region availability](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/region-availability-overview). AWS announced a Chile region planned for end of 2026; verify launch and service availability before considering it a current production option: <https://aws.amazon.com/es/local/chile/>.

This is a deployment baseline, not a contractual data residency guarantee. Verify region for every ancillary service, backups, logs and subprocessors.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/13-deployment-and-operations.md: 2. Environments
nodes.description:
## 2. Environments

- `local`: Docker Compose PostgreSQL, seeded synthetic test data, local object storage emulator optional.
- `dev`: shared development cloud environment, no real customer data/production credentials.
- `staging`: provider sandbox credentials, migration rehearsal, limited access, realistic synthetic fixtures.
- `production`: separate project/service accounts/secrets, backups and alerting enabled.

Never copy production customer data into dev/staging without formal anonymization and approval.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/13-deployment-and-operations.md: 3. Runtime services
nodes.description:
## 3. Runtime services

Start with three Cloud Run services (web, API, worker) and managed Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL. If the first MVP is particularly small, web/API can share deployment temporarily, but keep code packages separated so splitting is easy. Cloud Run may scale to zero; verify SSE connection behavior, min instances and timeouts before relying on it for a kitchen screen. SSE reconnect/polling is mandatory.

Worker must have constrained concurrency/max instances. Set DB connection limits and use Cloud SQL connector/pooling where supported; prevent autoscaling from exhausting PostgreSQL connections. `pg-boss` uses DB persistence, so monitor queue depth and queue-table growth.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/13-deployment-and-operations.md: 4. Infrastructure-as-code and deploy
nodes.description:
## 4. Infrastructure-as-code and deploy

- Use Terraform or Google Cloud deployment configuration checked into repository. Do not manually click-provision production resources without capturing configuration.
- CI: lint/typecheck -> unit -> integration tests -> migration validation -> build -> container scan -> deploy staging -> smoke/E2E -> manual approval -> production rollout.
- Migrations run once as a controlled release job before/with backward-compatible code deployment. Use expand/contract: add nullable fields/tables, deploy compatible code, backfill, then constrain/remove later.
- Every deploy has commit SHA, build metadata and rollback/forward-fix plan.
- Don't automatically run destructive migrations on every horizontally scaled app instance.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/13-deployment-and-operations.md: 5. Data protection / backup
nodes.description:
## 5. Data protection / backup

- Managed PostgreSQL automated backups and point-in-time recovery if available in chosen tier.
- Define target RPO/RTO in plain terms; for first paying restaurant, a documented recovery process matters more than an enterprise promise.
- Monthly restore test initially, then increase cadence when revenue/dependency warrants.
- Store PDFs/menu assets separately with lifecycle policies; database backup alone does not preserve object content.
- Retain secrets/rotation references separately from database backups.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/13-deployment-and-operations.md: 6. Observability
nodes.description:
## 6. Observability

Metrics:
- API latency/error by route/module/tenant (avoid PII labels).
- order creation, payment pending duration, payment mismatch, order status lag.
- queue depth, retries, dead-letter jobs, worker age.
- POS sync lag/failures/429s per connection.
- WhatsApp send failure/opt-out rate.
- Wallet pass sync lag/errors.
- database CPU/storage/connections, slow queries and backup status.

Structured logs include `request_id`, `tenant_id` (non-PII), `branch_id`, module, provider, connection ID and correlation ID. Redact secrets and raw payload fields. Add health endpoints for liveness/readiness; readiness checks dependencies conservatively to avoid restart storms.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/13-deployment-and-operations.md: 7. Cost controls
nodes.description:
## 7. Cost controls

- Set Cloud Run min instances to zero initially unless kitchen reconnect/latency demonstrates a need.
- Configure maximum instances to protect database and provider quotas.
- Cache public menu content, optimize images and avoid unnecessary egress.
- Keep job retries bounded with backoff; alert instead of retrying forever.
- Cap LLM usage per tenant/module and require explicit model invocation.
- Meter paid WhatsApp/provider activity.
- Review per-tenant support hours as cost of service, not just cloud bill.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/13-deployment-and-operations.md: 8. Operations runbooks required before first production restaurant
nodes.description:
## 8. Operations runbooks required before first production restaurant

1. Payment pending/reconciliation mismatch.
2. POS credentials expired/rotated/provider down.
3. Duplicate/missing order after timeout.
4. Queue backlog/dead-letter replay.
5. Customer data export/delete request.
6. WhatsApp opt-out/credential outage.
7. Backup restore and incident response.
8. Roll back web/API and safely handle database migrations.
nodes.norm_label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/13-deployment-and-operations.md: 8. operations runbooks required before first production restaurant

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/13-deployment-and-operations.md: 9. Release gates
nodes.description:
## 9. Release gates

No production release until: backups active, restore procedure tested, secret rotation documented, provider sandbox tests pass, alerting routes to a human, tenant-isolation tests pass, privacy and terms reviewed, and owner has a manual fallback for critical operations.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/15-prebuild-customer-validation.md
nodes.description: # Pre-Build Customer Validation & First Restaurant Pilot

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/15-prebuild-customer-validation.md: Pre-Build Customer Validation & First Restaurant Pilot
nodes.description: # Pre-Build Customer Validation & First Restaurant Pilot
nodes.norm_label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/15-prebuild-customer-validation.md: pre-build customer validation & first restaurant pilot

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/15-prebuild-customer-validation.md: 1. Objective
nodes.description:
## 1. Objective

Secure the first design partner/customer **before building the whole platform**. Validate the problem, UI, data access and willingness to pay with realistic workflows. Use a concierge/manual backend where it is safe and clearly communicated.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/15-prebuild-customer-validation.md: 2. Recruitment plan
nodes.description:
## 2. Recruitment plan

Partner recruits 3–5 restaurants spanning relevant workflows. Prefer restaurants where partner already has trust and direct access to the owner/manager. Record POS used (version/plan), branches, current ordering channel, event/catering volume, loyalty process, payment provider and staff responsibilities.

Do not interview only friends who praise the idea. Ask for concrete recent examples and artifacts with permission: anonymized order reports, current menu, quote template, campaign process and how long tasks take.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/15-prebuild-customer-validation.md: 3. Interview guide
nodes.description:
## 3. Interview guide

Ask, don't pitch first:
1. Tell me about the last time online/pickup orders or event quotations created an operational problem.
2. What happens today, step by step? Who touches it and how long does each step take?
3. What errors/costs/revenue loss occurred in the last month?
4. What tools/POS/payment/messaging service do you already pay for?
5. What have you tried? Why did it fail or succeed?
6. Which part must be solved for you to pay? Which features are nice-to-have?
7. Who decides and what budget/source would pay?
8. What data/API access can you grant and what permissions/approval are needed?
9. If we delivered only this workflow in 2–4 weeks, what result would make it worth continuing?

Avoid asking “Do you like this idea?” as the main validation question.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/15-prebuild-customer-validation.md: 4. Prototype screens to make before code
nodes.description:
## 4. Prototype screens to make before code

Create a clickable design prototype in Figma (or equivalent) for the selected wedge plus shared shell:
- Business setup and branch details.
- Module-selection page showing price/prerequisites.
- Module-specific customer journey (order or catering quote or loyalty enrolment).
- Owner dashboard with setup checklist, status and error recovery.
- Integration connection/setup page with capability state.
- Empty, success, failure, loading and disconnected states.
- Staff/kitchen flow if part of chosen workflow.

Prototype the “physical menu/no QR” case explicitly: pickup link, WhatsApp link, POS/CRM data acquisition and catering must still work.
nodes.norm_label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/15-prebuild-customer-validation.md: 4. prototype screens to make before code

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/15-prebuild-customer-validation.md: 5. Prototype feedback test
docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/15-prebuild-customer-validation.md: 6. Pilot agreement checklist
docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/15-prebuild-customer-validation.md: 7. Concierge pilot options
docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/15-prebuild-customer-validation.md: 8. Pilot success and stop conditions
docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/15-prebuild-customer-validation.md: 9. Conversion to paid production
nodes.description:
## 9. Conversion to paid production

At pilot end, present baseline vs result, costs/support effort, remaining gaps and specific paid tier proposal. Ask for a paid continuation/letter of intent before adding advanced automation. Use the owner's requested next module as a second-module validation test.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/03-design-system-and-frontend.md
nodes.description: # Shared Design System & Frontend Standards

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/03-design-system-and-frontend.md: Shared Design System & Frontend Standards
nodes.description: # Shared Design System & Frontend Standards

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/03-design-system-and-frontend.md: 1. Product feel
nodes.description:
## 1. Product feel

Aim for professional, calm, trustworthy restaurant software: warm-neutral surfaces, clear typography, a single brand accent, restrained status colors, strong hierarchy and high legibility in kitchens. Avoid making the admin dashboard look like a developer console. Public-facing menus can inherit restaurant branding while retaining accessible component behavior.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/03-design-system-and-frontend.md: 2. Shared frontend stack
nodes.description:
## 2. Shared frontend stack

- Next.js App Router + React + TypeScript.
- Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui (Radix primitives) maintained inside `packages/ui`.
- Icons: Lucide React.
- Forms: React Hook Form + Zod.
- Data fetching/cache: TanStack Query for interactive authenticated screens; use server rendering/static caching where suitable for public menu pages.
- API client generated from OpenAPI or typed from shared contracts; no ad-hoc `fetch` calls scattered across modules.
- Playwright for design-critical flows on mobile and desktop.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/03-design-system-and-frontend.md: 3. Tokens
nodes.description:
## 3. Tokens

Define semantic tokens, not component-specific hex values:

- `--background`, `--surface`, `--surface-raised`, `--foreground`, `--muted-foreground`, `--border`, `--primary`, `--primary-foreground`, `--secondary`, `--destructive`, `--warning`, `--success`, `--focus-ring`.
- Status must include text/icon and not rely on color alone.
- Tenant brand customization may override approved accent/logo/image tokens only. Do not allow tenants to override accessibility tokens or arbitrary CSS.
- Theme is light-first; dark mode is optional admin setting later, not a first-launch requirement.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/03-design-system-and-frontend.md: 4. Layout patterns
nodes.description:
## 4. Layout patterns

- Admin shell: left navigation, top branch selector, page title + primary action, main content, contextual side panel only where useful.
- Public catalog: brand header, category anchor list, search/filter if catalog warrants it, product cards, fixed cart action for pickup ordering.
- Kitchen: status columns or lanes, high contrast, large touch targets, explicit reconnect/last-updated state.
- Wizard forms: step indicator, clear required/optional fields, save/resume where user investment is significant.
- Empty states always explain why empty and offer the next useful action.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/03-design-system-and-frontend.md: 5. Localization for Chile
nodes.description:
## 5. Localization for Chile

- Spanish-Chile copy review by native/local partner. Avoid unreviewed machine-translated UX.
- CLP format with locale-aware `Intl.NumberFormat('es-CL', { style: 'currency', currency: 'CLP' })`; no decimal cents for ordinary CLP display unless provider transaction detail requires it.
- Store instants in UTC; display with `America/Santiago`; recurring schedules stored in local civil time plus IANA zone to handle daylight-saving changes.
- Phone collection: normalize to E.164; Chile numbers often `+56`; validate rather than assume.
- Dates: local Chilean format; distinguish pickup day/time and quote validity.
- Quantities use metric units; allergen/food labels editable by restaurant and not invented by AI.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/03-design-system-and-frontend.md: 6. Public menu performance
nodes.description:
## 6. Public menu performance

- Render a small critical path; lazy-load menu images; use modern image formats and responsive sizes.
- CDN-cache public published menu responses only with versioned keys/ETags and short invalidation path.
- Do not cache customer-specific order, loyalty or account data in shared edge caches.
- Ensure public QR slug is stable; QR content is a URL, not a serialized menu or secret token.
- Test on mid-range Android mobile and constrained network.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/03-design-system-and-frontend.md: 7. Frontend security
nodes.description:
## 7. Frontend security

- Treat all form values and query parameters as untrusted.
- Keep provider secrets exclusively server-side.
- Use secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookies for sessions when cookie auth is selected; CSRF defense for state-changing cookie-auth endpoints.
- Avoid dangerous HTML injection for menu descriptions; sanitize rich text.
- Use CSP, secure headers, dependency scanning and no secrets in client env variables.
- Hide/disable buttons based on permissions for UX, but always enforce server-side.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/03-design-system-and-frontend.md: 8. Frontend acceptance checklist
nodes.description:
## 8. Frontend acceptance checklist

- All primary flows usable at 360px width and on tablet landscape.
- Keyboard focus visible, labels accessible, loading/error/empty/success states included.
- No price, points balance or entitlement decision trusted from client state.
- Shared components are used consistently across modules and include interaction tests.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/12-security-privacy-chile.md
nodes.description:
# Security, Privacy & Chile Compliance Checklist

**Not legal advice.** Have Chilean counsel/accountant review actual data flows, controller/processor roles, contracts, tax treatment and marketing consent before production. This document turns known risk areas into engineering requirements.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/12-security-privacy-chile.md: Security, Privacy & Chile Compliance Checklist
nodes.description:
# Security, Privacy & Chile Compliance Checklist

**Not legal advice.** Have Chilean counsel/accountant review actual data flows, controller/processor roles, contracts, tax treatment and marketing consent before production. This document turns known risk areas into engineering requirements.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/12-security-privacy-chile.md: 1. Chile-specific timing
nodes.description:
## 1. Chile-specific timing

Chile Law 21.719 reforms the personal-data protection framework and establishes a Personal Data Protection Agency. The official consolidated-law source states its entry into force is **December 1, 2026**: <https://www.bcn.cl/leychile/Navegar?idNorma=1209272&idVersion=2026-12-01>. Since development and onboarding may overlap this date, design to the upcoming regime before first launch rather than retrofit later. Validate the law's final current text and implementing interpretation with Chilean counsel.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/12-security-privacy-chile.md: 2. Data inventory and purposes
docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/12-security-privacy-chile.md: 3. Consent and suppression
nodes.description:
## 3. Consent and suppression

- Consent is a first-class append-only record: purpose, channel, status, text/notice version, capture source/time, evidence and withdrawal time.
- Marketing consent defaults to false unless legal/product validation establishes an appropriate basis.
- Unsubscribe/opt-out applies immediately to unsent scheduled messages and all future campaigns for that purpose/channel.
- Do not let CRM segment membership override suppression.
- Store proof of consent/withdrawal in a minimal auditable record.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/12-security-privacy-chile.md: 4. Data minimization
nodes.description:
## 4. Data minimization

- Anonymous POS transactions are valid financial/aggregate events; don't create fake customer records.
- Customer identity linking must use verified/explicit signals, not name-only fuzzy match.
- Avoid storing complete WhatsApp text forever; configure retention and allow operational access only when needed.
- Do not store cardholder data or sensitive payment details.
- Loyalty barcode contains an opaque token, not phone/email/balance.
- Logs never include API secrets, access tokens, full message bodies by default, or unnecessary PII.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/12-security-privacy-chile.md: 5. Customer rights and lifecycle
nodes.description:
## 5. Customer rights and lifecycle

Build admin workflow for access/export, correction, deletion/erasure where applicable, restriction/withdrawal, and request audit. Deleting a customer profile must not silently delete legally required financial/transaction records; separate identity from financial record and pseudonymize/anonymize where legally appropriate. Establish tenant support SLA and escalation process with counsel.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/12-security-privacy-chile.md: 6. Security controls
nodes.description:
## 6. Security controls

- TLS for all endpoints, encryption at rest through cloud provider, least-privilege service identities.
- Secrets in Secret Manager, not `.env` in repository; local dev `.env.example` contains placeholders only.
- Separate production and staging service accounts/secrets/projects.
- Role and tenant/branch checks on every API; automated cross-tenant isolation tests.
- Secure sessions, MFA for owners if supported by auth solution, rate limits and account lockout protection.
- Webhook signatures/authentication where provider supports it; replay/deduplication defenses.
- Immutable audit of role changes, integration credential changes, manual loyalty adjustment, refunds, exports and campaign approvals.
- Dependency and container scanning; regular backups and restore tests.
- Incident response runbook: isolate credentials, revoke/rotate, preserve audit evidence, assess notification duties with legal counsel.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/12-security-privacy-chile.md: 7. Chile operational/commercial checks
nodes.description:
## 7. Chile operational/commercial checks

- Determine whether platform or restaurant is controller for each flow and document processor terms.
- Review cross-border transfer rules and subprocessor contracts even if primary database is in Santiago; provider systems may process data elsewhere.
- Review WhatsApp/Meta terms and consent/opt-out requirements.
- Review Google Wallet issuer/program requirements.
- Verify SII electronic receipt/invoice requirements. Do not imply that Webpay/Mercado Pago payment confirmation emits a compliant boleta/factura; fiscal documents need a separate confirmed integration or manual process.
- Review consumer-facing pricing/cancellation/refund rules and restaurant-to-customer quote terms.
- Get written permission for POS data use and external integration from restaurant owner/provider.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/12-security-privacy-chile.md: 8. Security acceptance checklist
nodes.description:
## 8. Security acceptance checklist

- No secret in client bundle or logs.
- Cross-tenant queries fail closed in automated tests.
- Opt-out stops the next campaign worker before send.
- Data export and deletion request can be tracked to completion.
- Backups encrypted and a restore test recorded.
- Production error payloads do not reveal internal stack traces or provider credentials.
- Privacy notice and contracts are reviewed and versioned before public launch.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/14-billing-entitlements.md
nodes.description: # Modular Catalog, Subscription Billing & Entitlements

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/14-billing-entitlements.md: Modular Catalog, Subscription Billing & Entitlements
nodes.description: # Modular Catalog, Subscription Billing & Entitlements

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/14-billing-entitlements.md: 1. Goals
nodes.description:
## 1. Goals

A restaurant picks services independently (like a hosting provider buying separate hosting/email/marketing products). Each purchased module activates its routes, jobs and integration setup. Shared capabilities are platform infrastructure and are not automatically charged as separate modules. Pricing should be understandable before enablement and should scale with third-party costs.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/14-billing-entitlements.md: 2. Separate four concepts
nodes.description:
## 2. Separate four concepts

1. **Catalog:** what products/modules can be bought and their price/usage rules.
2. **Subscription:** what tenant has purchased, billing period/status and external subscription reference.
3. **Entitlements:** what the tenant can use right now, possibly during trial/grace period.
4. **Usage:** metered activity used for limits or overage charges.

A payment failure does not delete data or abruptly corrupt an ongoing order. Apply clear grace/suspension policies and preserve required data access/export.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/14-billing-entitlements.md: 3. Tables
nodes.description:
## 3. Tables

- `module_catalog(id, version, name, public_description, base_price_minor, currency, billing_period, usage_policy_json, required_capabilities_json, optional_integrations_json, active)`
- `tenant_subscriptions(id, tenant_id, status, provider, external_subscription_id, current_period_start, current_period_end, trial_end, grace_until, cancel_at_period_end)`
- `subscription_items(id, subscription_id, module_id, module_version, quantity, price_snapshot_minor, status)`
- `tenant_entitlements(tenant_id, entitlement_key, scope_type, scope_id, enabled, source_subscription_item_id, effective_from, effective_to)`
- `usage_records(id, tenant_id, module_id, usage_type, quantity, unit, idempotency_key, occurred_at, metadata_minimized)`
- `billing_events(provider, external_event_id, status, processed_at)`.

Store price snapshots so future price changes don't mutate prior invoices. Keep platform subscriptions separate from restaurant customer payments.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/14-billing-entitlements.md: 4. Dependency/activation flow
nodes.description:
## 4. Dependency/activation flow

1. Owner selects modules and sees clear monthly/annual pricing, usage allowance, provider fees excluded/included and any prerequisites.
2. Backend resolves required capabilities. If adding pickup requires order management/catalog, those are provisioned as shared capabilities but not shown as a separate commercial charge unless product strategy explicitly prices them.
3. Owner confirms selection and terms.
4. Create subscription or record pilot/manual billing status.
5. Activate entitlements transactionally and launch onboarding checklists.
6. Enable provider connection only when owner authorizes it; don't request integrations unrelated to purchased modules.
7. On cancellation, stop new billable activity according to policy; retain data for configured grace/export/retention; don't delete shared records still used by another active module.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/14-billing-entitlements.md: 5. Dependency graph
nodes.description:
## 5. Dependency graph

Example:
- `qr-menu -> catalog.read_published`
- `pickup-ordering -> catalog.read_orderable + order-management + pickup-slot-rules`
- `loyalty -> loyalty-ledger + customer-identity (minimal); Google Wallet optional`
- `crm -> customer-records + consent + event-aggregation`
- `whatsapp-ordering -> messaging + order-management`; payment adapter optional if pay-at-pickup is available
- `whatsapp-campaigns -> messaging + consent/suppression + audience source`; CRM segments optional, manual/list-based audience only if policy permits
- `catering -> quote-engine + lead-records + PDF`; email/WhatsApp delivery optional

Make the graph declarative and validated at startup/CI. Detect dependency cycles in tests.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/14-billing-entitlements.md: 6. Pricing model recommendation
nodes.description:
## 6. Pricing model recommendation

- Fixed monthly module charge for core workflow.
- Included usage allowance where it helps customers predict cost (e.g. outbound messages or AI calls); show current provider cost pass-through/overage rules transparently.
- Optional one-time onboarding fee for provider setup only if measured manual work justifies it; avoid bespoke price negotiations becoming the default.
- Multi-branch pricing is explicit: per tenant base + additional branch or usage-based tier, based on validated buyer willingness.
- Pilot may be free/discounted but must have defined duration, success metrics and conversion offer.

Avoid exposing every underlying technical capability as a separate invoice item. Do not subsidize unlimited WhatsApp/AI usage without caps.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/14-billing-entitlements.md: 7. Chile billing provider
nodes.description:
## 7. Chile billing provider

Evaluate Mercado Pago recurring/subscription capability for platform billing, subject to merchant eligibility, recurring payment support, cancellation rules and fees: <https://www.mercadopago.cl/developers/>. Manual invoicing/transfer may be enough for the first customer. Do not make automated platform billing a V1 blocker unless customer insists. Separately validate Chilean tax invoicing obligations with an accountant; provider payment receipt is not assumed to be an SII electronic fiscal document.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/14-billing-entitlements.md: 8. Acceptance criteria
nodes.description:
## 8. Acceptance criteria

- Owner can purchase pickup without QR and catering without CRM.
- A module entitlement cannot be self-enabled via client manipulation.
- Module cancellation doesn't erase shared data still needed by active modules.
- Usage events deduplicate and are auditable.
- Price and usage rules shown before the owner confirms.
- Subscription/payment provider webhook retries are idempotent.

nodes.label: docs/catalog-and-availability.md: Availability rules
nodes.description:
## Availability rules

Confirmation and first simulated payment/kitchen submission require `acceptingOrders`, `shiftOpen`, an allowed local service interval and a non-stale review. Browsing/cart review remain available while closed. Existing paid/preparing orders remain visible and can proceed to pickup. Real late-settlement/paid-but-closed handling remains #15/#17.

`maxAgeMinutes` is 1–10080; the default is 1440. A staff stock or shift toggle cannot make stale prices fresh. Only a reviewed catalog replacement refreshes `updatedAt`. All changes use the branch lock and transaction, so quote checks see a consistent catalog.

Hours use the branch timezone (`America/Santiago` initially), with weekday `0=Sunday` through `6=Saturday`, `HH:mm` opening/closing times, opening inclusive and closing exclusive. A closing time earlier than opening extends into the next day; equal times are rejected. No intervals explicitly means unrestricted hours for the demo/manual schedule, still subject to the open/accepting/review checks. Santiago daylight-saving changes are handled through `Intl.DateTimeFormat` timezone data.

nodes.label: docs/catalog-and-availability.md: Canonical file import
nodes.description:
## Canonical file import

`examples/catalog.sample.json` is a **simulation fixture**. Replace codes/content with the approved branch's authoritative mappings for an eventual pilot. Match `expectedVersion` to the current value from the panel or authenticated `GET /api/catalog`; otherwise the import fails. The `manualApproved: true` field is an explicit operator assertion that the menu has been reviewed, not proof of the separate restaurant sign-off.

For a trusted owner/developer workflow, set `DATABASE_URL` and `CATALOG_STAFF_TOKEN` privately in the environment (or ignored `.env`), then run:

```sh
npm run db:import-catalog -- examples/catalog.sample.json
```

The CLI uses the same authenticated transaction, owner permission check and domain validator as the API. Credentials do not go in command arguments or import files. Files are bounded to 128 KiB, and no file is uploaded to an external service. The command operates only on the token's branch; tenant/branch properties in the import are rejected.

Product IDs are customer-facing numeric codes `1`–`9999`; modifier IDs use lowercase ASCII letters/digits/underscore/hyphen and start with a letter. Every product/extra has Spanish and English names, nonnegative integer `price` in CLP, `available`, and optional `mappings` containing exact opaque `toteat`/`fudo` identifiers. Imported prices are bounded to CLP 1,000,000 per item/extra; order totals are bounded below the SQL integer limit. Fractional, negative, duplicate or unknown fields are rejected before mutation. An available manually imported selection without its selected POS mapping cannot be added to a cart or checked out. The other provider's mapping can be stored independently.

nodes.label: docs/catalog-and-availability.md: Customer selection and safe confirmation
nodes.description:
## Customer selection and safe confirmation

Customers use any listed numeric item code, for example `42 x 2`. Optional extras use `42+cheese x 2`; multiple extra codes can be joined with `+`. The selected codes appear in the menu and the same syntax works in Spanish/English. Quantity is 1–20 per distinct selection. `remove 42+cheese` / `quitar 42+cheese` removes that selection. Invalid, repeated, unsupported or unavailable extras do not mutate the cart. Menu display and confirmed snapshots include localized extra names and prices.

Each cart review persists a five-minute quote with catalog version, cart identity, exact line selections/provider mappings and total. A price, availability or mapping change, a changed cart, or expiry requires review of a fresh quote and another explicit confirmation before creating checkout. A silent direct price mutation is also detected by comparing the priced lines. Repeated confirmation recovers an already confirmed order and its immutable amount rather than repricing it.

The confirmed order retains the catalog version, provider product ID and selected modifier IDs/names/prices. PostgreSQL preserves these and the quote across requests/restarts. Historical order lines are not rewritten when the current catalog changes. This supplies the quote foundation for #8; its separated financial/fulfillment state machine and full event contracts remain outstanding.
nodes.norm_label: docs/catalog-and-availability.md: customer selection and safe confirmation

nodes.label: docs/catalog-and-availability.md: HTTP surface
nodes.description:
## HTTP surface

All routes use authenticated restaurant/branch scope and return Spanish/English errors using `Accept-Language`. Unknown body properties, including attempted tenant overrides, are rejected. Domain validation returns 400, stale-version/availability/selection conflicts return 409, and insufficient roles return 403.

| Route | Permission | Body |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /api/catalog` | owner/operator/viewer | None |
| `POST /api/catalog` | owner | Canonical import document |
| `POST /api/catalog/products/:id/availability` | owner/operator | `expectedVersion`, `available` |
| `POST /api/catalog/service` | owner/operator | `expectedVersion`, `acceptingOrders`, `shiftOpen` |

Migration `002_catalog_availability.sql` is additive. It persists review/version/source/availability on the branch, mappings/extras on products, quotes on conversations and selection snapshots on order lines. Existing seed menus and historical orders remain valid. All domain changes and audit entries commit or roll back together. Real provider ingestion, verified availability feeds and restaurant acceptance evidence remain explicit follow-up gates.

nodes.label: docs/catalog-and-availability.md: Implemented scope and provider gate
nodes.description:
## Implemented scope and provider gate

This change implements the catalog code that can be verified without restaurant accounts: product/modifier mappings for both POS providers, bilingual labels, integer CLP prices, versioned edits and quotes, service availability, manual import and staff correction controls. QR-menu entitlement remains disabled and is not a dependency.

**Issue #7 remains open for provider-account evidence and restaurant approval.** The canonical import format is our shared model; it is not a guessed Toteat or Fudo native payload. The real adapters in #13/#22 must transform authenticated provider data and verify mappings against the authorized restaurant accounts from #2. The example codes beginning `SIM-` are synthetic and must never be submitted to a live POS. Manual review by a staff token does not prove provider validation or kitchen acceptance.
nodes.norm_label: docs/catalog-and-availability.md: implemented scope and provider gate

nodes.label: docs/catalog-and-availability.md: Staff controls
nodes.description:
## Staff controls

Sign in, choose Spanish or English, and select **Load catalog / Cargar catálogo** below the order workspace. Owner/operator staff can pause/resume ordering, mark the shift closed/open and mark products sold out/available. Viewer accounts have read-only access. Shift status is explicitly staff-confirmed; no live POS shift feed is connected.

The owner can expand **Edit items, prices and hours** to change names, prices, POS codes, extras and local service hours. Native form constraints handle missing fields and price bounds; the server validates the complete document and permissions. The owner must confirm a manual review before saving. Saving refreshes the review timestamp and increments the branch catalog version. Stock/shift toggles increment the version but do not refresh stale menu prices. Unsaved owner edits must be saved or explicitly discarded before reloading or applying another operation.

Each update sends `expectedVersion`. Concurrent/stale edits receive a conflict and must reload; there is no silent overwrite. Missing products from a replacement are retained as unavailable rows for historical order references. The editor supports up to 200 stored products, five optional extras per item and 21 service intervals. Required/exclusive modifier groups are outside this POC; import only the optional extras the flow can express.

nodes.label: docs/architecture.md: Catalog and availability extension (#7)
nodes.description:
## Catalog and availability extension (#7)

The shared catalog now supports manual reviewed imports, product/modifier mappings for both providers, stock/shift/hours gates and persisted versioned quotes. See [catalog behavior and remaining provider gates](catalog-and-availability.md). Customer confirmation cannot silently accept a changed or expired quote. Verified provider ingestion remains #2/#13/#22; #7 stays open for its external acceptance evidence.

nodes.label: docs/architecture.md: Durable model to implement in M1/M2
nodes.description:
## Durable model to implement in M1/M2

Use PostgreSQL with tenant-scoped foreign keys and unique keys. Every query includes authenticated tenant and branch, derived from staff identity or mapped provider account, never from customer-supplied text. Verify isolation with negative tests; consider RLS as defense in depth once connection-pool context handling is designed.

| Entity | Important invariants |
| --- | --- |
| tenants / branches / memberships | Timezone, currency, role, entitlements and mapped provider phone IDs |
| products / modifiers / provider mappings | Authoritative provider IDs, availability, integer CLP prices and catalog version |
| conversations / carts / quotes | Tenant + sender; expiry; immutable displayed quote with catalog version |
| orders / order_lines | UUID, source=whatsapp, confirmed snapshot, tenant/branch, explicit operational state |
| payment_attempts / payment_events | Unique merchant reference and provider event ID, amount/currency, verified status, refund ledger |
| pos_submissions | External reference, provider reference, attempt/status and unknown-outcome marker |
| inbox / outbox / deliveries | Unique tenant + provider + event ID, claim lease, retry count, backoff and dead-letter reason |
| order_events / audit | Append-only state changes with actor and correlation ID; no raw secrets/messages |

Store UTC timestamps; derive restaurant-local dates using `America/Santiago`, including daylight-saving changes. Use CLP integer minor-unit convention verified for the gateway (CLP normally has no fractional price component); never floating-point prices or browser-submitted totals. Do not overload order status with financial state.
nodes.norm_label: docs/architecture.md: durable model to implement in m1/m2

nodes.label: docs/architecture.md: Observability and required verification
nodes.description:
## Observability and required verification

Log correlation IDs, order IDs, provider outcome class, latency and retry count. Exclude message bodies, customer identifiers, credentials and checkout URLs. Alert on paid-but-unaccepted backlog, dead letters, provider errors and stale status sync. Test duplicates/concurrency, restart recovery, tenant isolation, price changes, forged callbacks, mismatched payment amounts, unknown POS outcomes, refunds and local-date metrics. Keep automated tests small and focused on these failure boundaries.

nodes.label: docs/architecture.md: Payment and fulfillment contracts
nodes.description:
## Payment and fulfillment contracts

1. Price/availability/hours are checked and a quote displayed. On confirm, validate the quote/version and freeze line items. A changed price requires renewed customer confirmation.
2. Create or recover a checkout for that immutable order and merchant. Set an expiry and unique correlation reference.
3. An authenticated provider callback and/or authoritative status lookup verifies amount, currency, merchant, reference and settled/approved status. A browser redirect proves nothing about payment.
4. In one transaction, record the verified payment and enqueue a POS submission. The customer sees payment received while acceptance remains pending.
5. The POS adapter checks the shift/menu mappings and submits the paid pickup. Persist provider references and acceptance independently. Only confirmed kitchen acceptance changes fulfillment state.
6. Reconcile callbacks/polling and notify accepted/ready states under WhatsApp messaging rules. Staff confirms collection with audit.
7. A paid order that cannot be accepted enters `needs_attention`; a named operator resolves it or refunds. Reconcile payment/POS ledgers daily.

For timeouts: check by external reference before retrying. Provider idempotency must be demonstrated, not inferred from a local unique key. Without an authoritative lookup/idempotency guarantee, require staff reconciliation rather than risking a second kitchen order. Queue processing is at-least-once; application side effects must tolerate replay.

nodes.label: docs/architecture.md: PostgreSQL and access implementation (#6)
nodes.description:
## PostgreSQL and access implementation (#6)

Optional PostgreSQL mode now implements transactional restaurant/branch repositories, migrations/seed, scoped staff tokens/roles, durable sessions/orders/line snapshots/payment references, inbox/outbox and audit records. See [the storage and access design](postgres-storage.md) for setup, isolation guarantees, restart tests and limits. Asynchronous messaging workers, quote/version contracts and real-provider financial reconciliation remain separate issues.

nodes.label: docs/architecture.md: Regional deployment target
nodes.description:
## Regional deployment target

Use Google Cloud **Santiago (`southamerica-west1`)** for Cloud Run and Cloud SQL PostgreSQL. Cloud Run lists the region in its [location documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/locations); verify the required Cloud SQL edition, machine types, queue and other product availability/cost at deployment time. [Cloud SQL locations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sql/docs/postgres/locations) is the source of truth.

Deploy a web/ingress service and a worker from the same codebase; select managed durable queue execution after checking regional availability (#19). Database is private, secrets are stored in Secret Manager, and service identities have least privilege. Maintain staging/production separation, HTTPS, webhook access paths, restricted authenticated admin access, migration/rollback steps and backup restore evidence. Real provider API calls stay server-side. Static assets can be cached regionally later; tenant data must never be publicly CDN-cached.

No cloud resource is provisioned by this setup. The included Dockerfile runs the **simulation**, for local/staging demonstration only. Durable storage and real adapter modes must land before real payments. Webhook availability alone is not pilot readiness.

nodes.label: docs/architecture.md: Runtime boundaries
nodes.description:
## Runtime boundaries

Use one TypeScript modular monolith for a two-person team. The current server is Fastify on Node 24. Shared domain services own business decisions; transport handlers translate payloads. Both Toteat and Fudo are first-pilot adapters, configured separately per restaurant/branch, with the selected provider snapshotted on each order. A provider API does not define the application's domain model.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Customer[Customer WhatsApp] --> Meta[Meta Cloud API]
  Meta --> Ingress[Signature verification and tenant routing]
  Ingress --> Inbox[Durable inbox - M2]
  Inbox --> WA[WhatsApp module]
  WA --> Catalog[Shared catalog]
  WA --> Orders[Shared ordering and quotes]
  Orders --> Checkout[Payment adapter]
  Checkout --> Verified[Verified payment reconciliation]
  Verified --> Outbox[Transactional outbox - M1/M2]
  Outbox --> POS[POS adapter]
  POS --> Kitchen[Restaurant kitchen]
  POS --> Status[Status reconciliation]
  Status --> Dashboard[Authenticated pickup dashboard]
  Status --> Notify[WhatsApp notifications]
```

Only WhatsApp ordering is enabled for the demo tenant; QR is disabled. Future QR, web ordering and loyalty use shared services and events, never depend on an enabled WhatsApp service. Entitlement changes control access to services, not ownership/deletion of catalog or order data.

nodes.label: public/AGENTS.md
nodes.description:
# Browser dashboard and catalog UI

Native ES modules: `app.js` handles API auth, chat, dashboard, pickup actions and locale; `catalog-ui.js` exports `createCatalogPanel`; `i18n.js` contains browser copy; `index.html` and `style.css` define semantic layout and presentation. Graph seeds: `createCatalogPanel`, `renderDashboard`, `translatePage`, `api`.

Keep the bearer token in page memory, insert untrusted content as text and preserve same-origin requests and server CSP. Only language preference belongs in localStorage. Role-based controls improve UX; server authorization remains authoritative. Preserve Spanish/English copy, accessible names, document lang and locale-aware CLP/date formatting. Show simulation and local pickup states accurately; browser actions do not establish provider payment settlement.

Align API fields with `../src/app.ts` and domain services. New assets need the server's allowlist. `npm run check` checks browser syntax; `npm test` covers API contracts. Visually inspect changed flows with keyboard/mobile and both languages; no automated browser suite currently exists.

The PostgreSQL delivery panel shows only scoped counts and redacted exception metadata. Owners/operators explicitly acknowledge cause correction before retrying a known failure, or reviewed follow-up before resolving an uncertain outcome without resending. Preserve optimistic `expectedVersion`, server role enforcement and truthful provider-acceptance labels. Viewer controls are read-only. Clear exception data when credentials change; never render sender addresses, messages, provider identifiers or panel credentials. Refresh and language changes reset acknowledgements.

Receipt facts are independent: show provider acceptance separately from sent/delivered/read/failure events, without treating absent evidence as failed delivery. Label reply versus notification sources because their numeric IDs can overlap. `sandbox-ui.js` owns Webpay sandbox actions and its local-only test checkout link. Sandbox orders must bypass simulation-pay and pay-at-pickup controls. Keep test-authorized CLP totals separate from revenue, and label sandbox kitchen mode in both languages.

Help requests use explicit reviewed-without-contact acknowledgement, preserve server role enforcement and clear on credential changes. A review does not claim customer contact. Closed customer-service windows are labeled as staff follow-up rather than uncertain delivery.

nodes.label: README.md
nodes.description:
# Easy Eatery

Modular restaurant SaaS, starting with **WhatsApp pickup ordering for one restaurant in Chile**. Shared catalog and ordering capabilities do not require a QR-menu subscription.

This setup includes a runnable **Spanish-default and English demo**, an optional **PostgreSQL mode with individual staff access**, a test-account WhatsApp Cloud API transport, and **24 GitHub issues across five milestones**. Both **Toteat and Fudo** are required for the initial pilot. Payment and POS adapters remain **simulated**. Default memory mode resets on restart; PostgreSQL mode preserves restaurant data. The real-provider pilot is tracked in the backlog.

The first prospect-demo scope now allows **our own kitchen dashboard and pay at pickup**, with **Webpay sandbox checkout** planned independently of a restaurant POS. Local kitchen and pay-at-pickup mode are implemented; Webpay sandbox now has an opt-in staff-assisted flow with local mock coverage; actual hosted sandbox acceptance remains pending. See [live-demo setup and account handoff](docs/live-demo-onboarding.md) and [tracking issue #27](https://github.com/arkajyotiMukherjee/easy-eatery/issues/27).

# Staff-assisted Webpay sandbox checkout

This opt-in workflow uses the fixed Transbank integration endpoint and local kitchen fulfillment. It cannot use a production gateway or POS. Local mock tests cover the application flow; an actual hosted sandbox checkout has not passed because this cloud runtime denies the integration host. nodes.description:
# Staff-assisted Webpay sandbox checkout

This opt-in workflow uses the fixed Transbank integration endpoint and local kitchen fulfillment. It cannot use a production gateway or POS. nodes.label: README.md: Durable WhatsApp message processing
nodes.description:
## Durable WhatsApp message processing

PostgreSQL Cloud mode queues signed inbound messages before replying to Meta and processes them asynchronously. Start the normal server after applying migration 004; its worker runs automatically. No additional provider account is needed to test the worker with fixtures. Explicit provider rejections retry with bounded backoff; uncertain sends pause for review. Authenticated `GET /api/whatsapp/delivery` shows scoped queue counts. See [delivery and recovery boundaries](docs/postgres-storage.md#durable-whatsapp-extension-10). Real-phone testing still needs the approved sender/recipient and HTTPS webhook.

nodes.label: docs/webpay-sandbox.md: Enable only in an approved test environment
nodes.description:
## Enable only in an approved test environment

Use PostgreSQL and explicitly apply migrations through 008 using `npm run db:migrate`. Follow `postgres-storage.md` for a disposable development branch and individual staff tokens. Keep existing configuration and data. Do not seed or change a customer branch just to inspect this feature.

Set `WEBPAY_SANDBOX_ENABLED=true`, `WEBPAY_SANDBOX_COMMERCE_CODE`, `WEBPAY_SANDBOX_API_KEY` and `WEBPAY_SANDBOX_RETURN_URL` using secure environment settings. Use only authorized integration credentials, never production merchant credentials. The return URL must be an approved public HTTPS URL ending in `/sandbox/return`; no public tunnel or hosting is provisioned by this change. The outbound hostname is fixed to `webpay3gint.transbank.cl`. Missing configuration fails startup when the feature is enabled.

For the selected development branch, run:

```sh
node --import tsx --env-file-if-exists=.env scripts/database.ts sandbox-mode <tenant> <branch> true
npm start
```

This turns off pay at pickup for new orders in that branch. Existing confirmed orders keep their original method, prices and fulfillment. Disable sandbox mode with the same command ending in `false`; this does not convert existing orders to cash or cancel an uncertain payment.
nodes.norm_label: docs/webpay-sandbox.md: enable only in an approved test environment

nodes.label: docs/webpay-sandbox.md: Evidence and gates
nodes.description:
## Evidence and gates

`npm test` covers the transport against local mock HTTP responses. `npm run test:db` uses isolated schemas and a fake gateway for scoped access, duplicate/concurrent returns, a single kitchen ticket, restart/status reconciliation, stale leases, mismatched totals/merchant, expired links, owner reversal and unknown-outcome handling. These checks do not prove hosted checkout, a real card authorization, refund acceptance, settlement or restaurant sign-off. Actual sandbox/browser return testing needs approved HTTPS hosting and runtime network access; production merchant onboarding remains a separate gate.

nodes.label: docs/webpay-sandbox.md: Full test reversals and exceptions
nodes.description:
## Full test reversals and exceptions

An owner can explicitly reverse a full test authorization before collection. The server rechecks the current role, revision, immutable amount and prior reversal claim inside the branch transaction. An operator/viewer cannot reverse. The action is claimed before external I/O and is never automatically retried. Collection and readiness are blocked while the reversal needs review. Authoritative reversed/nullified evidence records `sandbox_reversed` while retaining the ticket and audit trail. Partial reversals and production refunds are unsupported.

If a reversal times out, an `AUTHORIZED` status by itself does not prove that reversal failed: the order remains `sandbox_review`, and another reversal is prohibited. Reconcile and use the approved provider support process. Never manually edit rows, fabricate success, restart a payment or switch to cash to clear the exception. Refunds after collection need a separate reviewed operational design.
nodes.norm_label: docs/webpay-sandbox.md: full test reversals and exceptions

nodes.label: README.md: HTTP surface
nodes.description:
## HTTP surface

All `/api/*` routes require `Authorization: Bearer <token>`: the local `ADMIN_TOKEN` in memory mode, or an active restaurant-scoped staff token in PostgreSQL mode. The panel holds it only in page memory. PostgreSQL mode checks membership/expiry/revocation on every request and enforces roles again inside the transaction. The demo serves only known static assets.

| Method | Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/health` | Explicit simulation/persistence status |
| GET | `/api/dashboard` | Demo tenant's pickup metrics and order list, excluding customer IDs |
| POST | `/api/demo/messages` | `{ customerId, messageId?, text }` → `{ reply }` |
| POST | `/api/demo/orders/:id/pay` | Simulate payment and kitchen submission; never a production payment webhook |
| POST | `/api/demo/orders/:id/status` | `{ status: "ready" \| "collected" }` |
| GET | `/webhooks/whatsapp` | Meta verification challenge |
| POST | `/webhooks/whatsapp` | Signed, mapped test-account messages; available only with configured Cloud transport |

Do not point a real payment webhook at the demo payment endpoint. Durable storage does not turn the simulated financial workflow into a live payment system. Real adapters, asynchronous delivery/reconciliation and disabling demo mutations are explicit [pilot deployment requirements](https://github.com/arkajyotiMukherjee/easy-eatery/issues/19).

nodes.label: README.md: Pay at pickup without a POS
nodes.description:
## Pay at pickup without a POS

For memory-only testing set `PAY_AT_PICKUP=true`. For PostgreSQL, apply migrations and configure the specific branch through the developer CLI:

```sh
node --import tsx --env-file-if-exists=.env scripts/database.ts pickup-mode <tenant> <branch> true
```

Restart the updated server, open the panel with a token scoped to that branch, then confirm a cart. Staff uses **Accept and prepare → Mark ready → Record payment received at store → Confirm pickup**. Recording payment is an assertion by authorized staff that money was received; it does not charge a card. Orders remain unpaid through preparation/readiness. The simulated-pay endpoint rejects these orders. Confirmation/replay does not create another ticket or a fake POS reference; local mode needs no vendor catalog mappings. Existing confirmed orders keep their original payment/fulfillment method when branch settings change. Store-paid and due amounts are separate dashboard metrics; old simulation figures are demonstration data.

This is a supervised local demo. Real-phone recipient/webhook verification, durable async message delivery, ready notifications and online checkout remain separate work. Business verification is not being attempted with invented company information.

nodes.label: docs/webpay-sandbox.md: Rehearse the flow
nodes.description:
## Rehearse the flow

Confirm a synthetic cart in Spanish or English. The order remains unpaid and cannot use simulation-pay, cash recording or unpaid kitchen acceptance. An owner/operator uses **Issue sandbox checkout link** in the panel. The server persists one immutable attempt before calling the gateway; the browser receives an expiring opaque same-origin link, not provider authority. Treat the link as a private capability and share only with the assigned test customer. Reissuing a ready link invalidates the older link and reuses the same gateway transaction.

The handoff page labels the transaction as a test and submits `token_ws` by POST to the exact integration destination. Only that response permits the integration origin in its form CSP. A browser return or cancellation cannot supply the amount, order, merchant or authorization result. The server claims a commit once and checks the authoritative response against the saved merchant, CLP total, buy order and session. Verified test authorization moves one local ticket to preparation, without a POS reference or real-money revenue. Staff then marks ready and confirms test pickup.

Use **Reconcile sandbox status** after a timeout or interruption. Reconciliation performs a status lookup, never another commit, checkout creation or refund. An abandoned creation with no known provider token is shown as needing review; it cannot silently create another transaction. Link expiry does not erase a late authoritative payment result. A declined, cancelled, reversed or uncertain observation cannot turn into a cash payment automatically.

nodes.label: README.md: Run the demo
nodes.description:
## Run the demo

Requires Node.js 24+ and npm.

```sh
npm ci
cp .env.example .env
npm start
```

Open [the local demo](http://127.0.0.1:3000). Enter `ADMIN_TOKEN` from your local `.env` into the panel. Replace the example token with a long random value before sharing a test environment. If `.env` is absent, the server generates and prints a temporary panel key for loopback use.

Choose **English** in the header to test the UI and chat in English. Spanish is the default; your explicit language preference is remembered in this browser. English commands: `hello`, `menu`, `cart`, `remove 1`, `clear`, `confirm`, `new`. Changing languages preserves your cart. In a real WhatsApp test conversation, send `English` or `Español` to choose the language.

1. Send `hola` in the chat simulator. Any initial text displays the menu.
2. Send `1 x 2`, then `3`: two completos and one limonada total **CLP 11,500**.
3. Send `confirmar`. Review the total and the explicitly simulated payment reference.
4. In the pickup dashboard, click **Simular pago y enviar a cocina**.
5. Mark the order ready, then confirm pickup. The dashboard updates counts and paid revenue.
6. Send `nuevo` to start another order after payment. Cart commands include `carrito`, `quitar 1`, and `vaciar` before confirmation.

The simulation payment reference points to the panel; it is not a hosted checkout and cannot charge a card. The panel button is the only simulation payment control. Refresh the operations panel to see orders received through the real WhatsApp test transport.

Set `POS_PROVIDER=toteat` (default) or `fudo` in `.env` to choose the simulated provider label. Both real adapters require provider access and implementation in #13/#22/#23. If port 3000 is occupied, set `PORT=3311` and open that port instead.

nodes.label: docs/cloud-agent-handoff.md: Verified implementation baseline
nodes.description:
## Verified implementation baseline

Repository: `https://github.com/arkajyotiMukherjee/easy-eatery`.

Merged changes, verified at handoff:

| PR | Delivered behavior |
| --- | --- |
| #24 | Modular TypeScript foundation, bilingual browser/chat simulation, Cloud API text transport and signed ingress scaffold |
| #25 | PostgreSQL durability, migrations, individual hashed/expiring/scoped staff tokens, role enforcement, audit/outbox |
| #26 | Versioned bilingual catalog/manual import, product/modifier mappings, availability/hours, immutable/expiring quotes and staff catalog controls |
| #28 | Local kitchen/pay-at-pickup, financial state separate from preparation, authenticated audited staff actions, truthful dashboard totals |
| #29 | PostgreSQL durable WhatsApp jobs, asynchronous ACK/worker, per-conversation sequencing, bounded retries and ambiguous-send parking |

Baseline implementation merge: `85cc1c3d1d45c559bc38c4e0e6b678b63c383f00` (merge of #29). Use a newer main if available. The old local branch `codex/durable-whatsapp` contains its implementation commit `e1784c6`; it is not a requirement for cloud work.

Stack: Node 24+, TypeScript ESM, Fastify 5, browser-native HTML/CSS/JS, pg/PostgreSQL 17, Docker/Compose, GitHub Actions. No React/Next.js build or microservice platform is required. Current payment and POS adapters are simulations; real WhatsApp outbound transport exists. There is no production deployment.

Relevant code map (query these names first):

| Area | Files / graph seeds |
| --- | --- |
| Runtime, auth, ingress and routes | `apps/server/src/app.ts` (`createApp`), `index.ts` |
| Tenant/cart/order/quote | `platform/domain.ts` (`MemoryStore`), `catalog.ts` (`CatalogService`), `ordering.ts` (`OrderingService`) |
| Conversation | `modules/whatsapp/conversation.ts` (`Conversation`) |
| External transport/contracts | `integrations/whatsapp.ts` (`CloudWhatsAppTransport`, `WhatsAppDeliveryError`, `parseMessages`), `contracts.ts` |
| Durable units of work | `persistence/database.ts` (`PostgresRepository`) |
| Message worker | `persistence/whatsapp-queue.ts` (`WhatsAppQueue`) |
| Browser | `apps/server/public/app.js`, `catalog-ui.js`, `i18n.js` |
| Schema | `migrations/001` through `004`; never edit an applied migration |
| Operator tools | `scripts/database.ts`, `scripts/import-catalog.ts` |

Persistence loads a small branch's working set inside a branch-row lock, rechecks authorization, and atomically saves changes/audit/outbox. This deliberately coarse POC design is not unlimited-scale storage or database RLS. Tokens expire after seven days; owners/operators mutate their branch, viewers read only. Real customer staging still needs operational hardening and least-privilege DB identities.

Queue behavior: PostgreSQL Cloud ingress commits a unique job before ACK. Processing commits domain effects/cached reply/reply-pending state together. Network sends follow a committed claim. Explicit provider rejections retry with backoff, up to five attempts. Unknown outcomes and expired send claims become `needs_attention`; do not blindly replay them. Later messages from that conversation wait, unrelated conversations can proceed. Provider acceptance is not device delivery. Memory mode remains synchronous and test-only. `/api/whatsapp/delivery` exposes authenticated branch-scoped queue counts without message/contact contents.

Last passing baseline: `npm run check`; 16 application tests; 12 PostgreSQL subtests plus parent (13 TAP results); CI green for merged #29. Local browser rehearsal completed a synthetic CLP 4,500 pay-at-pickup order, checked both languages and recovered the collected order after server restart. These are local/fixture results, not a real WhatsApp or vendor kitchen rehearsal.
