nodes.label: docs/product-and-milestones.md: Commercial modularity
nodes.description:
## Commercial modularity

| Shared capability, included infrastructure | Independently enabled service | Connector |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tenants, staff, catalog, product/modifier IDs | WhatsApp ordering (first POC) | Meta WhatsApp Cloud API |
| Order/checkout orchestration, prices, audit | Public QR menu (later) | Toteat and approved Fudo external ordering |
| Payment ledger, integration routing, operational reporting | Web pickup storefront (later) | Approved hosted payment provider |
| Events and minimal customer identity | Loyalty, CRM, inventory, catering and campaigns (later) | Further provider adapters |

WhatsApp accesses the catalog directly through shared services. Disabling QR menu must not remove products or stop ordering. Full CRM, loyalty, inventory and marketing are outside this POC. Both requested POS adapters are in scope; a billing engine, marketplace, AI agent and microservice fleet are deferred.

nodes.label: docs/product-and-milestones.md: Delivery gates
nodes.description:
## Delivery gates

| Milestone | Value and exit gate | Complexity | Issues |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [M0: pilot and access](https://github.com/arkajyotiMukherjee/easy-eatery/milestone/1) | Restaurant validates the flow; POS access and checkout feasibility proven; owner approves actual providers | Low implementation, high external dependency | #1–#4 |
| [M1: foundation and demo](https://github.com/arkajyotiMukherjee/easy-eatery/milestone/2) | Repeatable local demo plus durable catalog/orders, tenant authorization and immutable quote contracts | Medium | #5–#8 |
| [M2: real WhatsApp](https://github.com/arkajyotiMukherjee/easy-eatery/milestone/3) | Permitted recipient completes bilingual local-kitchen/pay-at-pickup flow; durable delivery survives retries/restart; verified Webpay sandbox adds full payment rehearsal | Medium | #9–#12, #14, #27 |
| [M3: payment and kitchen](https://github.com/arkajyotiMukherjee/easy-eatery/milestone/4) | Verified sandbox payment produces one kitchen-accepted order for each provider; failure recovery and adapter parity verified | Highest, built after access gates | #13–#17, #22–#23 |
| [M4: customer demo and pilot](https://github.com/arkajyotiMukherjee/easy-eatery/milestone/5) | Regional staging, authenticated operations, runbooks, restaurant acceptance and pilot go/no-go | Medium, final integration | #18–#21 |

Milestones are outcome groups, not a requirement to finish every task in one group before starting another. Start Meta account access early (#9) while catalog work proceeds. Staging (#19) can proceed after durable ingress. POS integration and production payment engineering depend on explicit feasibility results (#2, #3); local kitchen/pay-at-pickup and the independent Webpay sandbox do not. Provider approval waiting time is not engineering effort and can dominate the schedule.

nodes.label: docs/product-and-milestones.md: First outcome
nodes.description:
## First outcome

A customer sends a WhatsApp greeting, sees the restaurant menu, chooses items, confirms a final CLP price, receives an approved hosted checkout link, pays, and collects a restaurant-accepted order. The same order reaches the restaurant's POS/kitchen once. Staff can identify Easy Eatery pickup orders, readiness and exceptions in a dashboard.

Start with one branch per restaurant, Spanish by default (`es-CL`) plus English for testing/staff, CLP integer amounts and `America/Santiago` business dates. Support **both Toteat and Fudo in the initial pilot**, configured per restaurant/branch and verified through separate sandbox journeys. Treat the POS and gateway as the restaurant's systems of record for acceptance and payment. A paid order is not automatically a kitchen-accepted order.

nodes.label: docs/product-and-milestones.md: First pilot release essentials
nodes.description:
## First pilot release essentials

Menu correctness, availability/hours, deterministic pricing, cart edits, explicit confirmation, secure payment verification, kitchen acknowledgment, duplicate protection, staff exceptions, readiness/pickup status and reconciliation are required. Staff auth, durability and operational ownership are required even for a small live pilot. Prototype feedback precedes the broad platform build.

Proposed pilot targets to agree in #1: zero duplicate kitchen fulfillment; every paid order reconciles to a POS order or assigned exception; no unexplained price mismatch; complete at least ten agreed scripted sandbox journeys before live traffic. Measure message-to-order conversion, checkout completion, payment-to-acceptance latency, pickup completion, exceptions and restaurant staff time. Set latency and conversion thresholds with the restaurant after observing its baseline.

nodes.label: docs/product-and-milestones.md: Scope update: prospect demo before restaurant onboarding
nodes.description:
## Scope update: prospect demo before restaurant onboarding

The founder has no Meta API access or restaurant POS account yet. The first prospect demo will use real WhatsApp, local kitchen fulfillment and pay at pickup, then add independently verified Webpay sandbox checkout. A restaurant POS is not required for that demo. Both Toteat and Fudo remain integrations for the subsequent restaurant pilot described below. See [the account and execution plan](live-demo-onboarding.md) and [standalone-demo issue #27](https://github.com/arkajyotiMukherjee/easy-eatery/issues/27). Current payment/POS adapters are still simulated; this scope update does not claim implementation.

nodes.label: docs/product-and-milestones.md: Suggested two-person division
nodes.description:
## Suggested two-person division

The Chile-based partner owns restaurant interviews, Spanish flow feedback, merchant/POS access, menu verification and kitchen rehearsals. The engineering owner builds shared services, transport, adapters, reconciliation and staging. Pair on payment/KDS acceptance and the customer demo. The estimates in issues are planning ranges, not delivery promises; re-estimate after M0 and avoid assigning dates before access is proven.

Restaurant/POS integration critical path: **#1 → #2 → #3; #5 → #6 → #7 → #8 → #10 → #11; #13 + #22 + #14 → #15 → #16 → #23; #17 → #18 → #21**. #9, #19 and #20 have their own dependencies in GitHub. Both POS systems must pass #23 before pilot sign-off.

The runnable simulation covers menu → cart → confirmed total → simulated payment → simulated kitchen → ready → collected. The initial foundation PR did not connect real providers or a database. Issue #6 adds optional PostgreSQL persistence and scoped staff access; live Meta/POS/checkout/kitchen and cloud deployment still require their own acceptance gates.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/16-shared-domain-and-event-contracts.md: 1. Global identifiers and money/time rules
nodes.description:
## 1. Global identifiers and money/time rules

- All entities have UUID/ULID internal IDs, `tenant_id`, created/updated timestamps where applicable, and branch scope where operationally necessary.
- External provider IDs are stored separately with provider name and connection ID. Never use provider ID as platform primary key.
- Store instants as `timestamptz`; schedule local events in `America/Santiago` plus explicit timezone.
- Money: `amount_minor` integer and ISO currency code. CLP UI usually displays whole pesos; do not use floating-point arithmetic.
- Every write that may be retried receives an idempotency key where appropriate.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/16-shared-domain-and-event-contracts.md: 2. Canonical core entities
nodes.description:
## 2. Canonical core entities

- `Tenant`: commercial customer/business account and module subscriptions.
- `Branch`: physical location, address, hours, local policies, timezone and connected POS/payment configuration.
- `User`, `Membership`, `Role`, `Permission`.
- `ModuleCatalog`, `Subscription`, `Entitlement`.
- `Catalog`, `MenuCategory`, `MenuItem`, `ModifierGroup`, `ModifierOption`.
- `Customer`, `CustomerIdentity`, `Consent`.
- `Order`, `OrderItem`, `OrderStatusHistory`.
- `PaymentAttempt`, `Refund`, `PaymentEvent`.
- `LoyaltyAccount`, `LoyaltyTransaction`, `LoyaltyRedemption`, `WalletPass`.
- `IntegrationConnection`, `SyncRun`, `ProviderEventInbox`, `OutboxEvent`.
- `EventLead`, `Quote`, `QuoteItem`, `QuoteVersion`.
- `Conversation`, `Message`, `Campaign`, `CampaignRecipient`, `SuppressionEntry`.
- `AuditLog`.

This is a boundary outline, not a request to create every table in M0/M1. Only migrate what the first workflow requires.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/16-shared-domain-and-event-contracts.md: 3. Event envelope
nodes.description:
## 3. Event envelope

All domain events use an envelope similar to:

```json
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "type": "order.confirmed.v1",
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "occurredAt": "2026-10-15T12:00:00Z",
  "tenantId": "uuid",
  "branchId": "uuid",
  "aggregateType": "order",
  "aggregateId": "uuid",
  "correlationId": "uuid",
  "causationId": "uuid-or-null",
  "data": {}
}
```

No full PII, credentials or raw message body in the general event envelope. Consumers query authorized domain records as needed.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/16-shared-domain-and-event-contracts.md: 4. Initial event taxonomy
nodes.description:
## 4. Initial event taxonomy

- `catalog.published.v1`
- `order.created.v1`, `order.confirmed.v1`, `order.status_changed.v1`, `order.completed.v1`, `order.cancelled.v1`
- `payment.created.v1`, `payment.succeeded.v1`, `payment.failed.v1`, `payment.refunded.v1`, `payment.reconciliation_required.v1`
- `pos.sale.imported.v1`, `pos.order.status_changed.v1`, `pos.connection.degraded.v1`
- `customer.identity_linked.v1`, `customer.consent_changed.v1`, `customer.privacy_request_created.v1`
- `loyalty.points_earned.v1`, `loyalty.reward_redeemed.v1`, `loyalty.points_reversed.v1`, `wallet.pass_sync_failed.v1`
- `quote.created.v1`, `quote.sent.v1`, `quote.accepted.v1`, `quote.expired.v1`
- `whatsapp.message_received.v1`, `whatsapp.message_delivery_changed.v1`, `campaign.approved.v1`, `campaign.opt_out.v1`
- `module.entitlement_changed.v1`

Version schema changes deliberately; do not change meaning of an event while retaining same version.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/16-shared-domain-and-event-contracts.md: 5. Transactional outbox/inbox
nodes.description:
## 5. Transactional outbox/inbox

- Business transaction inserts/updates primary entity and one `outbox_events` row before commit.
- Worker leases event, publishes internally/executes consumer, marks completion and tracks attempts.
- At-least-once processing means consumer checks event ID/source reference uniqueness.
- Failed jobs move to dead-letter state after bounded retries and appear in dashboard/alerting.
- Replay requires operator permission and must remain idempotent.
- Provider webhook is first inserted to `webhook_inbox` with dedupe key; acknowledge quickly; worker processes after persistence.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/16-shared-domain-and-event-contracts.md: 6. API conventions
nodes.description:
## 6. API conventions

- `/api/v1` path version.
- Tenant/branch context always derived from authenticated membership or validated public slug/token.
- Public routes use rate limiting, opaque order tracking tokens and reduced fields.
- Standard errors: `VALIDATION_ERROR`, `NOT_FOUND`, `FORBIDDEN`, `CONFLICT`, `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`, `REQUIRES_ACTION`.
- Include `requestId` for support.
- Do not reveal whether arbitrary foreign tenant object IDs exist.
- OpenAPI documented, request/response schemas validated, generated docs reviewed.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/16-shared-domain-and-event-contracts.md: 7. Critical invariants
nodes.description:
## 7. Critical invariants

- Payment success comes from verified provider status, not frontend.
- Order item prices are server-calculated and snapshots stored on confirm.
- Loyalty changes are ledger entries; no balance-only mutation.
- Identity merge requires defensible match; every merge/unmerge is audited.
- Entitlement guard on server every time; UI gating is secondary.
- A module being disabled cannot stop unrelated consumers of a shared event.
- Deletion and cancellation are domain-specific states, not generic hard delete.

nodes.label: docs/integrations.md: Capability matrix
nodes.description:
## Capability matrix

| Capability | Toteat | Fudo | Current code |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Catalog access | Public API documents products | General API documents product data; access conditions apply | Bilingual seeded catalog |
| External order injection | Public order-creation contract | Separate approved external-order integration | Simulated adapter only |
| Kitchen acceptance/readiness | Verify statuses, shift and webhook behavior against pilot account | Verify external-order events and actual Delivery/kitchen behavior | Staff advances simulated states |
| API-generated hosted payment link | Not established by inspected public order API | Not established by inspected help documentation | No real checkout; panel simulation |
| Commercial/access gate | Owner enables API and supplies account-specific configuration | External-order approval and required Delivery module | No real credentials configured |

nodes.label: docs/integrations.md: Hosted checkout gate
nodes.description:
## Hosted checkout gate

[#3](https://github.com/arkajyotiMukherjee/easy-eatery/issues/3) must establish the supported payment flow for **each POS**: checkout creation, merchant settlement, expiry, authenticated callbacks/status lookup and refund support. The restaurant should receive settlement. If either POS has no suitable API, record an owner-approved separate gateway such as Webpay or Mercado Pago and map its verified settlement into the POS. This is a proposed alternative, not a connected integration.

Confirm payment before submitting the paid pickup; keep paid and kitchen-accepted states separate. Only verified server-side payment evidence authorizes the real POS submission. The current `/api/demo/orders/:id/pay` is an authenticated simulation control and must not exist as a real financial authorization path. Production adapters and a mode gate are backlog work.

nodes.label: docs/integrations.md: Provider parity gate
nodes.description:
## Provider parity gate

[#23](https://github.com/arkajyotiMukherjee/easy-eatery/issues/23) must run the same domain acceptance cases against **both** providers. Store the chosen provider on each immutable order; a later account setting change must not redirect it. Keep per-tenant credentials and provider references isolated. Demonstrate actual acceptance and readiness using two sandbox restaurant configurations. A mock passing twice is not evidence that either vendor accepted an order.

Do not contact vendors or send restaurant data until the owner authorizes that communication. This setup creates tasks and documents requirements; it does not request API approval, accept provider terms, create merchant accounts or move money.

nodes.label: docs/integrations.md: WhatsApp test-account setup
nodes.description:
## WhatsApp test-account setup

Use **Meta WhatsApp Business Platform Cloud API**, rather than relying on the mobile WhatsApp Business app. The [official Meta collection](https://www.postman.com/meta/whatsapp-business-platform/overview) and its [webhook guide](https://www.postman.com/meta/whatsapp-business-platform/folder/lboq68h/webhooks) are reference entry points. Some Meta documentation requires login; confirm current app-specific setup, supported Graph version, recipient restrictions and messaging rules in the developer console.

1. The account owner creates/configures the business app and test sender. Add and verify the permitted test recipients shown by Meta. Do not put personal contact details in GitHub issues.
2. Obtain the app secret, sender phone-number ID, access token and an explicitly supported Graph API version. Create a separate random webhook verification token.
3. Set `WHATSAPP_TRANSPORT=cloud` and the `WHATSAPP_*` variables in an ignored local `.env`. The process fails closed on missing Cloud credentials. Keep `POS_PROVIDER=toteat` or `fudo`; **both remain simulated** in this scaffold.
4. Expose the test server through an approved HTTPS development endpoint. Configure `/webhooks/whatsapp` as callback, complete the challenge, and subscribe the app/account to messages as required by Meta.
5. The current single-tenant demo maps only `WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID`; other receiving IDs are ignored. The route verifies `X-Hub-Signature-256` over raw body bytes and processes batched messages. Status-only notifications do not start conversations.
6. Send `hola` from a permitted recipient, then select items and `confirmar`. Send `English` to switch the conversation language, then use `menu`, `cart`, `confirm`, `remove 1`, `clear` and `new`. Send `Español` to switch back. The session retains its cart.
7. The outbound reply includes an explicitly simulated payment reference, not a payable URL. Open the authenticated panel and simulate payment there. A supported real hosted URL is M3 work.

Only immediate replies to permitted test-recipient input are scaffolded. Production readiness notifications need messaging-window checks, approved templates when required, delivery statuses, retries and human handoff (#10/#12). The in-memory webhook process is not restart-safe and does not provide durable outbox guarantees. Avoid connecting real customer traffic until M2/M3 gates are complete.

nodes.label: docs/integrations.md: Fudo
nodes.description:
### Fudo

[Fudo's external-order guide](https://soporte.fu.do/es/articles/15707531-integracion-de-pedidos-externos-via-apis) makes this integration subject to approval, indicates approval can take up to one month, and requires its Delivery module for externally created pickup/delivery orders. This route does not insert orders into Mesas y Mostrador. The restaurant must validate that workflow.

The [general API guide](https://soporte.fu.do/es/articles/11939789-api-publica-de-proposito-general) describes Pro-plan access for business data. That is separate from external-order approval. Do not substitute generic sale/order APIs for an approved external-order contract. Obtain the authorized technical documentation, credentials and redacted fixtures before writing the adapter. Payment-link availability remains a feasibility question. Track the adapter in [#22](https://github.com/arkajyotiMukherjee/easy-eatery/issues/22).

nodes.label: docs/integrations.md: Toteat
nodes.description:
### Toteat

The [official API index](https://developers.toteat.com/toteatApi_v2.yaml) lists products, order creation, order status, shift status and event hooks. Its descriptive guidance recommends `https://api.toteat.com/mw/or/1.0/` for production and `https://apidev.toteat.com/mw/or/1.0/` for development; its `servers` entry still contains an older URL. Confirm the usable base with the actual account rather than generating a client from that entry without review.

The [configuration guide](https://developers.toteat.com/tags/config_tag.yaml) describes owner-enabled API access with token, restaurant, local and user identifiers. The [order contract](https://developers.toteat.com/paths/create_order.yaml) documents `POST /orders`, query credentials (`xir`, `xil`, `xiu`, `xapitoken`), payment data and a precondition to check an open shift. Avoid logging credential-bearing URLs. Keep product/modifier and payment-method mappings specific to the account.

**Inference:** recording payment data on an injected order does not prove that a checkout link can be generated or that money has moved. The public paths inspected did not establish that capability. Verify it with Toteat before committing to POS-hosted checkout. Confirm pickup semantics, duplicate handling, uncertain-outcome lookup and actual KDS/printer behavior using the restaurant account. Track implementation in [#13](https://github.com/arkajyotiMukherjee/easy-eatery/issues/13).

## Concrete issue updates

Post the relevant grouped implementation evidence in `docs/issue-evidence.md` to issues #10/#12, #14/#15/#17/#27, #13/#22/#23 and #18/#19/#20/#21. Link the actual merged PR and implementation commits. Distinguish local/mock tests from hosted, real-device, vendor or restaurant evidence.

These exact unchecked criteria had complete local implementation evidence at review; recheck the current code and live text before changing a checkbox:

- #8: “Persist idempotency keys and inbox/outbox events in the same transaction as order changes.” PostgreSQL rollback/replay/concurrent-confirmation tests verify this implementation. Other state/real-POS criteria remain outstanding.
- #11: “Default conversations to Spanish; support explicit English/Español commands and localized menu/cart/checkout messages without altering the order or total.” The language/cart/order tests and ES/EN rehearsals cover this. Interactive pagination, session expiry and actual WhatsApp checkout delivery are separate incomplete requirements.
- #12: customer-service-window enforcement with staff fallback, and failed/late/no-sensitive-data notification tests. Cite `whatsapp-support.integration.ts` and the missing/future/stale timestamp checks. Staff-recorded pickup payment is an audited assertion, not gateway settlement. Assess the complete human-help and notification criteria before closing the issue; do not claim real-phone delivery from fake-transport results.
- #14: server-priced immutable attempts and persisted integration/order/session references with authoritative commit/status. Expiry, abandonment, replay and gateway errors have local coverage. The required opaque checkout link is currently staff-assisted rather than automatically sent in WhatsApp; real hosted success remains unproved. Keep that delivery/acceptance requirement open.

Existing checked criteria in #7, #10 and #27 were retained. Do not uncheck verified historical behavior or check a whole bundled criterion when only one part is implemented. nodes.label: docs/github-reconciliation.md: Required PR workflow
nodes.description:
## Required PR workflow

1. Read `AGENTS.md`, query the committed graph, read the scoped guides/handoff, and preserve local changes. Use the existing local checkout; do not reset it or create a worktree merely for administration.
2. Use `gh` to find the PR from `codex/pilot-readiness` to `main`. If absent, create it with the implementation and validation summary from `docs/issue-evidence.md`. Reference partial issues without auto-closing them. Do not merge unrelated PRs merely because they are open.
3. Review the complete diff, current head/base SHAs, mergeability, review requests/discussions and required checks. Wait for the repository's POC checks, including PostgreSQL and context freshness. Do not infer CI success from the local evidence or bypass protection with admin/force options. Diagnose and fix a failing check before merging.
4. Merge only the reviewed head, using a head-match guard. Attach the created or existing PR to the local Codex task. Verify the resulting merged state and merge SHA, rather than treating an accepted merge request as proof of completion.
5. Apply the issue evidence below without overwriting unrelated body edits. Re-read each live body before checking exact criteria. Use an identifiable evidence section or comment so retries do not duplicate updates. Keep external acceptance requirements unchecked.
6. Re-evaluate completed issues and milestones from their full criteria. Update local backlog/handoff/decision evidence to the verified GitHub results, refresh context, check it, and commit/publish the follow-up through the repository workflow. Never record a pending operation as completed.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/README(1).md: Non-negotiable product principles
nodes.description:
## Non-negotiable product principles

- Every commercial module can be enabled or disabled independently, subject only to declared shared-capability dependencies.
- Shared capabilities such as menu catalog, customer identity and order management are not automatically separate line items on the restaurant's bill.
- QR menu is optional. Pickup ordering, WhatsApp ordering, CRM and catering must not require QR menu to be enabled.
- One tenant may have multiple branches, different service entitlements per branch, and different POS connections per branch.
- PostgreSQL is the source of truth for orders, payment state, customer identity, loyalty ledger and entitlements.
- Third-party side effects run asynchronously when possible and are retried idempotently.
- Provider webhooks and browser redirects are not trusted as payment proof without verification.
- Do not build microservices, Kubernetes, Kafka, a graph database, or a second real-time database for the MVP.
- Never state that a POS connector is supported until access, capabilities, limits, and failure/recovery behavior are validated with a real account.
- Restaurant-facing UI defaults to Spanish (Chile), CLP, `America/Santiago`, metric quantities and Chilean phone formatting; timezone must use IANA rules rather than a fixed UTC offset.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/README(1).md: Research caveat
nodes.description:
## Research caveat

Public vendor pages do not establish an independently audited POS market share for Chile. Fudo markets 35,000+ businesses across Latin America; Toteat markets 5,000+ customers across the Americas. These are vendor-reported, region-wide figures and cannot prove which is most popular specifically in Chile. Toteat's published API docs clearly document external order intake, products/menu retrieval, sales/reporting, order status and webhooks. Fudo's general public API is available on Plan Pro, while its external-order integration is an approval-gated flow and Fudo's support page says approval may take up to one month. Therefore: **design adapters for both; prototype Toteat first if the target pilot restaurant can grant access; prioritize Fudo first instead if the first paying design partner uses Fudo and Fudo approves required permissions.**

nodes.label: docs/demo-and-pilot.md: Five-minute discovery demo (available now)
nodes.description:
## Five-minute discovery demo (available now)

Run the application using the README. Use synthetic customer data. Spanish is the default; choose **English** in the header to test the entire dashboard and chat in English. Only the display preference is stored in browser local storage; the panel token stays in page memory. A language change preserves the server cart/order and only affects subsequent chat replies; existing messages keep their original language.

| Step | Spanish | English | Visible evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open | Abrir demo | Open demo | Key from terminal or `.env`; authenticated dashboard |
| Greet | `hola` | `hello` | Localized menu with three seeded products |
| Choose | `1 x 2`, then `3` | Same item numbers | Two completos plus lemonade; total CLP 11,500 |
| Edit | `quitar 3`, then `3` | `remove 3`, then `3` | Correctly recalculated total |
| Confirm | `confirmar` | `confirm` | Frozen order snapshot; simulated payment reference |
| Pay | Simular pago y enviar a cocina | Simulate payment and send to kitchen | Paid and preparing; simulated provider reference |
| Ready | Marcar listo para retirar | Mark ready for pickup | Ready status |
| Collect | Confirmar retiro | Confirm pickup | Collected count increases; revenue remains CLP 11,500 |
| Repeat | `nuevo` | `new` | Empty cart for another order after payment |

Re-send confirmation before payment: the same order is recovered, with no second kitchen submission. Attempt to mark an unpaid order ready: the API rejects it. Show the QR-module-disabled note to explain shared catalog independence. Set `POS_PROVIDER=fudo` and restart to demonstrate the same local mock flow labeled Fudo; default is Toteat. **Neither mode calls a real POS**. Restarting clears records in memory mode; PostgreSQL mode preserves them and uses scoped staff tokens.

Ask the restaurant to validate its actual menu, modifiers, pickup promise, busy/closed handling and staff responsibility. Record objections and changes in #4 rather than building the full platform. A visually complete simulation is enough for initial feedback, while a pilot requires the real-provider gates below.

nodes.label: docs/demo-and-pilot.md: Pilot go/no-go
nodes.description:
## Pilot go/no-go

Required: both provider approvals/configurations, authoritative catalog, secure hosted checkout, durable state/replay protection, authenticated staff dashboard, payment/POS reconciliation, refunds, preparation/pickup ownership and a tested support fallback. No demo endpoint may authorize real payments. Do not label the pilot ready while Fudo approval or either kitchen integration is unverified.

The restaurant partner owns menu sign-off, kitchen/printer/KDS validation, service hours and customer support. The engineer owns deployment, incident diagnosis and integration correctness. Agree who contacts a customer when payment succeeds but kitchen acceptance fails and who can issue a refund. Review data collection, retention/deletion, restaurant access and local privacy requirements with appropriate local support; avoid marketing capture in this ordering POC.

Before service: verify open shift, correct menu, working sender/templates, POS connection, payment status and assigned staff. During service: watch unaccepted paid orders, dead letters and stale readiness. After service: reconcile payments/refunds, POS orders and collected records; investigate every unexplained mismatch. Rehearse provider outage and manual recovery before accepting live orders.

Record owner feedback and agreed baseline measures: completion rate, missed/duplicate orders, payment-to-acceptance time, pickup wait, reconciliation exceptions and staff effort. Expand to another branch or module after the observed pilot supports the next step.

nodes.label: docs/demo-and-pilot.md: Sandbox acceptance before live pilot
nodes.description:
## Sandbox acceptance before live pilot

Use authorized Meta test recipients, gateway sandbox transactions and separate Toteat/Fudo restaurant test accounts. Run the complete journey for **each provider**, in Spanish and English, and capture redacted provider references and restaurant confirmation that the expected kitchen station received it.

| Case | Required result |
| --- | --- |
| Happy path | Authoritative final amount; verified sandbox payment; exactly one kitchen-accepted pickup; collected metrics reconcile |
| Initial greeting / unsupported input | Menu/help instead of an invented order |
| Cart or language change | Existing order/cart preserved, correct localized names and integer CLP total |
| Sold-out or price change | Reject/reconfirm before payment; never silently substitute items or charge a changed amount |
| Closed kitchen / shift | Block checkout or route a paid exception to staff; no unsupported preparation promise |
| Duplicate messages / confirm / payment / POS callbacks | No duplicate fulfillment or revenue |
| Browser return / forged payment / wrong amount or merchant | No paid authorization and no kitchen submission |
| POS submit timeout | Reconcile by provider reference; unknown outcome goes to staff if safe retry cannot be proven |
| Paid but rejected / late payment | Assigned exception, customer communication and auditable refund/recovery |
| Missing callback / process restart | Durable inbox/outbox recovers; dashboard shows stale state and exception |
| Ready notification | Messaging-window/template rules enforced; failure visible to staff |
| Tenant/provider isolation | No other account's orders, contacts, credentials or callbacks accessible |

## Validation record for this foundation

Automated coverage checks the simulation loop, amount/state boundaries, duplicate inbound handling, separate customer carts, schema/auth, signature validation and delivery retry. The separate PostgreSQL suite verifies restart recovery, rollback and tenant/branch access. Cloud credentials, real checkout, both real POS systems and cloud infrastructure are not verified by these tests. Use the GitHub acceptance checklists to record external evidence later.

nodes.label: docs/issue-evidence.md: Issues #10 and #12: delivery, staff handoff and notifications
nodes.description:
## Issues #10 and #12: delivery, staff handoff and notifications

Migration 005 adds scoped versioned staff recovery, including explicit uncertain-send review without resend. Migration 007 stores signed receipt evidence separately from queue outcomes, including out-of-order, duplicate and pre-receipt callbacks. Migration 008 adds verified provider timestamps, human handoff and transactional bilingual local-pickup notifications. Both replies and notifications fail closed outside the verified service window; replay cannot reopen it. Missing-window jobs require staff review, and no unapproved template or marketing fallback is used. Device receipts never authorize payment or queue replay. The redacted staff panel respects viewer/operator/owner roles and records review without claiming customer contact.

Evidence: PostgreSQL/fake-transport tests cover tenant isolation, authorization, races, restart, replay, closed/future windows, bounded rejections, ambiguous sends, state supersession and no false success. Chromium checks cover both languages, desktop/mobile, keyboard acknowledgement, private-field exclusion, credential reset and staff controls. Actual Meta sender/recipient/subscription, real-device acceptance, template approval and retention/deletion policy remain open.

nodes.description:
## Issues #14, #15, #17 and #27: sandbox checkout and local fulfillment

Opt-in staff-assisted Webpay integration flow uses durable server-priced merchant/order/session snapshots, one claimed checkout, opaque expiring POST handoff, authoritative commit/status and one local kitchen ticket. Browser return/cancellation is not authorization. Test-authorized totals are separate from real-money revenue. Unknown create/commit/refund outcomes never retry automatically or switch to cash. Owner-only full test reversal requires current authorization and revision; partial/uncertain reversal evidence blocks fulfillment for review.

Evidence: official SDK contract source 52ad60075ce7d9eacf7f8cc42a795ae43bd483ff; mock HTTP transport and PostgreSQL concurrency/restart/mismatch/expiry/reversal tests; Chromium ES/EN owner/operator/viewer checks, POST handoff and fake-gateway full reversal. Actual hosted sandbox success remains unproved because this runtime denies the integration host and approved HTTPS/runtime configuration is absent. Production settlement, production refunds and post-collection refunds are not implemented or accepted.

## Issues #18, #19, #20 and #21: local operations evidence

The integrated slice passes 28 application tests and 43 PostgreSQL TAP results. All three ES/EN real-HTTP rehearsal modes pass. The final nonroot Docker image completed the CLP 11,500 synthetic ordering/payment/collection lifecycle, with no build CA/proxy credentials persisted. An isolated custom-format PostgreSQL backup/restore preserved migration checksums, order/payment state, audit records and owner/viewer restrictions. See `docs/operations-rehearsal.md` for the feedback template, staging/rollback/privacy gates and evidence limits.

No restaurant feedback, paid cloud deployment, production restore, approved data-retention policy, real provider order or go/no-go acceptance is claimed. Hosting account/budget, support ownership, production simulation controls and restaurant sign-off remain prerequisites for a live pilot.

Snapshot: 30 October 2026. These notes interpret the source archive alongside explicit current founder direction and the existing repository. They do not change the original documents.

- Runtime: preserve Node 24+, TypeScript ESM, Fastify and browser-native UI. Earlier Next.js/NestJS proposals are architectural options, not a request to migrate frameworks. Root `AGENTS.md`, current source/tests and current explicit decisions govern implementation.
- Loyalty is now an explicitly requested local demo slice. Start with source [MVP-A](restaurant-platform-specs/06-module-loyalty-and-pos.md): authenticated staff workflow, member lookup/code, authoritative immutable ledger, reasoned manual entries, redemption and transaction history.
- Source MVP-B adds Google Wallet; MVP-C adds supported automated POS earning/redemption. The requested local demo simulates unfinished Wallet and POS behavior. Simulation must be visible; local success does not prove issuer approval, vendor acceptance, real pass delivery or restaurant readiness.
- The ledger remains authoritative during Wallet update lag/outage. Duplicate sale events must earn once, refunds append compensating entries, and redemption must not overspend. These remain implementation acceptance targets until passing tests and rehearsal are recorded.
- QR-menu subscription and CRM marketing are optional. Keep loyalty acceptance separate from marketing consent. Use only synthetic data in the local demo.
- This archive import contains no loyalty code. The separate implementation handoff must arrive and pass its checks before starting the local loyalty demo. No external publishing or live vendor/customer action is authorized by this import.

Continue with [the current execution handoff](../../cloud-agent-handoff.md), [architecture](../../architecture.md), and the root [repository guide](../../../AGENTS.md). Current implementation evidence must be recorded separately from these historical source specifications.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/11-chile-payments.md: 1. Product decision
nodes.description:
## 1. Product decision

Keep a provider-neutral payment abstraction. A first customer can start with pay-at-pickup if that is accepted by the restaurant; otherwise ship one online payment provider only. For Chile, shortlist:

1. **Transbank Webpay Plus** for a Chile-local hosted card-payment flow and direct integration.
2. **Mercado Pago Checkout Pro Orders** for a hosted checkout/payment-link flow that can work across website and WhatsApp.

Do not build two complete providers before first customer demand. Select the first based on restaurant merchant account readiness, sales/channel needs, fees, payment methods and integration test access.

Official docs:
- Transbank Webpay Plus reference: <https://github.com/TransbankDevelopers/transbank-developers-docs/blob/master/referencia/webpay/README.md>
- Transbank merchant activation: <https://ayuda.transbank.cl/activar-webpay-plus>
- Mercado Pago Chile Checkout Pro Orders overview: <https://www.mercadopago.cl/developers/es/reference/online-payments/checkout-pro-orders/overview>
- Mercado Pago create order: <https://www.mercadopago.cl/developers/es/reference/online-payments/checkout-pro/create-order/post>

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/11-chile-payments.md: 2. Shared payment domain
nodes.description:
## 2. Shared payment domain

- `payment_providers` identifies provider adapter and platform/tenant account model.
- `payment_connections` stores tenant/branch mapping and Secret Manager refs.
- `payment_attempts` records internal order, amount/currency, idempotency key, provider reference, checkout URL, status and provider timestamps.
- `payment_events`/`payment_webhook_inbox` deduplicates and records provider events.
- `refunds` records original provider payment and amount/reason/status.
- `reconciliation_items` tracks mismatch or unknown status.

Keep platform SaaS subscription charges separate from restaurant customer-order payments. For the first customer, prefer restaurant-owned merchant accounts/direct provider authorization so restaurant funds settle directly with merchant unless a payments/legal review explicitly approves a different model. Do not pool/hold restaurant funds yourself without legal/commercial review.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/11-chile-payments.md: 3. Payment adapter interface
docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/11-chile-payments.md: 4. Transbank Webpay Plus flow
nodes.description:
## 4. Transbank Webpay Plus flow

The official reference documents merchant authentication headers `Tbk-Api-Key-Id` (commerce code) and `Tbk-Api-Key-Secret`, distinct integration/production credentials, and a transaction create operation that returns a unique transaction token. Official base hosts documented there include integration `https://webpay3gint.transbank.cl` and production `https://webpay3g.transbank.cl`; always prefer maintained official SDK and current docs over hand-built URLs.

Implementation outline:
1. Merchant obtains and activates Webpay Plus credentials; validate integration vs production credentials.
2. Backend validates order total and creates `payment_attempt` in pending state.
3. Call official SDK transaction create with unique `buy_order` (within provider length/character rules), internal session ID, amount in CLP and return URL.
4. Store provider token/reference and redirect customer to provider-hosted flow.
5. Return handler receives provider token/result; do not trust URL parameters as final proof. Use documented commit/status transaction operation to verify outcome.
6. Commit verified payment state transactionally and emit `payment.succeeded` or failure event.
7. Reconcile pending/unknown attempts and handle duplicate return/webhook calls idempotently.

Use SDK integration environment and test credentials in staging. The owner/customer must complete merchant onboarding and provider's integration validation before production. Never embed `Tbk-Api-Key-Secret` in the frontend.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/11-chile-payments.md: 5. Mercado Pago Checkout Pro Orders flow
nodes.description:
## 5. Mercado Pago Checkout Pro Orders flow

The current Mercado Pago Chile docs label Orders API as the recommended new Checkout Pro integration path; older Preferences API is a legacy-compatible path, with new features intended for Orders.

Implementation outline:
1. Merchant authorizes/creates appropriate Mercado Pago account/application credentials.
2. Backend builds an order payload using the authoritative CLP total and order reference.
3. Send `POST https://api.mercadopago.com/v1/orders` with `Authorization: Bearer ...` and documented `X-Idempotency-Key`.
4. Store returned order ID and `checkout_url`, then redirect or send the hosted link.
5. Configure documented payment/order notifications; verify events using the current provider authentication/signature mechanism and query provider state if needed.
6. Normalize status; only verified successful status marks paid.
7. Reconcile delayed/duplicate/out-of-order provider notifications and refunds.

For WhatsApp, send only a backend-generated hosted checkout URL associated with a specific order; never accept a user-provided “I paid” message as confirmation.
nodes.norm_label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/11-chile-payments.md: 5. mercado pago checkout pro orders flow

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/11-chile-payments.md: 6. Webhook contract
nodes.description:
## 6. Webhook contract

- Public HTTPS endpoint identifies provider and tenant connection through a nonsecret route identifier/lookup; verify provider signature/authentication per current docs.
- Persist inbox record idempotently before acknowledging.
- Enqueue state update and respond quickly (2xx per provider spec).
- Validate payment reference, expected order, amount and currency; if mismatch, mark `needs_review`, do not mark order paid.
- Store minimal/redacted payload and retain according to compliance policy.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/11-chile-payments.md: 7. Retry and reconciliation rules
nodes.description:
## 7. Retry and reconciliation rules

- Retry transient timeouts with the same idempotency key when provider supports it.
- On ambiguous timeout where provider outcome is unknown, query by reference before recreating.
- Payment state is monotonic except audited refund/reversal paths; late success after local cancellation enters explicit compensation/manual review.
- Scheduled reconciliation checks pending/unknown payment attempts and provider totals.
- Staff view shows “pending verification” instead of false paid/unpaid certainty.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/11-chile-payments.md: 8. Country-specific choices
nodes.description:
## 8. Country-specific choices

- Use CLP as integer pesos (provider schemas may constrain amount type; validate SDK behavior).
- Have local accounting/tax counsel determine VAT display and receipt/invoice obligations. Payment-provider approval is not equivalent to SII fiscal-document integration.
- No raw card data, CVV or full PAN in database/logs.
- Display all additional fees/charges transparently and ensure restaurant controls final price.

nodes.label: docs/sources/original-platform-specs/restaurant-platform-specs/11-chile-payments.md: 9. Acceptance criteria
nodes.description:
## 9. Acceptance criteria

- Browser return alone cannot mark paid.
- Duplicate provider event does not duplicate payment/order/reward.
- Amount mismatch is held for review.
- Provider secret rotation is testable without redeployment of source code.
- Pay-at-pickup works if online provider not enabled, with clear UI and policy.
- POS order handoff failure is visible and reconciled independently from payment state.

nodes.label: docs/postgres-storage.md: Authentication and roles
nodes.description:
## Authentication and roles

`npm run db:staff -- <tenant> <branch> <role> <display-name>` creates a named staff user, branch membership and a cryptographically random 256-bit opaque bearer credential. The token is printed once; only its SHA-256 digest, ID, expiry and scope are persisted. The CLI uses database-operator privileges and is not exposed as a public signup endpoint. Default validity is seven days. Keep CLI output out of Git, tickets and logs; the panel does not save the token in browser storage.

| Role | Dashboard | Simulated customer/order actions | Account administration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| owner | Own branch | Own branch | Bootstrap via trusted DB CLI only in this POC |
| operator | Own branch | Own branch | None |
| viewer | Own branch | Denied | None |

`npm run db:revoke -- <token-id>` immediately invalidates the credential on subsequent requests. Disabling a membership invalidates all its tokens. Token expiry and membership role are rechecked inside a transaction, so a cached identity cannot bypass a role downgrade/revocation before work starts. For rotation, issue a replacement staff credential and revoke the old ID through the trusted CLI. Full self-service staff lifecycle, OIDC and owner-management UI remain future work.

nodes.label: docs/postgres-storage.md: Data integrity and unit of work
nodes.description:
## Data integrity and unit of work

Migration `001_restaurant_storage.sql` creates tenants/branches, users/memberships/tokens, sender mappings, products, conversations, orders/immutable line snapshots, simulation payment attempts, inbox replies, outbox state events, delivery receipts and audit events. Tenant-and-branch composite keys/FKs prevent cross-scope order/session/product references. Tokens have a unique digest and provider references are unique within their account scope.

The repository authenticates staff into a server-derived scope. Webhooks authenticate exact raw bytes first and then resolve the configured receiving phone ID through `channel_accounts`. Customer text, body properties, query parameters and `X-Tenant-ID` cannot select a restaurant. Unknown JSON properties are rejected rather than silently stripped.

Each unit of work uses one checked-out PostgreSQL client for `BEGIN` through `COMMIT`/`ROLLBACK`, following [node-postgres transaction guidance](https://node-postgres.com/features/transactions). It locks the branch row before loading that branch's working set, as described by [PostgreSQL row-lock semantics](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/explicit-locking.html). This serializes concurrent app instances for the small POC without relying on an in-process mutex. Queries are parameterized, all domain reads/writes include tenant/branch scope, and save rejects changes to the transaction's scope or confirmed line/amount/provider snapshot.

The domain's Maps are transaction-local working sets in PostgreSQL mode. The database is the durable source; nothing from a previous request is required to reconstruct the next. Persisted inbox replies prevent repeated messages from adding items again after restart. Payment/POS references survive restart. State changes enqueue uniquely keyed outbox records in the same transaction, and mutations append an audit record with actor/action and scope. Audits do not contain message bodies, tokens or phone numbers.

This deliberately loads/saves one branch's small dataset per operation and uses a branch-level lock. It prioritizes correctness for the initial pilot; it is not suitable for unlimited order history/high throughput. Before increasing scale, replace bulk hydration with bounded per-aggregate queries and narrower locking while retaining the same isolation tests. Database RLS is not enabled; isolation currently relies on the authenticated repository boundary plus composite constraints. Use separate migration/admin and least-privilege application database users before staging customer data.
nodes.norm_label: docs/postgres-storage.md: data integrity and unit of work

nodes.label: docs/postgres-storage.md: Durable WhatsApp extension (#10)
nodes.description:
## Durable WhatsApp extension (#10)

Migration 004 adds a scoped durable message queue. PostgreSQL Cloud mode commits a verified inbound job before acknowledging the webhook. Domain changes, the cached reply and reply-pending state commit together; network sends run after a committed claim. The server polls automatically, with branch locks and persisted claims coordinating multiple processes. Explicit provider rejections have bounded retries/backoff; a timeout, malformed acceptance response, or expired send claim becomes `needs_attention` and is not automatically resent. Later messages from that conversation wait; unrelated conversations can continue. A provider acceptance reference is stored when returned. This is not proof of device delivery or exactly-once network sending.

Use authenticated `GET /api/whatsapp/delivery` for branch-scoped counts by queue state without customer identifiers. Failed/uncertain jobs need operator investigation; there is no blind retry control. Keep the affected conversation paused until the provider-side outcome is understood. Signed status evidence, redacted recovery UI and verified-window notifications now have local coverage; see `whatsapp-delivery-status.md`, `whatsapp-recovery.md` and `whatsapp-support.md`. Actual device acceptance and retention/deletion policy remain follow-up work in #10/#12/#20. Memory mode retains synchronous test-only delivery.

The timer stops before the application pool closes. After a crash, pending work/replies remain in PostgreSQL; expired send claims are parked for review because the external outcome cannot be inferred from a local receipt. Apply migrations before starting the updated runtime. Do not enable Cloud mode until real sender mapping, recipient permission, HTTPS callback and private runtime credentials are verified.

nodes.label: docs/postgres-storage.md: Migration and failure behavior
nodes.description:
## Migration and failure behavior

`npm run db:migrate` takes a transaction-scoped migration lock, records each migration's checksum and applies pending SQL atomically. Re-running it is safe; modifying an already applied migration fails. Add a new numbered migration for changes. Startup checks for the schema and never silently runs DDL or seed. Migration rollback and application transaction rollback release the checked-out client.

The original #6 baseline persisted inbox replies and successful outbound-delivery receipts. The #10 extension described above now adds durable async delivery in PostgreSQL Cloud mode. Network calls occur outside the state transaction. A crash between an outbound send and its receipt commit can still resend a reply; the new queue prevents blind automatic replay of ambiguous sends; provider delivery status and manual reconciliation remain acceptance work in **#10**. The outbox has no live payment/POS worker in this change. **#8** still owns the full separated financial/fulfillment state model and richer event contracts. Persisted catalog-version/expiry quote checks are implemented in the #7 extension. **#13/#22** still own real provider side effects. The local fake adapters must not be mistaken for exactly-once financial processing.

nodes.label: docs/postgres-storage.md: Modes and boundaries
nodes.description:
## Modes and boundaries

`PERSISTENCE=memory` retains the quick local prototype. `PERSISTENCE=postgres` requires `DATABASE_URL`, an applied migration, a seeded branch and an individual staff token. It never falls back to memory or the shared admin key when the database is unavailable. `/health` checks connectivity and reports the storage mode. Both modes still use simulated checkout/POS adapters.

The existing bilingual panel accepts the scoped credential in its panel-key field. It shows the connected restaurant/branch and actual storage mode; viewer accounts have no order-action controls. Changing credentials clears the displayed chat/dashboard, and late responses from an earlier credential cannot replace the current account's data. The simulator uses a new synthetic customer on each login; WhatsApp identities and their persisted conversations are independent of this browser behavior.

nodes.label: docs/whatsapp-delivery-status.md
nodes.description:
# Provider delivery-status evidence

After migration 007, PostgreSQL Cloud mode records signed WhatsApp `sent`, `delivered`, `read` and `failed` status events separately from queue processing state. The existing webhook HMAC check and receiving-phone mapping run before ingestion. Status-only callbacks do not start conversations, alter orders or trigger retries.

The normalizer accepts at most 100 statuses per webhook body (the HTTP body limit remains 128 KiB). It retains only bounded provider message IDs, recognized status, numeric provider timestamp and an optional numeric error code. Recipient IDs, error descriptions/URLs, message text and raw payloads are discarded. Unknown statuses and malformed fields are ignored. This is a bounded test-account ingestion path; confirm actual provider batching and retention policy before real traffic.

The unique scoped event key makes webhook replay idempotent. Events can arrive before the outbound acceptance receipt commits: they remain available for correlation when the matching job's provider message ID is saved. Matching includes tenant, branch and receiving phone, so a provider ID in another restaurant cannot supply this job's evidence. An unknown message ID does not resolve an uncertain send whose acceptance receipt was never saved.

nodes.label: docs/whatsapp-delivery-status.md: Read the evidence separately
nodes.description:
## Read the evidence separately

Authenticated `GET /api/whatsapp/delivery/receipts` returns up to 100 replies/notifications with a saved provider acceptance ID for the staff member's branch. It exposes source (`reply` or `notification`) and queue ID/state and evidence flags, excluding recipient/account/provider identifiers and payload text:

- `provider_accepted`: the transport returned a provider message ID; acceptance alone does not prove device delivery.
- `provider_sent`: a signed `sent` event was observed.
- `device_delivered` / `device_read`: signed device delivery/read evidence was observed; read also implies delivery.
- `provider_failed`: a signed failure event was observed, retained even alongside delivered/read evidence.
- `delivery_status`: `read`, then `delivered`, then `failed`, then `sent`, otherwise `unknown`, using all retained events rather than arrival order.

A late `sent` or `failed` callback cannot erase prior read/delivered evidence. A contradictory failure is preserved in its own flag for review. `latest_provider_timestamp` describes the latest retained event time, not a promise that the events arrived in order or that a human read the message. No event automatically retries a send, changes a queue job to `sent`, releases a parked conversation, authorizes payment or advances kitchen fulfillment. Use the explicit [recovery workflow](whatsapp-recovery.md) for staff review.

nodes.label: server/AGENTS.md
nodes.description:
# Server application

This directory owns the single runnable application. `src/index.ts` composes environment configuration, persistence and transport; `src/app.ts` exposes the testable Fastify factory. `public/` holds native browser modules served through an explicit asset allowlist.

Use `src/AGENTS.md` for HTTP/backend changes and `public/AGENTS.md` for browser changes. Cross-boundary changes must align route schemas, response fields, bilingual UI copy and tests. Static filenames must also be allowed in `src/app.ts`. There is no frontend bundler or build output step: `npm start` runs TypeScript through tsx. Root Dockerfile/Compose and `.env.example` describe deployment and local database configuration.

Validate with `npm run check` and the relevant tests from the repository root.

nodes.label: docs/whatsapp-support.md
nodes.description:
# Staff handoff and permitted pickup notifications

PostgreSQL Cloud mode applies migration 008 alongside the delivery/status migrations. The queue records verified provider timestamps without allowing replay or receipt time to refresh them. Both reply sends and proactive notifications reserve the transport timeout within the 24-hour customer-service window. Missing, future or expired timestamps fail closed. Console simulation does not send real messages; synchronous memory Cloud callbacks also refuse freeform sends without a valid provider window.

Help, allergy questions, payment problems and unsupported requests create idempotent branch-scoped staff handoffs. Their bilingual reply preserves the cart and makes no allergen-safety or response-time promise. Unsupported media routes to help without interpreting attachments. The staff panel shows only redacted request IDs/reasons. Owners/operators may explicitly record review without contact; viewers can read. Review is audited and never claims that a customer was contacted or that the issue was resolved.

For orders bound to a verified WhatsApp conversation, persisted domain transitions stage one notification per order/kind: restaurant accepted, ready, or staff recorded payment at pickup. Local pay-at-pickup acceptance and readiness remain unpaid. Sandbox acceptance is explicitly labeled as a test. Notifications contain no card data, checkout capability, amount, marketing copy or settlement claim. Old acceptance/readiness is suppressed if the order has advanced; uncertain/reversed sandbox payments suppress pending kitchen notifications.

The worker claims before sending, checks the current state and service window again, and runs network I/O outside transactions. Explicit provider rejections have bounded retries; ambiguous sends and expired claims park for review. Missing/expired windows route to `staff_required`. There is no unapproved utility-template fallback. Provider acceptance is separate from the signed receipt evidence described in `whatsapp-delivery-status.md`.

`GET /api/whatsapp/support` returns up to 100 scoped open handoffs and recent notification diagnostics. `POST /api/whatsapp/support/:id/review` requires `{"confirmation":"reviewed_without_contact"}` and current owner/operator authorization. A repeated or foreign review returns 409; successful review returns `customerContacted: false`. Use the restaurant's approved private support process for actual follow-up. Notification diagnostics have no resend control for uncertain outcomes.

The integration suite uses synthetic timestamps, fake transports and isolated PostgreSQL schemas to verify bilingual content, deduplication, restart/races, privacy, state supersession, window expiry/replay, bounded rejection retries and staff authorization. No real customer or provider acceptance is established. Approved sender/recipient access, real-device rehearsal, template approvals, retention periods, deletion/export policy and restaurant support ownership remain external gates. This feature does not choose a production retention period or purge audit/customer data.

Notification diagnostics have no resend control for uncertain outcomes.

The integration suite uses synthetic timestamps, fake transports and isolated PostgreSQL schemas to verify bilingual content, deduplication, restart/races, privacy, state supersession, window expiry/replay, bounded rejection retries and staff authorization. nodes.label: docs/whatsapp-recovery.md: Inspect and choose the safe action
nodes.description:
## Inspect and choose the safe action

`GET /api/whatsapp/delivery/jobs` returns the oldest 100 `failed` or `needs_attention` jobs for the authenticated branch. It includes job ID, state, recovery version, attempt count, bounded error code and timestamps. `customer_window_closed` means staff follow-up is required; it is not proof of provider rejection or an uncertain send. Sender addresses, phone/account identifiers, inbound text, reply text and provider IDs are excluded. Resolve older exceptions before requesting the list again when more than 100 need attention.

The list is a queue diagnostic, not proof of provider or device delivery. Investigate the operational cause using authorized provider tools and an appropriate private support process. Do not put customer conversations or credentials into issues, logs or this repository. This API deliberately cannot blindly resend an ambiguous job.

| Job state | Operation | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `failed` | `POST /api/whatsapp/delivery/jobs/:id/retry` with `{"expectedState":"failed","expectedVersion":0}` | After correcting a known processing failure or explicit provider rejection, permit a fresh bounded retry sequence. A committed reply is reused; otherwise processing resumes. |
| `needs_attention` | `POST /api/whatsapp/delivery/jobs/:id/resolve` with `{"expectedState":"needs_attention","expectedVersion":0,"confirmation":"reviewed_without_resend"}` | Staff explicitly completes review without resending the uncertain reply. The job becomes `resolved` and later messages in that conversation can proceed. |

Use the current `version` returned by the exception list as `expectedVersion`; the examples use version 0 only for an initial failure. Each recovery action increments the version. If another retry fails later, an old request cannot reopen it: staff must review the new failure and submit its new version.

A resolved job is not marked `sent`; the response contains `deliveryConfirmed: false` and `resent: false`. It creates no delivery receipt, payment change or kitchen transition. The original ambiguous attempt can still have reached the recipient. Review the conversation before releasing subsequent work; the operator may need to handle customer follow-up separately through an authorized channel.

Retrying an uncertain job or resolving a known failure returns HTTP 409. A stale/replayed request, a job from another branch or a nonexistent ID also returns 409 without revealing which case applies. Concurrent processes serialize recovery through the existing branch lock; only one recovery transition commits. Each successful action records the staff actor and job ID in `audit_events`; rollback also rolls back that audit record. Viewer mutation returns 403, invalid/expired/revoked credentials return 401, and malformed confirmation returns 400.

nodes.description:
## Local setup

Set the ignored `.env` values shown in the README, then run Docker Compose, migrations, seed and staff issuance. The Compose database binds to loopback port 55432 and uses a named volume. `docker compose down` stops it without removing the volume. Do not use `down -v` unless deliberately discarding the local database. Only run seed against a development/test environment: it inserts a sample menu.

Seed defaults: tenant `santiago-demo`, branch `main`, restaurant `Mesa Sur`, provider `toteat`. To create another configuration, set `SEED_TENANT_ID`, `SEED_BRANCH_ID`, `SEED_RESTAURANT_NAME` and `SEED_POS_PROVIDER` (`toteat` or `fudo`) before `npm run db:seed`. Set `SEED_WHATSAPP_PHONE_ID` when mapping an authorized test sender. A phone ID can map to exactly one branch; attempting to seed it into a different branch fails and rolls back.

Repeatable seed inserts missing rows only: it does not reset prices, change provider configuration, overwrite another phone mapping or issue replacement credentials. `db:staff` is explicit so re-seeding does not unexpectedly mint access tokens.

nodes.label: README.md: PostgreSQL and individual staff access
nodes.description:
## PostgreSQL and individual staff access

For durable local data, set `PERSISTENCE=postgres`, `LOCAL_POSTGRES_PASSWORD` to a random local password, and `DATABASE_URL` to `postgresql://easy_eatery:<URL-encoded-password>@127.0.0.1:55432/easy_eatery` in `.env`. Docker Compose uses the password from that file; the application uses the connection URL. Keep both private.

```sh
docker compose up -d --wait postgres
npm run db:migrate
npm run db:seed
npm run db:staff -- santiago-demo main owner "Restaurant Owner"
npm start
```

Use the **individual token** printed by `db:staff` in the existing panel key field. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored in the database. It expires after seven days. Owner/operator tokens can perform demo order actions; viewer tokens can only read the dashboard. PostgreSQL mode **ignores `ADMIN_TOKEN`**. The restaurant/branch comes from the credential, never a request header or customer message. Seeds preserve existing catalog/account settings.

```sh
npm run db:staff -- santiago-demo main operator "Kitchen Staff"
npm run db:staff -- santiago-demo main viewer "Read-only Staff"
npm run db:revoke -- <token-id>
```

See [PostgreSQL setup and access design](docs/postgres-storage.md) for another restaurant/branch, sender mapping, migrations, revocation, testing, and operational limits. In PostgreSQL mode the POS selection is stored per branch, so `POS_PROVIDER` does not override database settings.

Use Node's built-in test runner with tsx. `npm test` selects `*.test.ts`; PostgreSQL integration is separate (`npm run test:db`). `npm run check` validates TypeScript and browser module syntax.

- `poc.test.ts`: Fastify/demo API, authentication, WhatsApp flow/transport/signatures, language and replay behavior.
- `catalog.test.ts`: strict import validation, mappings/modifiers, availability/hours and quote invalidation.
- `pickup.test.ts`: local pay-at-pickup acceptance, store payment, status gates and payment-mode separation.
- `whatsapp-status.test.ts` / `whatsapp-status.integration.ts`: bounded status normalization and signed, scoped, replay-safe provider evidence; synthetic fixtures never establish real-device acceptance.

- `postgres.integration.ts`: migrations, tokens/roles, tenant/branch isolation, transaction rollback, durable replay, concurrency and process restart.

Graph seeds: test file paths, `createApp`, `OrderingService`, `PostgresRepository`. AST extraction may not represent every test callback; read the relevant file to verify coverage. Keep tests behavior-focused, deterministic and fake external transports/providers. Close app/pool resources. ## Evidence and completion contract

Maintain GitHub issues with checked implementation criteria and linked PR/test evidence. Keep an issue open when some acceptance gates remain blocked. Do not close #7 because its canonical importer exists, #10 because only fixtures pass, or #27/#21 because browser simulation succeeds. Update `backlog.json`, `backlog.md` and the handoff with matching status.

At each delivery boundary report: merged/open PRs and exact commits; tests and their limits; demo instructions; which integrations are simulation/mock/sandbox/real; blockers with owner and exact needed input; and the next independent task. Snapshot new product decisions in `docs/context-decisions.json` and this brief, update the relevant guides, refresh canonical graph/source hashes, and commit them with the change.

Stop at a truthful readiness boundary:

1. **Local prospect demo:** bilingual synthetic ordering, persisted local kitchen/pay-at-pickup, staff roles, coherent totals and recovery. Implemented baseline; preserve and improve it.
2. **Real-phone prospect demo:** verified recipient, real inbound/menu/cart/confirm, durable delivery, local kitchen/ready/collection, public HTTPS and redacted evidence. Still unproved.
3. **Hosted sandbox demo:** authoritative provider test approval/rejection/cancel handling and one local kitchen ticket. Still unproved.
4. **Restaurant pilot:** approved restaurant/menu/operations, correct selected POS kitchen routing, authorized sender and settlement, privacy/recovery/staging ownership and sign-off. Externally gated. Both-provider support requires distinct Toteat and Fudo acceptance evidence.

If a cloud run cannot satisfy the next external gate, finish all independent scoped work, leave safe runnable defaults, and provide a concise blocker matrix. Do not repeat blocked account setup or mislabel the whole pilot complete.

- **Both Toteat and Fudo** remain intended restaurant-pilot connectors. Each branch/order selects one destination; never send an order to both. The first prospect demo is not gated on either connector. A specific restaurant rehearsal uses its selected connector; claiming both-provider acceptance requires separate evidence for both.

This is an unresolved connectivity result, not proof that a merchant account is required or that a particular country is blocked. A normal approved cloud test environment may be checked; do not bypass a security challenge, rotate evasive proxies, disable TLS validation or substitute a fake success.

Build the adapter and approval/rejection/cancel/expiry/replay tests with a mock server now. A real sandbox success remains externally unverified until it actually happens. Use a server-priced immutable attempt, opaque expiring application checkout link, allowlisted provider URL, POST handoff, persisted token/order/session/environment, and authoritative server-side commit/status validation. A browser return URL or demo pay endpoint cannot authorize payment. Never collect card data in Easy Eatery. Sandbox authorization must be separate from actual money received.

nodes.label: docs/cloud-agent-handoff.md: Meta / WhatsApp
nodes.description:
### Meta / WhatsApp

The founder initially had only a WhatsApp Business mobile app. They subsequently created Facebook/developer access, the Arkaive Studio business portfolio, and an Easy Eatery app with the WhatsApp use case. The Meta console displayed a test sender and a temporary token. The official WhatsApp Business Tools MCP was configured and OAuth login succeeded on the founder's desktop; a business-list call verified access.

Last observed MCP result: the business was **not verified** and its **profile was incomplete**. These are separate statuses. The founder says legal company registration is pending and explicitly defers business verification. Do not invent legal/tax/address details, submit verification, buy a subscription, or migrate/deregister the existing mobile number.

Do not assume an unverified business necessarily prevents every test-sender operation. Recheck actual account eligibility, profile prerequisites and the specific console/API response. Use the test sender if legitimately supported. Respect a genuine prerequisite error; continue fake-transport development independently. Recipient verification, a real inbound/outbound ordering loop, public webhook subscription and ready notifications have **not** been proved.

Official MCP guide: `https://developers.facebook.com/documentation/mcp/whatsapp-business-tools-mcp`; endpoint `https://mcp.facebook.com/whatsapp_business_tools` (Streamable HTTP + OAuth). It manages/debugs developer assets; the product runtime calls Cloud API directly. Follow the connected MCP's business-picker rules: list businesses first, show results and obtain an explicit selection even if one exists; inspect profile prerequisites before onboarding. Never auto-select assets or automatically grant broad permissions.

A cloud worker does not inherit desktop browser cookies, temporary tokens, OAuth/keychain storage, Codex user configuration, localhost callbacks or MCP registrations. Discover its actual tools; ask the owner to reconnect only when needed. Store runtime secrets in the cloud environment's secret facility, never in Git/graphs/issues/chat. The founder prefers to personally accept terms and complete password/OTP/CAPTCHA/security-sensitive grants. Do not request passwords in chat. No Twilio account is needed for the existing direct-Meta adapter.

nodes.label: docs/cloud-agent-handoff.md: Restaurant, hosting and operations
nodes.description:
### Restaurant, hosting and operations

No pilot restaurant, approved menu/hours/pickup promise, merchant settlement account or actual staff sign-off exists. Do not invent them. Production receipts must settle to the authorized restaurant merchant. Production financial transactions, refunds, billing and legal commitments require the owner and actual provider approval.

Architecture targets hosting near Chile (existing plan: Santiago). Prepare deployment/IaC, rollback, secrets, database/worker lifecycle, health checks, redacted logs and cost estimates now. Cloud project access and an approved spending cap have not been provided. Do not provision paid infrastructure or expose staff/demo routes publicly by default. Localhost services/tokens on the founder's computer are not available in cloud jobs.

nodes.label: docs/cloud-agent-handoff.md: Toteat and Fudo
nodes.description:
### Toteat and Fudo

There are no approved restaurant accounts/test branches/credentials or restaurant-side kitchen acceptance evidence. A public developer login is not equivalent to approved external-order access. Do not spend engineering time fabricating authentication or order contracts.

Prior research (revalidate authoritative docs before coding): Toteat owner configuration exposes restaurant/local/user identifiers, API enablement and external-order settings. Fudo external-order integration requires its separate approved workflow and Delivery capability; general-purpose data API access does not establish order-injection permission. Generic payment fields do not establish hosted-checkout-link capability for either vendor.

Sources: `https://developers.toteat.com/tags/config_tag.yaml`, `https://developers.toteat.com/toteatApi_v2.yaml`, `https://soporte.fu.do/es/articles/15707531-integracion-de-pedidos-externos-via-apis`, `https://soporte.fu.do/es/articles/11939789-api-publica-de-proposito-general`.

Can complete now: common adapter boundaries, scoped configuration validation, mock-server harness, explicitly synthetic contract fixtures, duplicate/timeout/error tests, capability matrix and operator runbooks. Implement actual request formats only where current official/authorized contracts support them. Fail closed in real mode without approved configuration. Never call a synthetic fixture a vendor contract test or mark provider acceptance complete.

Blocked until owner/vendor access: approved authentication/permissions, actual catalog IDs/modifiers/payment mappings/shift behavior, test order injection, correlation lookup/idempotency proof, callbacks and correct restaurant KDS/Delivery pickup routing. Draft access questions for the Chile partner; do not send vendor emails or make commitments without explicit authorization.
